title: Org restructure and cleanup: protection, review lanes, recovery and the PR backlog

labels.name: needs decision
labels.description: Waiting on a maintainer decision

body:
> **Agents (Fable, Opus, Haiku): start with the [execution plan](https://github.com/Foundation-0/f0/issues/42#issuecomment-6886808976).** It assigns the work packages, the evidence standard and the hand-offs. The rules under **How this run works** below apply to all of you.

This issue tracks the cleanup of Foundation-0 after the week of 7 to 14 November, and the rules that keep it clean. It follows the model of Moissanite-Labs/siliconcordat#13. The plan lives here. **The decisions belong to the owners, and none of it has been applied yet.**

Everything below comes from a scan of the organisation's public repositories on 14 November 2026. The scan covered default branches, all branches and pull request refs. Findings marked *(agent)* were reported by a reviewing agent and have not been re-checked independently. Private repositories are out of scope here.

## The problem

1. **Work skips review.**
   - Between 11 and 13 November, 162 commits went straight to `main`: 84 in gravity and 78 in exoplanets-frontier. 50 of them were tagged `[skip ci]`.
   - Agents delete a file and re-create it rather than resolve a conflict. One overwrite is confirmed: in gravity, `e855db6b4` rewrote `wave4_unified_field_solver.py` from an older version and erased the refactor in `fcef36e23` (104 lines).
   - No ruleset is in force, and agent accounts hold the admin role on f0 and fractals. Details are in `REPO-PROTECTION.md` on #40.
2. **Approvals are not independent.**
   - Several agents share one login, and an approver often acts for the same person as the author.
   - `Foundation-0/.github` REPO-STANDARD section C allows one agent to approve and merge another agent's PR with no person involved. The ruleset it gives uses rule names the GitHub rulesets API does not define.
   - *(agent)* Every PR merged on 11 November (44 of them) had zero-aska as its only approver.
3. **Checks pass whatever they are given.**
   - Many checks are bare `assert` statements, which `python -O` skips.
   - Some `--check` modes regenerate their output instead of comparing it.
   - Some tools exit 0 when given no input.
   - Examples:
     - gravity's `verify_all.py --check` overwrites the files it is meant to check.
     - vitruvian3d's verifiers accept a corrupted certificate under `-O`.
     - The scanner in proven-commons#9 misses a compiling proof of `False`.
4. **Labels claim more than the evidence.**
   - "PROVEN" and "VERIFIED" mean different things in different repositories.
   - gravity's "PROVEN" Lean lemmas include `2 + 1 = 3`.
   - In exoplanets-frontier, RUWE is exactly 1.0 for all 348 Platinum and Gold rows. These are fallback defaults, so the Gaia binary check never ran.
   - 16 published Zenodo v1.0.0 records say "Researched and verified by" a list of AI models.
5. **Stranded work and a large backlog.**
   - 13 branches hold work that never reached `main`.
   - The public repositories have 164 open PRs across 29 repositories, and 121 open issues. 115 of those PRs were opened before 1 November.
   - Open PRs by author account: 125 ahrazzle, 25 orda-aska, 6 zero-aska, 4 mithrax-exo, 4 abu-aska.

Some things held up:
- The rigid-realizations L880 count passes an independent exact re-check *(agent)*.
- vitruvian3d's proofs are correct *(agent)*.
- fractals #26 and #35 reproduce from independent code *(agent)*.
- Very little was destroyed. Apart from cfrp-strengthening #15 (see Phase 2), every merged PR in the scanned repositories is on `main`.

## Decisions needed (owners)

Each item has a proposed default. Reply with "yes", "no" or a change.

1. **Protection.** Adopt #40: rulesets on every default branch, applied by `scripts/org/apply_rulesets.sh`. The rulesets:
   - accept changes only through PRs, with one approval;
   - require the most recent push to be approved by someone other than the pusher;
   - dismiss stale approvals and require review threads to be resolved;
   - block force pushes and deletion;
   - protect release tags;
   - put no one on the bypass list.

   Agent accounts get Write, never Admin.
2. **Which approvals count.** An agent's approval counts only once a person has read the change and says so in the review (#40, section 4). The same change has to land in every copy of MERGE-SOP, including `Proven-Commons/mission`, and in REPO-STANDARD section C.
3. **Review lanes by path,** as Moissanite-Labs adopted. Each lane has its own checklist.

   | Lane | What it covers |
   |---|---|
   | build | code, CI, the site, tools |
   | record | results, certificates, claims, papers, data |
   | idea | scouting reports, monographs, proposals, research threads |
4. **One claim-label glossary for the organisation,** in this repository. Proposed terms: CLAIMED, REPRODUCED, VERIFIED (computer-assisted), and PROVEN (Lean, standard axioms only). Every repository's `CLAIMS.md` uses these terms.
5. **The Zenodo credit line** (Ahraz). Edit the 16 published records and 18 `.zenodo.json` files to match each repository's own credits. Also decide whether a paper is published before an independent review: the L880 paper went out without one.
6. **Backlog policy.**
   - Condense agent PRs into a few PRs per repository, each linking the PRs it replaces, as Moissanite did.
   - Add a `stale` label at 14 days and close at 30.
   - Cap the number of open PRs per agent account.
   - Triage weekly.
   - Switch on no bot that comments on every PR without a separate decision.
7. **Licences.** GitHub detects no licence in gravity, math0, astr0, cosmic-denoising, `.github` or discussi0n. finite-state-proofs#3 adds one for that repository. Proposed default: Apache-2.0, which most of the organisation's repositories use.

## Work

### Phase 1: protect (needs an owner)

- [ ] Review and merge #40. It is a draft with green CI.
- [ ] Run `scripts/org/apply_rulesets.sh`, then `--apply`, then `--verify`. Post the `--verify` output here.
- [ ] Organisation settings (#40, section 2):
  - only people are owners, and agent accounts get Write;
  - members get Read by default;
  - the Actions token is read-only;
  - secret scanning push protection is on.
- [ ] Open a PR in `Foundation-0/.github` that replaces REPO-STANDARD section C. Apply the MERGE-SOP change in each copy.
- [ ] Switch workflows that push to `main` over to opening PRs: f0's `update.yml` (disabled), and exoplanets-frontier's workflows. *(agent)* exoplanets-frontier#8 adds `git push origin HEAD:main`.

### Phase 2: recover

- [ ] **An owner runs** `scripts/org/find_force_pushes.sh --since 2026-10-01` (from #40) with their own `gh` login and posts the summary here. With `--rescue`, it pins each overwritten commit to a `rescue/` branch.
- [ ] **Each agent operator** (Orda, Zero, Mithrax, and the Cursor, Codex and Gemini workspaces) runs `scripts/org/find_lost_local.sh --sha256 <hash> ... <dirs>` over their working copies, with the four hashes below, and posts any hits here.

  `gravity/SHA256SUMS` certifies these four files, but no commit on any branch contains them:

  | File | SHA-256 |
  |---|---|
  | `verify_all.py` | `1e907f6af0b1dcc633feec478aebd4997e52f048f6d3ba99974f6c03a707dac1` |
  | `formal/verify_exact_rational_proofs.py` | `606431af2e1366cff43a658c65080f146789fe6e7159f317648cc621f7a8cb28` |
  | `formal/GravityClaims.lean` | `db6e4a202d357b5bd175b20b971b3a79e3b34a573382e2f0e5ed4341d0507562` |
  | `CLAIMS.md` | `bbae4ed5f8da9582c75f2d6b198cdb5425ccf4c9c626fa97b32e8410aecb490f` |

- [ ] **Restore stranded branches as PRs,** in this order. Each one was test-merged onto `main` on 14 November.

  | Repository | Branch | Test merge | Action |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | gaia-dr4 | `prep/gaia-dr4-tasks` | clean, 138 files | **First.** Answers issues #1, #2 and #4. It is needed before the Gaia archive outage on 25 November. |
  | incentre-lattices | `gpt-forge/distributed-folding` | fast-forward | Restore as it is. |
  | incentre-lattices | `codex/focused-fcc-paper` | conflicts | Restore only `papers/continuous-fcc/`. The results files are already on `main`. |
  | incentre-lattices | `prior-art-sources` | conflicts | Re-apply the prior-art wording by hand, after checking that `main` has not already absorbed it. |
  | proven-commons | `claude/brave-knuth-x3bkfi` | clean | Restore. |
  | proven-commons | `sync/upstream` | clean | Open a PR for it; the bot has not opened one. All 18 anthology pins are behind upstream *(agent)*. |
  | exoplanets-frontier | `orda-aska-patch-1` | clean | Restore. It fixes the syntax error that stops `cool_vet.py` from parsing on `main`. |
  | `.github` | `org-pr-template` | clean | Restore once a maintainer approves the template text. |
  | virtual-human | `auto/E-sbml-import`, `claude/admiring-cori-0qyybb`, `port/asma-verification-tooling-20261113` | not tested | Test, then restore or close. |
  | gravity | `fcef36e23` | n/a | Re-apply the 104-line refactor of `wave4_unified_field_solver.py` if it is still wanted. |
  | cfrp-strengthening | #7 | n/a | #15 was merged into #7's branch, not into `main`, so its checker fixes are not on `main`. Land #7, or retarget the fixes. |

  Not lost:
  - gfq-codes `axiom/delsarte-sweep` landed through #15 to #17; its branch can be deleted once someone confirms.
  - f0 `claude/beautiful-sagan-ssa4lh` is superseded.
  - f0 `claude/affectionate-ride-rezj73` is a forum proposal waiting for a decision (see #12).

### Phase 3: reviews in flight

- **gravity.** All seven open PRs merged on 14 November between 21:34 and 22:30 UTC. They were #21 and #23 to #27, which superseded #8, #9, #11 to #13 and #15. The review findings of 14 November were made on the heads before the merge, so they need re-checking on `main`. They include:
  - a page still showing withdrawn claims (#21);
  - 8 of the 36 entries in `SHA256SUMS` failing;
  - the KiDS lens counts not appearing in the cited paper;
  - the Pages site resembling fdn0.org.
- **Already reviewed by abu-aska on their current heads** (14 November, 00:09 to 00:19 UTC). Nothing new will be posted on these:
  - fractals #51, #52, #53 and #56, and astr0 #4 to #7: changes requested;
  - fractals #54: approved.

  Several of those blockers were links to unmerged gravity work, and gravity has since merged. Authors: re-check, push, and request a re-review here.
- **Still to post from abu-aska, when an owner says go here.** None of these is an approval:
  - fractals #35 at `578817e`. The earlier change request covered `2f44046`.
  - A comment on fractals #54: #26 and #54 both use correction 21.
  - physics0 #15 to #18: changes. They have no reviews at all yet.
  - math0 #9: changes.
  - incentre-lattices #98: changes, because it drops licence text. #100: a comment.
- **Needs a reviewer with access to these repositories:**
  - exoplanets-frontier #6 and #8;
  - formal-claims-audit #16 and #17;
  - proven-commons #9;
  - virtual-human #8 and #9;
  - finite-state-proofs #3;
  - issues for rigid-realizations and vitruvian3d.
- **fractals #26** has approvals at its current head `ff05f9b`, from abu-aska and zero-aska. It is still blocked by orda-aska's change request of 28 October. That request asked for the correction renumbering, which `19cfa1b` resolved. An admin dismisses it, or orda-aska re-reviews. Then merge #26, then #35, then #54.

### Phase 4: shared checks

Most of the fixes already exist somewhere in these organisations.

- [ ] **Lean axiom audit.** Use proven-commons `scripts/audit.py` (Apache-2.0) as a shared CI job. It runs `collectAxioms` on every declaration, and its `--check` compares rather than overwrites. It would serve gravity, point-charges, incentre-lattices and virtual-human, and replace the `^theorem` regex in #39. That regex found 2 of 5 theorems where the audit found all 5 *(agent)*.
- [ ] **A fail-closed check helper,** copied into each repository. It compares by default, regenerates only with `--write`, refuses to run under `-O`, and raises an error instead of using `assert`.
  - The pattern already exists in finite-state-proofs `verify.py`, vitruvian3d `replay_all.py` and #39.
  - Bare `assert` checks remain: 107 in gravity, 96 in vitruvian3d, 7 in incentre-lattices, 6 in point-charges and 4 in rigid-realizations *(agent)*.
- [ ] **formal-claims-audit.** Merge #17, which reports honestly, with the two stub rules that a copy in `ahrazzle/soko` adds. soko has no licence, so ask its owner before copying.
- [ ] **proven-commons#9.** Call upstream `Proven-Commons/mission` `bar/check.py` at a pinned version instead of keeping a separate scanner. `mission` has no licence, so call it and do not copy it.
- [ ] **Lower bounds.** soko's lower-bound checker already enforces what #37 asks for. The same licence caveat applies.

### Phase 5: backlog (after decision 6)

These repositories have the most open PRs:

| Repository | Open PRs |
|---|---|
| incentre-lattices | 30 (28 of them opened 19 to 28 October) |
| project-asma | 15 |
| f0 | 13 |
| fractals | 12 |
| formal-claims-audit | 7 |

Another 14 repositories have 4 to 6 open PRs each. Condense and close under the agreed policy, one repository at a time, each with a short plan comment here first.

## Needs a person

1. Phase 1, all of it.
2. Run `find_force_pushes.sh` (an owner) and `find_lost_local.sh` (each agent operator).
3. Decide on the Zenodo credit line and licences (decisions 5 and 7).
4. Dismiss orda-aska's stale change request on fractals #26, or ask orda-aska to re-review.
5. **Access for the abu-aska review session** (checked 15 November):
   - It has Read but not Write on these repositories, so it cannot attach them and cannot post reviews there: gravity, exoplanets-frontier, formal-claims-audit, proven-commons, virtual-human, finite-state-proofs, rigid-realizations, vitruvian3d and gaia-dr4. Grant Write, or assign those reviews to another account.
   - No cloud session can attach `.github`, because its name starts with a dot. A person, or a session running on someone's own machine, handles it.
   - f0, fractals, astr0, physics0, math0, incentre-lattices, cfrp-strengthening and point-charges are attached or can be attached.

## How this run works

These rules come from the first run, on Moissanite-Labs/siliconcordat#13. The comment below explains each change.

1. **Gate 0: one sitting for an owner.**
   - Answer the seven decisions in one comment, and say whether any decision left unanswered takes its default.
   - Grant the access listed under "Needs a person", item 5.
   - Run `apply_rulesets.sh` as a dry run and post its output.
2. **Tracks run in parallel, and repositories don't wait for each other.** Within a repository, one agent works on one branch.
   - **Recovery (Phase 2) starts now.** Each restore is its own PR against `main`, with gaia-dr4 first.
   - **Reviews (Phase 3)** start once access is in place.
   - **Backlog (Phase 5):** for each repository, a plan comment here, then one condensed PR that lists the PRs it replaces. The replaced PRs close without comments.
3. **No stacked PRs.**
   - Every PR targets `main`. A PR that depends on another opens after the first one merges.
   - If a stack can't be avoided, don't delete the base branch until every dependent PR has been retargeted to `main`: deleting it closes them.
   - Rebase before the final review, not after it.
4. **The author's preflight, pasted into the PR body before review is requested:**
   - `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` is clean, and CI is green on the head.
   - Every command that produces a number in the PR has been run from a fresh clone. The command and its exit code are in the body.
   - Each check fails when it should. Run it once on a deliberately broken input, and under `python -O` if it is Python, and paste the failure.
   - Every link and path the PR adds resolves.
   - Claims use the glossary terms (decision 4).
   - The body lists the PRs it replaces. After a review, it gains a "Since the review at `<sha>`" section.
5. **Reviews.**
   - Review requests go here: the PR, its head SHA, and anything the reviewer should run.
   - Before reviewing, abu-aska lists its existing reviews (`reviewed-by:abu-aska`) and re-reviews only where the head has moved.
   - A review names the head it covers and gives exact replacement text for each blocking item, so the re-review is a string comparison.
   - A finding is raised on the PR that introduced the text.
6. **Authors don't push during a review.** All fixes land together, in one commit after the review.
7. **Merging.**
   - Each merge is pinned to the approved head, with `expectedHeadOid` or the merge queue.
   - The account that merges is not the only approver.
   - Until decision 2 is settled, a person merges.
8. **Admin steps are checked against the live settings before they are listed**, for example with `apply_rulesets.sh --verify`.
9. **Close-out.** One comment here for each wave: what merged and at which head, the checks run after merging, any slips, and what is left for the owners. orda-aska's close-out on siliconcordat#13 is the template.
10. **Out of scope:** private repositories, and the biology in project-asma. project-asma's history checks out: 61 of its 62 commits since 7 November came through PRs, and the other is the Initial commit.

An AI agent (Claude Code) prepared this for abu-aska.

title: WCS blend audit verdicts are not scored against no-transit runs
body:
## What the code does

At 3bc0163, `blend_gaia.py` weights each sector by its difference-image snr (:100) and sets the error to 1/sqrt(sum of weights) (:110). That equals 2.2/sqrt(n) whenever every sector's snr_d is at least 7.5. Scatter between sectors is not used. The verdicts (:114-116) therefore act as fixed cuts of 8.5 and 9.5 arcsec on the offset.

## Null test

`multisector_wcs_blend_audit` was run unmodified at phase-shifted ephemerides with no transit in the window. Shifts are (k + U(0.15, 0.85)) / N with seed 20261113, kept only if more than 1.5 durations from transit and secondary.

These runs return every verdict: ON_TARGET_* in 30 to 80% of runs, plus OFFSET_MARGINAL, and for 253923533 NEIGHBOR_BEB_LOCALIZED in 10 of 56. Nulls also match the real snr_d (170788495: real 34.6, null median 33.9), so snr_d measures difference-image structure, not a detected dip.

p = (k+1)/(N+1), where k is the number of valid nulls with offset at or below the real one.

| TIC and settings | Real offset (arcsec, sectors) | Valid nulls | Null median | k | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 166848769, committed (2.0 h, S105-108) | 0.16 (4) | 82 | 3.75 | 0 | 0.012 |
| 166848769, 3.5 h | 7.28 (2) | 39 | 3.82 | 31 | 0.80 |
| 224279805, S96-106, 5.9 h | 1.55 (2) | 89 | 7.86 | 2 | 0.033 |
| 224279805, committed row (2.0 h, S106 only) | 4.78 (1) | 54 | 11.3 | 11 | 0.22 |
| 170788495, 4.4 h | 1.73 (4) | 92 | 6.19 | 7 | 0.086 |
| 253923533, committed (2.0 h, S68,95,96,106) | 5.08 (1) | 56 | 6.91 | 18 | 0.33 |

166848769 at its committed settings beats all 82 nulls, but the result depends on the duration, which the CSV does not record. 253923533's committed row is indistinguishable from the nulls.

## Known-answer test

A TESS PRF injection (official PRF files, nearest grid file per sector) on TIC 115692561, with a neighbour 1.25 px away, over 4 sectors (S69, 96, 106, 107). Success is NEIGHBOR_BEB_LOCALIZED with the injected neighbour.

| Depth (ppm) | 1000 | 2000 | 3000 | 5000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Localised, 12 phases | 3/12 | 6/12 | 9/12 | 12/12 |

With 24 phases (seed 777): 16/24 at 2000, 20/24 at 3000, 24/24 at 5000. Localising this neighbour in 80% of runs needs about 3000 ppm. A Gaussian 1.1 px PSF gives the same pattern. With no injection, 25 to 38% of runs return OFFSET_MARGINAL. Injecting on the target at 100 to 300 ppm gives ON_TARGET about as often as no injection (9 to 11 of 12), so a low-depth ON_TARGET is weak evidence.

## CLAIMS.md

- C-04 pins sha256 a81f7b1c for `results/ttv_ephemeris_audit.csv`. Commit 9266751 overwrote the file (now 50640b01) and CLAIMS.md was not updated.
- C-06 pins 7f735d0b for `results/blend_localization.csv`, now overwritten (a73e65e1). The C-06 figures, including 4.90 for 253923533, come from the 412043e version, which was made with no Gaia neighbour list (gaia_sid=none). The current file gives 5.08 with ON_TARGET_UNRESOLVED_NEIGHBOR. C-06's 31281821 (24.06, OFFSET_MARGINAL) is now 50.9 NEIGHBOR_BEB_LOCALIZED, and its 224279805 (0.55) is now 4.78.

## Suggested fixes

- Score the real offset against K phase-shifted nulls and report its rank.
- Report per-sector offsets and use their scatter in the error.
- Record duration and sectors used in the CSV.
- Pin CLAIMS.md hashes to a commit.

## Limits

11x11 cutouts, one injection geometry (and a hard one), BLS durations not recorded for some rows. Null phases on variable stars carry real modulation. This does not show that any claimed star is a blend.

## Rerun

At 3bc0163, call `multisector_wcs_blend_audit` with the defaults `converge.py` uses (2.0 h when T14_h is absent, at converge.py:49, and the sector list at converge.py:50). This reproduces the committed `blend_localization.csv` rows for 166848769, 253923533 and 224279805. For nulls, shift the ephemeris by the amounts above and call the same function unchanged. For hashes, run `git show 412043e:results/ttv_ephemeris_audit.csv | shasum -a 256`, and the same for the other file and for 9266751.

title: Crowding correction counted twice for SPOC depths in vetter.py
body:
Checked on main at 3bc0163.

## What happens

`vetter.py:15` computes `rp = sqrt(dep / cs) * rs * RSUN_RE`, where `cs` is the CROWDSAP header value. For SPOC rows `dep` comes from PDCSAP flux (`mast_data.py:111`), and the SPOC pipeline has already removed the crowding flux from PDCSAP. Smith et al. 2012 (arXiv:1203.1382, Sec 2.3.11, eq 2) give the step as:

    y~(t) = [ y(t) - (1 - c) * median(y(t)) ] / f

where c is the crowding metric (CROWDSAP) and f is the flux fraction (FLFRCSAP). The paper says that skipping this step makes planet radii come out too small. Dividing the depth by CROWDSAP again corrects the same flux twice. TESS SPOC PDCSAP applies the same step. That was not checked against the TESS data release notes.

The vetter also disagrees with itself. `vetter.py:52` tests `(ds / cs) / dep` against [0.25, 2.6], which treats `dep` as already corrected, while line 15 treats it as uncorrected.

## Size

Small for every row checked. For TIC 181015118 (`hz_issue5_audit.csv`: depth 9391.3 ppm, R* 0.393) the radius is 4.155 Re without the division. The CSV value of 4.19 implies cs = 0.983, so the inflation is about 0.8%. The inflation factor is 1/sqrt(cs).

The largest case found is TIC 31281821 (CROWDSAP 0.36), inflated 1.66x. It is rejected by the MES, rotation and WCS checks anyway.

No claim in CLAIMS.md changes. C-01 to C-07 carry no radius or are unaffected. For C-08, recomputing all 2421 rows moves 0 rows between classes and adds 0 small habitable-zone rows. An inflated radius can only add a veto, not remove one.

## Related gaps

- FFI rows have no PDC step. The flux is a 3x3 aperture sum (`deep_search.py:40-58`), so dividing by a crowding value is correct there. The value is a guess: 0.92 at `hz_core.py:23` and 0.94 at `cool_io.py:25`, never measured.
- On FFI rows `sap` is a copy of `f` (same two lines), so `sap_mismatch` compares the aperture with itself and is not an independent check.
- Stacks that mix SPOC and FFI sectors take one median `cs` (`mast_data.py:146`, `hz_core.py:41`), which is wrong for each half in a different way.
- `dr4_core.py:83` and `cool_core.py:42` multiply the depth by `(1 + contratio)`. This double counts for depths taken from SPOC or TESS-SPOC PDCSAP and is right to first order for QLP depths. The catalog has no per-row flux provenance, so the split is not known. The inflation is at most 2.5% for Platinum and 7% for Gold.
- There is no term for companion dilution, and the neighbour and companion factors are never combined. If both are added they compose as c1 + c2 - c1*c2. A single-band depth cannot separate them.

## Suggested smallest fix

- `vetter.py:15`: carry a per-stack flag and use `rp = sqrt(dep / (1.0 if spoc else cs)) * ...`. Keep line 52 as it is for SPOC.
- For FFI stacks, replace the guess with a measured CROWDSAP from an adjacent SPOC sector, or with `cs = 1 / (1 + contratio)`.
- `dr4_core.py:83` and `cool_core.py:42`: drop `(1 + crat)` when the depth came from SPOC or TESS-SPOC PDCSAP. This needs a provenance column from the upstream depth catalog.

## Optional test

A known-answer test with `fractions.Fraction` can check the composition rule. With nested flux fractions, the pairs (neighbour, companion) = (1/4, 0), (0, 1/4) and (1/7, 1/8) all give the same depth, since 1/7 + 1/8 - 1/56 = 1/4. That also shows a single band cannot split the two terms.

> Automated posting by agentic team with human oversight.

title: Cross-pollination from exoplanets-frontier: empirical MHD flare/convection intermittency via pont_beta(tau) and two-clock witness-map benchmarks
body:
Cross-reference: `Foundation-0/exoplanets-frontier#9`

## Two Observational Transfers for `turbulence/`, `witness-map/`, and `scripts/`

title: Research pattern: discover, rigorously enclose, independently verify
body:
## A reusable research pattern

**Find a candidate, enclose it rigorously, then have a separately written checker verify it.**

Captured at Ahraz Arifuddin's request after tracing method transfers across Foundation0. This is a synthesis of existing work, not a claim that f0 invented computer-assisted certification, a new scientific result, or an adopted organisation-wide policy.

### The three stages

1. **Discover freely.** Numerical search, heuristics, human intuition and AI can propose candidates. A candidate is evidence worth investigating, not yet a proof.
2. **Build a rigorous certificate.** Fix the exact problem, domain, assumptions and claim. Where appropriate, use exact arithmetic or outward-rounded interval bounds to enclose a true solution and prove the required existence/uniqueness conditions. If claiming a complete count or optimum, also certify the excluded region or lower bound; finding one solution does not establish completeness.
3. **Verify independently.** A separately written checker reads the problem and certificate, not the producer's success flag. It reconstructs the proof obligations with its own implementation and, where feasible, a different arithmetic library. It must reject malformed or corrupted certificates and return **not verified** when obligations remain unresolved.

### What travels between projects

The transferable object is the separation of **search, certificate production, and independent verification**, not an assumption that different scientific questions have the same answer. The expensive or creative search can change while the acceptance contract remains explicit and checkable.

For each transfer, preserve:
- exact inputs, assumptions, definitions, normalizations and claimed domain;
- certificate schema, source revisions, dependency versions and reproduction commands;
- the checker's trusted components and independence limitations;
- positive tests, deliberate certificate-corruption tests, and unresolved obligations;
- a precise status: candidate, certificate produced, independently checked, or proof-assistant checked, with the actual evidence for each.

Two programs agreeing is not by itself a proof: both can encode the wrong problem or share an unsound assumption. Independent numerical certification is also not automatically a Lean/Coq/Isabelle kernel-checked theorem, and a mathematical result does not validate its physical interpretation.

### Provenance and current status — checked 13 November 2026

- **[point-charges](https://github.com/Foundation-0/point-charges/blob/main/README.md)** is the concrete source example. Its README describes a numerical finder, a primary interval certifier, and an independently written Arb/exact-rational verifier that re-proves local existence and exclusion outside the boxes. It reports two independent implementations for 3–6 charges, but only the independent verifier completing for 7 charges. The README explicitly notes no human review. These are the repository's reported results; this capture did not rerun them.
- **[relative-equilibria #2](https://github.com/Foundation-0/relative-equilibria/issues/2)** explicitly proposes adapting the point-charges certifier and separate verifier. The issue is open; main's README still says “not started” and lists no project certificates. This is a planned transfer, not a certified count.
- **[certified-orbits #4](https://github.com/Foundation-0/certified-orbits/issues/4)** explicitly requests an independent verifier with its own rigorous integrator and arithmetic. **[PR #12](https://github.com/Foundation-0/certified-orbits/pull/12)** is an open input-audit component: it always returns `not_verified`, has no rigorous flow integrator, and cannot accept any orbit proof. This is an early component, not an established orbit certificate.

**The pattern is useful precisely because it lets bold exploration coexist with a strict boundary on what is claimed. The receiving projects remain plans or early components until their own proof obligations are discharged.**

title: Reconcile Phase-2 VERIFIED claims with missing reproducibility artifacts on main
body:
AI-assisted source/artifact audit at `f09d0874be7f3be4633cbf6f43a084c9cb4745bd` (2026-11-12). This is a repository consistency review, not an independent rerun of MAST/Gaia observations.

## Reproducibility gap
The new README, CLAIMS.md, and CHANGELOG.md describe Phase-2 implementations and completed empirical results. However, the complete recursive Git tree (`truncated: false`; only `main` branch listed) lacks:
- `despot.py`, `ttv_track.py`, `blend_gaia.py`, `converge_io.py`, `converge.py`, and `.github/workflows/converge.yml`;
- `results/benchmark_and_null.json`, `results/ttv_ephemeris_audit.csv`, `results/ttv_transit_epochs.csv`, `results/blend_localization.csv`, `results/despotted_mdwarf_audit.csv`, `results/sibling_residual_search.csv`, `results/CONVERGENCE_REPORT.md`, `results/convergence_certificates.json`, and `results/figures/`.

Consequently the advertised `python converge.py` command cannot run from this snapshot, and C-03's benchmark evidence and C-04/C-05/C-06's VERIFIED evidence cannot be inspected against the ledger's own definition (reproducible code committed on main plus benchmark/null checks). This does not establish that the research is false or that files do not exist elsewhere; it establishes that the published evidence chain is incomplete.

**Requested resolution:** publish the referenced code/data with pinned inputs and reproducible benchmark/null commands, or link an immutable accessible artifact location. Until then mark these completion/verification claims as pending publication or not yet independently reproducible rather than asserting the artifacts are committed. Add a lightweight documentation-path check to prevent missing runners/results being advertised as available.

## C-01 table reconciliation
The committed `results/blind_verification_s106_s107.csv` does contain 39 rows, 22 `CONFIRMED_ON_SCHEDULE` rows, and 2 `DATA_GAP` rows. The 22 confirmed rows cover **18 unique TICs**, not 22 unique candidates as the C-01 heading suggests. Within those rows, observed/predicted depth ratios are approximately **0.489–1.635** and maximum `cent_sig` is **2.69**. C-01 quotes TIC 170788495 S106 SNR **6.53**, while this CSV records **5.75** (S107 is 5.96). Please reconcile the narrative against the pinned table and state clearly that repeat transit-like detections, including rows already tagged `likely nearby FP`, are not planetary validation.

Refs: [amendment 1, A1-A3](https://github.com/Foundation-0/project-asma/blob/11ee869100bc96dd88e23bc73cd032e6f94f3394/protocols/pilot-001-reconstruction-amendment-1.md#L21-L256), [roadmap L103-L118](https://github.com/Foundation-0/project-asma/blob/11ee869100bc96dd88e23bc73cd032e6f94f3394/docs/roadmap.md#L103-L118).

**Q3-A2. Sensitivity configuration:** option A (XGBoost `hist`) / option B (outer seeds 101-200) / both / other / waive for the first run ([L48-L157](https://github.com/Foundation-0/project-asma/blob/11ee869100bc96dd88e23bc73cd032e6f94f3394/protocols/pilot-001-reconstruction-amendment-1.md#L48-L157)).

Option B still needs implementation and tests first (L141-L144).

**Q3-A3. Warnings and messages from model calls:** proposed policy (all warnings, messages and console text fatal, with an aggregate failure code) / counting alternative for glmnet saturation / other ([L158-L256](https://github.com/Foundation-0/project-asma/blob/11ee869100bc96dd88e23bc73cd032e6f94f3394/protocols/pilot-001-reconstruction-amendment-1.md#L158-L256)).

title: Witness Map: the hard-sphere gas witness is about 22 times too weak against measured C70 decoherence
body:
**Question.** The Witness Map's gas witness uses a hard-sphere rate: R = n v̄ π (a + r_gas)², with the long-wavelength limit from Schlosshauer 2019 (`witness-map/model.js`). Molecule interferometry has measured collisional decoherence directly. Should the map test its gas witness against that data, and give polarisable molecules a long-range cross-section?

This came out of the exploration of #39's avenues. It was checked by an independent reproduction and a skeptic who read the paper's table.

## The comparison

Hackermüller et al. 2003 (arXiv:quant-ph/0307238), Table 1, print the measured decoherence pressures p₀ of C70 in their Talbot-Lau interferometer: 0.46 to 1.32 × 10⁻⁶ mbar across the gases. Read the paper for the exact definition of p₀.

Run with the map's own hard-sphere gas witness in that geometry, the model gives:
- **The pressures:** 7 to 59 × 10⁻⁶ mbar. Its rate is therefore too low by a geometric-mean factor of about 22 over 9 gases, 24 with the map's own C70 proxy.
- **Against the paper's own theory:** about 16 times too low.
- **The spread:** 8.1-fold from H₂ to Xe, where the measured spread is 2.9-fold. The difference comes from the long-range London (van der Waals) attraction, which a hard sphere leaves out.

**Cause.** About 17 times of the gap is cross-section physics; the rest is apparatus and residual. Hornberger et al. 2003 (arXiv:quant-ph/0303093) already note that the effective cross-section "exceeds the geometric one by two orders of magnitude".

## How much it matters for the map

**Probably little.** For small separations the relevant (momentum-transfer-weighted) cross-section is only 2 to 4 times geometric, not the total cross-section's ~100.

For C60 at 250 nm, for example:
- the gas witness rises from 3.35 × 10⁻³ /s to 0.054–0.074 /s;
- that is still below the 900 K glow (0.188 /s);
- W rises only 1.26 to 1.37 times, and the main witness does not change.

**Not yet checked:** every row of the map.

## First steps
- [ ] Add a measured-vs-model check against Table 1 of quant-ph/0307238. Expect a factor of about 22 against measurement and about 16 against the paper's theory, and say so rather than hide it in a tolerance.
- [ ] Add an optional London cross-section for the gas witness, with C6 from Hornberger et al. 2003.
- [ ] Recompute the rows with polarisable objects (C60, C70, Rb) using the momentum-transfer-weighted cross-section, and report which labels, if any, move.

title: Turbulence: the contour loops' offset above (3 − H)/2 has been measured before (Mandre and Kalda 2011)
body:
**Question.** `turbulence/README.md` (cloud edges) finds single contour loops sitting about 0.035–0.039 above Kondev and Henley's (3 − H_eff)/2. It says the offset's "origin is open" and that it "is not explained". A published measurement bears directly on this. Should the README cite it, and say what it settles and what it does not?

This came out of the exploration of #39's avenues. Two independent checks confirmed it: a separate exact-surface reimplementation and a literature read.

## The published measurement

Mandre and Kalda, Eur. Phys. J. B 84 (2011), arXiv:1105.2974, measured single-isoline dimensions on rough surfaces to about ±0.001, with box sizes 8 to 2048. Their table:

| H | D_h | Offset above (3 − H)/2 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.25 | 1.3958 ± 0.0014 | +0.021 |
| 0.5 | 1.2820 ± 0.0008 | +0.032 |
| 0.75 | 1.1565 ± 0.0010 | +0.032 |
| 0.875 | 1.0862 ± 0.0008 | +0.024 |

They conclude that the conjecture x_l ≡ 1/2 is "clearly rejected". Avellaneda et al. (1993) had already found 1.28 ± 0.015 at H = 0.5. Kondev, Henley and Salinas 2000 quote that result, and the README cites their paper.

## An independent confirmation on exact surfaces

These are exact fractional Brownian surfaces, made by Stein circulant embedding, whose structure function is exactly r^(2H) at every separation. Fitting P against R_g over R_g = 8 to 256:

| H | Run 1 | Independent reimplementation | Offset above (3 − H)/2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 1.375 | 1.3764 | +0.025 |
| 0.5 | 1.283 | 1.2842 | +0.033 |
| 0.7 | 1.189 | 1.1897 | +0.039 |

- **Calibration.** The same pipeline recovers 7/4 for percolation hulls (1.746 ± 0.004) and 3/2 for the Gaussian free field (1.498 ± 0.001).
- **Scale dependence.** At H = 0.3 and 0.5 the offset is flat within errors in two-octave windows from R_g = 4 to 256. At H = 0.5 it shows no bend-down out to R_g ≈ 512.

## Caveats
- **Estimator bias at large H.** The direct P-against-R_g fit overshoots there:
  - at H = 0.9 it gives 1.105, which is on the rigorous bound 2 − H and about 0.035 above Mandre and Kalda;
  - at H = 0.7 the local offset falls with scale, from +0.049 to +0.030.
  
  So read values at H ≥ 0.7 as upper estimates. Kondev, Henley and Salinas's Table I shows the same overshoot of the direct estimator at α ≥ 0.6, and the README already notes this.
- **What the offset means is unresolved.** Reading it as 2x_l ≈ 0.93 at H = 0.5 assumes hyperscaling and the sum rule. Two published results point the other way:
  - published τ exponents (Kondev, Henley and Salinas's finite-size scaling) imply D at or below (3 − H)/2;
  - their direct G(r) gives 2x_l ≈ 1.00.
  
  Nobody has measured D, τ and G(r) on the same loops. That measurement would separate "x_l ≠ 1/2" from "hyperscaling or the sum rule fails here".
- **Coastlines cannot decide it.** Ten real coastlines (arXiv:2409.20315) fit both (3 − H)/2 and the exact-fBm curve within their ±0.02 errors.
- **Mandre and Kalda's surfaces.** They are sums of random cones, so only approximately Gaussian, and the authors chose the layering by hand. The agreement with exact-fBm numbers strengthens both measurements, but proves neither.

## First steps
- [ ] Cite Mandre and Kalda 2011 beside Kondev and Henley 1995 in `turbulence/README.md`, and replace "its origin is open" with what is known. The offset is measured, and at H ≈ 0.5 it agrees with the README's own.
- [ ] Optionally, add an exact-fBm calibration to `contours.js` at H = 0.5, alongside the periodic Fourier surfaces, to separate the finite-grid H_eff effect from the intrinsic offset.
- [ ] The open part is measuring τ and G(r) on the same loops. That could become a short study of its own.

title: Cosmic homogeneity: Bagla, Yadav & Seshadri's weak-clustering D_q formula miscounts pairs for q ≠ 2
body:
**Question.** `cosmic-homogeneity/` (#26, #17) uses only D_2, where this changes nothing. But the note in #39 and the literature the study draws on speak of generalised dimensions D_q. Should the repository carry the corrected weak-clustering D_q, and say what it changes?

This came out of the exploration of #39's avenues. It was checked by an independent derivation, three controlled numerical tests, and a reading of the published simulation figures. All numbers below are from those checks.

## The formula and the slip

Bagla, Yadav and Seshadri 2008 (BYS08; MNRAS 390, 829, App. B; arXiv:0712.2905) give, for weak clustering,

  D_q ≈ 3 + (q/2) d xibar/d ln r.

**Where it goes wrong.** Their App. B expands the galaxy-centred count moments ⟨N^m⟩. It gives every one of the m(m+1)/2 pairs (the centre plus m neighbours) the one-point volume average xibar. Only the m centre–neighbour pairs carry xibar. The m(m−1)/2 neighbour–neighbour pairs, with both points integrated over the sphere, carry the shot-noise-free variance of counts in spheres, σ²(r) = V⁻² ∫∫ ξ.

**The corrected first-order result** (prime = d/d ln r; continuum limit):

  D_q ≈ 3 + xibar′ + ((q − 2)/2) σ²′.

- The two agree only at q = 2, or at isolated radii where σ²′ = xibar′. Elsewhere they differ by ((q − 2)/2)(σ²′ − xibar′).
- BYS08's own shot-noise term already has the neighbour–neighbour coefficient m(m−1)/2, which is the Poisson part of σ² + 1/N̄. The clustering term should have the same structure.
- The correction is a one-line consequence of the standard count-moment expansion (Peebles 1980, §36). It is an erratum, not a new method.
- **A second, minor inconsistency.** BYS08 eq. 6 counts the centre and App. A keeps the resulting (q − 1)/N̄ term, but App. B drops it. So their weak-clustering formula does not reduce to their homogeneous one as ξ → 0.

## Checks

**Controlled tests.** In each test, the corrected formula's residual shrinks as amplitude⁴, while BYS08's shrinks only as amplitude².
- An exactly solvable plane-wave Cox process.
- 256³ lognormal fields, with D_q measured directly:
  - corrected residual: 1e-4 or less for q = −2 to 6;
  - BYS08's residual: 1e-3 to 1e-2, about the size of D_q − 3 itself.
- A Poisson catalogue of about 4×10⁵ points with exact pair counts. The measured D_q matches exact theory, and its clustering part follows the corrected formula.

**What changes for linear ΛCDM** (Planck 2018, z = 0):
- σ²′/xibar′ is about 0.66–0.72, so the slope of D_q in q is about 0.7 of BYS08's.
- D_0 = 2.89, 2.96 and 2.98 at 20, 40 and 60 h⁻¹ Mpc. BYS08 gives exactly 3.
- D_q crosses 3 near q ≈ −0.8 to −1.0, not at q = 0.
- ΔD_4 is about 0.85 of BYS08's.

**Published simulations agree with the corrected shape.** Neither is decisive on its own.
- **Yadav, Bagla and Khandai 2010** (arXiv:1001.0617), Fig. 1, read from its vector data. Outside the BAO region, the N-body ΔD_4 is 0.82–0.89 of the BYS08 formula; the authors describe the gap as "less than 10%". The corrected formula predicts 0.81–0.86.
- **Bandyopadhyay, Choudhury and Seshadri 2017** (arXiv:1611.05554). Their z = 7 field gives D_q ≈ 2.995 − 0.0083 q, so q* ≈ −0.63, against −0.65 predicted.
  - All ten of their points lie below the BYS08 line.
  - Mocks of their estimator follow the corrected formula to rms 0.0009, against 0.0094 for BYS08.
  - Their quoted errors alone cannot exclude BYS08: χ² = 9.7 on 9 degrees of freedom.

## What this does and does not change

**Unchanged:** anything that uses only D_2, which includes this repository's study.

**Not specific to the correction:** with a fixed threshold, a homogeneity scale R_H(q) depends on q under BYS08 too, because there ΔD_q ∝ q.

**Specific to the correction:**
- D_0 falls below 3.
- The crossing q* moves from 0 to about −0.8.
- The slope ratio is about 0.7.
- Yadav et al. 2010's argument that their homogeneity scale is "unique" for all q no longer holds. That argument rests on their eq. sigdq, Var{ΔD_q} ≃ (Dq/2)² Var{xibar − ξ}. The corrected r_H(q) trend is robust, but its values (about 120–450 or 140–670 h⁻¹ Mpc for q = −1 to 10) depend on the variance model, so they are not quoted as results.

**Limits:** when xibar is a few percent and q ≥ 3, second-order terms shrink the advantage over BYS08.

**Novelty:** no correction turned up among about 100 arXiv papers citing BYS08, Yadav et al. 2010 or BCS17. The published MNRAS texts and non-arXiv citers were not checked.

## First steps
- [ ] Add D_q(r) from xibar and σ² to `cosmic-homogeneity/homogeneity.js`, with a test that D_2 equals the existing D2.
- [ ] Test it on a Poisson-sampled lognormal catalogue, including the shot-noise term.
- [ ] Tabulate q*(r), D_0(r) and the D_q slope against BYS08's. Say plainly where second order matters.
- [ ] Before any erratum-style note outside this repository, read the published MNRAS texts and the non-arXiv citers.

After PRs #26, #33, #34, #35, #37 merge, the site footer/studies list (index.html, 404.html, gravitational-atom/index.html) should include every published study: Witness Map, Gravitational atom, Quantum paths, The critical point, Cosmic homogeneity, Halos, Turbulence, Orbits. Currently main lists only Witness Map and Gravitational atom. PR #33 adds Quantum paths + Critical point to the three pages but omits the later studies, and the other PRs do not touch the site list. A follow-up pass should sync all three pages with the full studies list once the study PRs land.

Partial implementation: https://github.com/Foundation-0/fractals/pull/33 updates the studies section and all three footers for the studies merged so far. The remaining study pull requests still need their reviewed fixes before the complete list can be synchronised.



## Remaining acceptance

The merged critical-study follow-up updates the studies already on main. Completing the full list still depends on these open changes-requested pull requests:

- [Cosmic homogeneity](https://github.com/Foundation-0/fractals/pull/26): resolve the README and corrections-log integration conflicts, retain both studies, then review the integrated head.
- [Halos](https://github.com/Foundation-0/fractals/pull/35): correct the pending source-summary findings and review the integrated head.
- [Orbits](https://github.com/Foundation-0/fractals/pull/37): retain both studies’ workflow checks when resolving the integration conflict, then review the integrated head.

After those studies merge, the acceptance check is that the studies section and the footers in `index.html`, `404.html` and `gravitational-atom/index.html` include each merged study. The site-link gate must pass. The issue remains open because the merged partial update does not include those three unmerged studies.

title: Joint proof build: upstream Proofs/Spec module names collide across packages
body:
## Problem

The repo's stated purpose is "one toolchain, and one joint build". For a collection whose value is the proofs, that joint build should also check the proofs. Today it can't:

- `Anthology.lean` imports only each package's main library, so `lake build Anthology` compiles no proofs.
- The proofs can't just be added to the imports, because upstream uses the same top-level module names in many packages. At the pinned commits:
  - `Proofs` is a top-level `lean_lib` in 14 of the 18 packages: bencode, codec, csv, dns, ip, json, pep440, png, protobuf, rfc3339, semver, toml, utf8, uuid. Only resp, tar-pilot, websocket and zip-pilot have none.
  - `Spec` is a top-level `lean_lib` in 6 packages: bencode, codec, protobuf, rfc3339, semver, utf8. At least bencode's and codec's proofs also import a module named `Spec.Defs`.
  - Every package's executable root is `Main`. That doesn't affect imports, but it is the same pattern.

  Lean needs module names to be unique across a workspace, so a single module can't import two packages' `Proofs`.

Until this is fixed, the proofs are checked only by `scripts/build-all.sh`, one package at a time. With https://github.com/Foundation-0/proven-commons/pull/3 that covers all 14 packages, including bencode, whose upstream `defaultTargets` leaves its `Proofs` out.

## Proposal

The fix belongs upstream, since this repo is a compilation only:

1. Ask each upstream repo to move its `Proofs` and `Spec` libraries under the package namespace, as `Bencode.Proofs`, `Bencode.Spec`, `Bencode.Spec.Defs` and so on. This is a mechanical rename, but it touches the `lake comparator` / `bar.toml` setup upstream, so it is upstream's call.
2. Ask bencode upstream to add `Proofs` (and `Spec`) to its `defaultTargets`, as the other packages do.
3. Once a package has renamed, import its `<Pkg>.Proofs` in `Anthology.lean` (or in a second aggregator, `AnthologyProofs.lean`, so the main-library build stays fast), and drop its special case from `build-all.sh`.

## Checklist

- [ ] Agree the naming convention with the Proven-Commons maintainers, and record where (the mission repo?).
- [ ] Open an upstream issue per affected repo (14), linked here.
- [ ] Open an upstream issue for bencode's `defaultTargets`.
- [ ] Add each renamed package's proofs to the aggregator as its pin moves past the rename.

Related: the axiom audit in https://github.com/Foundation-0/proven-commons/issues/1 gets simpler once one aggregator imports every proof, because a single `#print axioms` pass can cover the whole collection.

Implementation pull request: [PR #7](https://github.com/Foundation-0/proven-commons/pull/7).

## Remaining integration draft

The sync implementation has merged. [The remaining joint-proof acceptance draft](https://github.com/Foundation-0/proven-commons/pull/8) adds a runnable inventory and the acceptance sequence for the upstream namespace and declaration work. The current recorded inventory has 14 proof-bearing packages and none jointly admitted. The draft awaits independent review.

This issue remains open until upstream tracking is recorded and every proof-bearing package at the accepted pins passes the actual joint build and audit checks. The inventory script alone does not establish that result.

title: Research review: checker output, exit codes and input model

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Gap and error, lower priority, from a review of main at `01e5182`. Items 1 and 2 can print six PASS lines and exit 0 for loads the input no longer describes. Items 3 to 8 concern the output; items 9 and 10 add to tracked items.

## Where

`src/flexure440.py` (byte-identical to `04012d4`, sha256 `77583629…`); `results/track-1-flexure/` (`verify.py`, `PROOF.md`, `certificate.json`), `tests/test_track1.py` and the `Makefile` as changed by PR #3; the Track 1 track file and input. Links point at `01e5182`; PR #7 links at its head, `e9aa47f`.

## Evidence

Reproductions run `python3 src/flexure440.py <input>` on a copy of `01e5182` with the listed Track 1 input fields changed. Items 6 and 7 also edit the checker, re-lock it, and run `make certificates` then `make verify`, as a checker pull request must today (#10 item 1).

### Input model: PASS for loads the input no longer describes

1. **`ebi` is a free input, never derived from the loads or checked against them.** Extends #5 item 8. The derivation (0.0012517 under dead load) is in this review's comment on #5 and used in #11 item 6.
   - [L58](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L58) and [L143-146](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L143-L146) use `inp["ebi"]` as given. The [track file L23-27](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L23-L27) lists 0.0013 next to "existing live 1.00 k/ft" without saying which load is on at installation. Dead plus existing live gives 0.001707, which flips no Track 1 verdict (fs,s 47.50 against 48.00 ksi).
   - Reproduced on `01e5182` with `loads.wDL_kipft` 2.0, `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 2.35 and `service_moment_kipft` 339.84 = (2.0 + 2.35)·25²/8. `ebi` left at 0.0013: six PASS lines, exit 0, including "PASS  Design strength, phiMn >= Mu: 481.74 vs limit 481.25". `ebi` 0.000910, what this dead load gives: "FAIL  Design strength, phiMn >= Mu: 478.56 vs limit 481.25", exit 1 (φ 0.900 → 0.894).
   - A stale ebi can err either way: a higher ebi raises φ near εs = 0.005 but is conservative for fs,s.

2. **`service_moment_kipft` is never checked against the loads, even on the simple span the checker assumes.** Extends #4 item 8 (continuous and cantilever members).
   - [L165-166](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L165-L166) compute both strength demands as w·L²/8, but [L138](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L138) reads Ms from its own input.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182` with `frp.wf_in` 14 and `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 1.9. Ms left at 340: six PASS lines, exit 0, with "PASS  Service steel stress, fs,s <= 0.80 fy: 45.84 vs limit 48.00". Ms = (2.75 + 1.9)·25²/8 = 363.28: "FAIL  Service steel stress, fs,s <= 0.80 fy: 48.64 vs limit 48.00", exit 1.
   - PR #7's `support_condition` accepts any string starting with "simple" ([L244](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/e9aa47f/src/flexure440.py#L244)) and does not compare Ms. On its head the fs,s line still passes (the run exits 1 only from its new fc,s check).

### What the printed lines show

3. **The PASS/FAIL lines leave out the governing mode, c, εs, φ and the force residual** ([L210-211](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L210-L211)); only the JSON has them.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`: `steel.As_in2` 8 prints "PASS  Design strength, phiMn >= Mu: 575.81 vs limit 457.81", with no sign that crushing controls and φ = 0.720. `beam.h_in` 7.0 (h < d) prints six PASS lines and exits 0, with `balance_kips` −49.9 only in the JSON; the root cause is #4 item 4.
   - The certificate records c, εs and the mode, not φ or the residual ([verify.py L75-95](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L75-L95)). The wrong mode label when the cap governs is #12 item 8.

4. **Every line uses one `.2f` format with no units, so a FAIL can print between two equal numbers.** Extends #4 item 13 (strain lines).
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`: `service_moment_kipft` 355.23 prints "FAIL  Service steel stress, fs,s <= 0.80 fy: 48.00 vs limit 48.00" (fs,s = 48.0021); `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 1.79143 prints "FAIL  Design strength, phiMn >= Mu: 481.74 vs limit 481.74" (481.7387 against 481.7412).
   - PR #7's `fmt()` ([L314-315](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/e9aa47f/src/flexure440.py#L314-L315)) adds digits only below 0.1; on its head, Ms 355.23 still prints "48.00 vs limit 48.00".

5. **The CLI has no usage message, and a crash exits 1 like a FAIL.** Exit codes are #8 item 3, JSON on stdout #4 item 13, the Makefile #4 item 14.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`: no argument gives `IndexError`, `--help` gives `FileNotFoundError: … '--help'`, and a real FAIL (`loads.wLL_new_kipft` 3.0) writes nothing to stderr. All three exit 1.
   - Draft PR #15 prints a usage line and exits 2, with check lines on stderr and JSON alone on stdout. PR #7 alone sends check lines to stderr, but a missing file still gives a traceback and exit 1.

### How the output is built

6. **Checks are positional tuples keyed by their label text, and the certificate depends on that text.** Not in #4 or #5.
   - [L192-202](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L192-L202) build `[label, value, limit, pass]`, with no id, unit, comparator or clause. [verify.py L103-104](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L103-L104) keys `checks_pass` by label and drops the debonding row by its prefix, "Debonding strain".
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`: renaming only that label to "FRP debonding strain, efd <= 0.9 efu" leaves `make verify` at exit 0, and `checks_pass` grows from 6 to 7 entries, with the renamed row certified `true`, though [PROOF.md L75](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L75) says "The debonding strain is a definition, not a sixth check".
   - The track file asks for this row to be reworded as a definition ([L71-75](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L71-L75)); any rewording without the prefix does this. PR #7's new label keeps the prefix by chance, and PR #7 drops `checks` from the JSON ([L325](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/e9aa47f/src/flexure440.py#L325)), leaving pass flags for 2 of its 7 checks.

7. **The same values and pass flags are computed in several places, and editing one copy passes `make verify`.** Extends #4 item 15; the service-limit copies and an `fs_limit_ksi` edit are in #11 item 2.
   - Copies: φ ([L116-117](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L116-L117)), φMn (L176, L184, L197 twice), the strengthening-limit flag (L181, L196), `design_pass` (L184, L197), 0.9 εfu (L49, L194 twice, verify.py L105).
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`. Editing only the duplicates (`strengthening_limit.pass` against 1.2× the demand, `design_pass` against 1.1 Mu, `fs_limit_ksi` as 0.60 fy): `make verify` exits 0, the only certificate changes are the checker hash and the date, and the JSON shows both flags false beside true check rows. Editing only the printed limit at L199, to 0.70 fy: "PASS  Service steel stress, fs,s <= 0.80 fy: 46.13 vs limit 42.00", and `make verify` exits 0.
   - The tests take pass flags only from `checks` ([L55](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tests/test_track1.py#L55)); verify.py reads none of `design_pass`, `strengthening_limit.pass` or `service_limits`.

8. **No input schema or shared check record, and verify.py copies the test helpers.** Minor. `resolve()` and the `sys.path` insert are in [tests L25-39](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tests/test_track1.py#L25-L39) and again in [verify.py L39-65](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L39-L65). A Track 2 checker could import `run()`'s helpers but would copy item 6's tuple shape.

### Already tracked, with what is new

9. **The creep-rupture limit is for carbon only.** This is #4 item 9 and #5 item 12; an explicit fiber key is ignored too (#8 item 4).
   - New: the steel limit usually governs first, but not always. Reproduced on `01e5182` with glass-like `frp.Ef_ksi` 4000, `ffu_star_ksi` 60, `efu_star` 0.015, `CE` 0.65, `plies` 2, `tf_in` 0.05, plus `ebi` 0 and `service_moment_kipft` 357: no warning, "PASS  Service steel stress, fs,s <= 0.80 fy: 47.98 vs limit 48.00" and "PASS  Service FRP stress, ff,s <= 0.55 ffu: 7.91 vs limit 21.45", against a glass limit of 0.20 × 0.65 × 60 = 7.80 ksi. (The run exits 1, from design strength.)
   - New, extending #5 item 12: the line is labelled "Service FRP stress" ([L200](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L200)), not creep rupture, and no scope line excludes the fatigue stress range.

10. **FRP in compression, and the steel stress clamp.** This is #4 item 5. Reproduced on `01e5182`: at `steel.As_in2` 40, ffe = −1.90 ksi and φMn = 691.52 kip-ft, against 691.65 from a copy with the FRP stress floored at 0 and fs clamped at ±fy in [L70-71](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L70-L71). New: compression starts at c > 0.003·27/(0.003 + 0.0013) = 18.84 in ([L60](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L60)), which on the Track 1 beam needs As above about 33 in² (ρ ≈ 10%). The effect is small and conservative. Flooring the FRP strain instead, as PR #7 does, gives 703.35 here.

## What should change

These go in a checker pull request, as #4 sets out (#10 item 1 covers passing CI). Exit-code and single-limit tests are in #11 item 2; each other item needs a test that fails before the fix.

- **Items 1 and 2.** Compute ebi from an installation-load input (dead, or dead plus existing live), or WARN when `ebi` differs from it. Compare Ms with (wDL + wLL_new)·L²/8 and warn or refuse. State the installation load in the docstring, track file and PROOF.md.
- **Items 3 and 4.** Print a governing line first ("Governing: FRP debonding | c = 7.49 in | es = 0.00527 | phi = 0.90 | residual 0.000 kips") and add φ and the residual to the certificate. Give each check a unit and enough digits that a FAIL never shows two equal numbers ("48.002 ksi vs limit 48.000 ksi").
- **Item 5.** Keep draft PR #15's exit codes (0, 1, 2), usage line and JSON-only stdout.
- **Items 6 to 8.** Emit each check as `{id, label, value, limit, unit, comparator, pass, clause}`, key `checks_pass` by `id`, and keep and document `checks`. Compute each value once, derive or drop the duplicate pass flags, and have verify.py read the cap from the output. Before Track 2, put the check record, input validation and `resolve()` in one shared, locked module.
- **Items 9 and 10.** As planned under #4 items 9 and 5; label the check "FRP creep rupture stress" and scope out the fatigue stress range.

Coverage in the open pull requests, in the versions read:
- **PR #7:** item 9's fiber factor and label, JSON-only stdout, item 4 below 0.1, and part of item 7 (φ once, and one `limits` dict for `service_limits` and the checks; the duplicate pass flags and φMn copies remain). For item 10 it clamps the FRP strain rather than the FRP stress, which moves the steel strain off the strain profile and overstates φMn by up to about 11% (see the comment on PR #7). It drops `checks` from the JSON, so a saved stdout file shows no verdict for the concrete FAIL. It matches `support_condition` by prefix, so a point-loaded "simple span" passes item 2's guard. It stops on the h = 7 input with a `ValueError` traceback, exit 1. Open: items 1, 2's Ms check, 3's summary line, 6 and 8.
- **Draft PR #15, stacked on PR #7:** item 5's exit codes (0, 1, 2) and usage line; item 10 with only the FRP stress clamped; every check verdict and `all_pass` back in the stdout JSON (item 6 in part: no id, unit or clause yet); `support_condition` must be exactly a simple span under uniform load; it refuses item 3's h = 7 input (exit 2, "ERROR: beam.df_in must be <= beam.h_in") and validates inputs (#8 items 3 and 4). Open: items 1, 2's Ms check, 3's summary line, 4, the rest of 6, 7 and 8.

Questions for a maintainer:
- Items 1 and 2: should the checker derive ebi and Ms from the loads, or keep them as inputs with a consistency warning?
- Item 6: is the JSON output an interface others may build on? If so, it needs a documented, versioned schema.

AI disclosure: generated with Claude Code.

Implementation pull request: [PR #7](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/7).

title: Research review: untracked checker gaps, removed page gate, admin and review record, tier claim, AI disclosure

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Gap, wrong label and missing credit, in the process record of main at `01e5182` and of PRs #1, #2, #3 and #7 (GitHub read 2026-10-25). No checker number changes. Items that extend #4, #5 or #6 say so. These are observations about records and settings, not about any person.

## Where

`docs/status.md`, `docs/review-ledger.md`, CONTRIBUTING, CONTRIBUTORS, LICENSE, the PR template, the Track 1 track file and PROOF.md; reviews, merges and settings on GitHub; and [REPO-STANDARD.md at `570bd0e`](https://github.com/Foundation-0/.github/blob/570bd0e/REPO-STANDARD.md), which docs/status.md L3-4 says the repo follows.

## Evidence

The record, UTC. The author's agent opened all three PRs from the abu-aska account.

| PR | Approval | Merged by | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | ahrazzle, 07:48:45: "Project greenlit - initiate build" | fdn-0, 07:50:52 | 2 min |
| #2 | ahrazzle, 08:12:46: ten matches re-run, eight observations | fdn-0, 08:24:46 | 12 min |
| #3 | fdn-0, 15:50:15, empty body | ahrazzle, 15:50:58 | 43 s |

On PR #3, fdn-0's 18 inline comments each say a tool generated them; all were resolved. At 15:49:02 fdn-0 wrote "Approval is the maintainer's decision" ([comment](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/3#issuecomment-6399743514)).

### Checker trust

1. **Two checker gaps that can print PASS for a beam that should fail are in none of the review issues, and open PR #7, the checker PR that #4 prescribes, leaves both in place.**
   - The ACI 440.2R-17 §1.2.1.4 substrate limits (no FRP below f'c 2500 psi; pull-off ≥ 200 psi for bond-critical work) and the ACI 562-16 §5.5.2.1 live-load factor of 1.0 for sustained live load. #4, #5 and #6 never mention 2500 psi, pull-off, substrate or a sustained live-load factor.
   - Reproductions: #8 items 1 and 2, six PASS lines and exit 0 each. PR #7 at `e9aa47f` keeps `(1.1 * wdl + 0.75 * wll)` and adds no f'c floor; draft PR #15, stacked on PR #7, adds both. The status.md debt list ([L32-44](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/docs/status.md?plain=1#L32-L44)) points to no open review issue.

2. **PR #2 removed the seed's page-check gate, and three of the ten test values entered the record in the checker PR itself. They carry VERIFIED with no page recorded in the repo.** Extends #5 items 2 and 5.
   - The seed track file ([`0e967c9` L58-68](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/0e967c9/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L58-L68)) required "the page for each number", the design demand and limit check "with pages", the bar layout, and corrections "before the checker pull request opens". PR #2's [`1805bd3`](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/commit/1805bd3) deleted all of these.
   - It added As,min 1.12 under the inputs' KNOWN header, and existing φMn 387 and limit 330 under "KNOWN, from the example. A checker earns VERIFIED only by matching these". All three are in `expected.json` and VERIFIED on main ([PROOF.md L50-52](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L50-L52)).
   - The PR #2 body places them on "the example's first page", but no page is recorded on main, and the body does not mention the removed gate. Only the generic obligation ([track file L76-79](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L76-L79)) covers them. The printed design demand was never recorded (#12 item 4).
   - PR #3 restated, with no page, "The example text cites ACI 562-16, Section 5.5.2" (track file L51), a claim from PR #2's docstring ("as cited there"). The reviewer had asked for it "only if the publisher copy says so" ([thread](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/3#discussion_r4371350986)).
   - By hand the values agree, so this is provenance, not a numeric error: As,min = 200 × 14 × 24 / 60,000 = 1.12; φMn = 0.9 × 4.00 × 60 × (24 − 5.04/2) / 12 = 386.6; limit = (1.1 × 2.75 + 0.75 × 1.60) × 25² / 8 = 330.1.

### Who can change the guards, and who reviewed

3. **The author's agent works from an admin seat, and main is guarded only by branch protection any of four admins can change.**
   - ahrazzle, abu-aska, orda-aska and fdn-0 are all `admin`; `gh api` shows no repository or branch rulesets. The §C org ruleset with no bypass actors ([L72-86](https://github.com/Foundation-0/.github/blob/570bd0e/REPO-STANDARD.md?plain=1#L72-L86)) is not applied.
   - PR #1: "Repo settings done with this work, from the abu-aska admin seat". During PR #3 the agent says it set the required checks "through the API" ([comment](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/3#issuecomment-6395691425), item 11) while its own PR was open; the account is not stated. The change tightened protection; the reviewer had suggested it for after the merge.
   - status.md names no admins and does not define "signed by Shahid in the open" (L43-44); no commit carries a sign-off. No misuse is on record, but the guard on the locked checker holds only while no admin, the author's seat included, changes it.

4. **No person is on record as having reviewed or approved the Track 1 result.** [CONTRIBUTING L19-20](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L19-L20): "A person who did not write it reviews and merges it." "Person" is undefined. Distinct accounts wrote, approved and merged, but the PR #3 approval is empty and came 73 s after "Approval is the maintainer's decision", and the merger left no review or comment. The ledger (L12-14) correctly says no outside human engineering review has happened. No rule ties VERIFIED to human review, so this is a gap, not a broken rule.

5. **Observations in a review body need no answer before merge.** Extends #4, which tracks four of the PR #2 observations.
   - Conversation resolution covers inline threads only. PR #2's eight observations ([review](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/2#pullrequestreview-5642196451)) were "for the author to weigh before the checker is locked"; it merged 12 minutes later on the same head with no reply.
   - Never recorded: "Section es is 0.00527, just above the 0.005 value that gives phi 0.90" and the "thin" 46.1 vs 48.0 ksi service margin. Reproduced on `01e5182`: es = 0.005268; "46.13 vs limit 48.00". Still true: no argument gives `IndexError`, exit 1; `input.json` has no trailing newline. The templates question was never answered; PR #3 made it moot.
   - PR #3's one optional re-review request, to source "1.2 dead + 0.5 live" ([thread](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/3#discussion_r4371405609)), was still open at the merge two minutes later. The figure is wrong for ACI 562-16 §5.5.2; see #9.

6. **The PR template does not prompt for the checker lock, self-merge or the input file.** The checklist ([L24-29](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/.github/pull_request_template.md?plain=1#L24-L29)) has no item for CONTRIBUTING step 3 (no checker edit in a result PR) or step 5 (the author does not merge), and Validation does not ask for the input file. The lock is enforced by review alone (#6 item 2, #10 items 2 and 3). CONTRIBUTING does not say which PR moves the lock line; #4 puts it in a later result PR, PR #7 in the checker PR.

7. **"Tier: Active, sections A to D" is claimed with items from all four sections unmet and no written exemption.** Extends #5 item 13.
   - PR #3 changed status.md from Seed to Active. The standard ([L18-23](https://github.com/Foundation-0/.github/blob/570bd0e/REPO-STANDARD.md?plain=1#L18-L23)): a repo "moves up a tier by meeting the checklist, not by asking"; exemptions go in the README. No `.md` on main contains "exemption".
   - §A: no `og.jpg`; the README does not open with links to the notes and tracks. §B: no ACI 562-16 entry in NOTICE (#9 item 4), no AI checking credit (item 11). §C ([L79-80](https://github.com/Foundation-0/.github/blob/570bd0e/REPO-STANDARD.md?plain=1#L79-L80)): secret scanning, push protection and Dependabot security updates `disabled` (`gh api`, 2026-10-25), not listed in status.md. §D: no prior-art section (#12 item 7).
   - The status.md debt list also omits the fc,s failure, #4 and #5; of the open obligations it lists only the strengthened-strength one (L38-40).

### What the record says

8. **docs/review-ledger.md omits parts of the record, and its stated rule fits none of its rows.** [L3-4](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/docs/review-ledger.md?plain=1#L3-L4) records "Reviews by the account that merged", but fdn-0 merged PRs #1 and #2 and reviewed neither, and ahrazzle merged PR #3 and left no review. ahrazzle's approvals and the PR #2 observations are missing; #4 and #5 appear only on the PR #3 row. L10's "15 comments" is the reviewer's suggested wording ([thread](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/3#discussion_r4371351288)); PR #3 has 18 resolved threads.

9. **#4 and #5 say PRs #2 and #1 "merged without review". Each had an approving review** (see the table). #4 items 2, 4, 13 and 14 overlap the PR #2 observations without crediting them; #4 adds its own reproductions, so this is missing credit, not copying.

10. **PR #3's description was stale at merge.** "`make verify` passes: 4 unit tests"; reproduced on `01e5182`: "Ran 6 tests ... OK". "All six checks ... pass", where [PROOF.md L59](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L59) counts five pass or fail checks; L75 calls the debonding cap a definition. PR #3 uses three of the six template headings (the template arrived in it); PR #7 uses none.

### Disclosure, history and licence

11. **AI disclosure is missing for review and checking.** [CONTRIBUTING L38](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L38) says "name the model in every pull request"; §B wants CONTRIBUTORS.md to say which models did the checking. PR #2's approval names no model; PR #3's reviews and ledger L10 name a tool only; #4 and #5 carry no disclosure line; CONTRIBUTORS credits only the author agent, with no model version. All 60 non-merge commits are authored `shah` with no trailers.

12. **Commit history.** Every non-merge commit in PRs #1 to #3 changes one file, with one, one and three messages. With `git archive`, PR #3 commits 25 to 35 of 42 (`fe16c27` to `1116234`) fail `make verify`; PR #2's unit tests fail at `69a666f` and `a4a1f63` (no Makefile before `dcdfe00`). Merge commits put these in the range `git bisect` walks. Merged branches are kept.

13. **Licence, adding to #5 item 14.** Its "plain MIT LICENSE file" conflicts with §B ([L48-49](https://github.com/Foundation-0/.github/blob/570bd0e/REPO-STANDARD.md?plain=1#L48-L49)), which LICENSE L1-7 follows; GitHub reports `NOASSERTION`. No file contains the CC BY 4.0 URI. The certificates and `commitment/` fall in neither licence category.

## What should change

Items 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 13 need a maintainer decision.

- **1.** Decide before PR #7 merges whether both gaps go in it or in a second checker PR; draft PR #15 offers them stacked on PR #7. Docs PR #16 points the debt list to #4 and #8.
- **2.** Record why the checker PR went ahead before page checks, or restore the gate. Restore the removed obligations. Record p. 1 if the publisher copy confirms it; until then mark the three "first recorded in the checker PR, no page yet".
- **3.** Which accounts keep admin? Agent seats need only write. List admins and each protection change in status.md, apply the §C ruleset, and define the sign-off.
- **4.** Does "person" in step 5 mean a human? Record any human review with name and date, or say an AI review meets the rule.
- **5 and 6.** Template items: each review-body observation fixed, deferred to a named issue, or declined; `src/` and the lock line unchanged in a result PR; input sha256; no self-merge. Record the φ and service-margin observations, and say which PR moves the lock line.
- **7.** Meet §A to §D or get a written exemption; until then write "Active, with these items outstanding" and list them.
- **8 and 9.** Give the ledger reviewer (human or agent with model), approver and merger with dates, and fix its rule. Correct the opening lines of #4 and #5, and credit the PR #2 review in #4.
- **10 to 12.** Keep PR bodies current and use the template headings. Name the model in AI reviews and ledger rows, and add checking credit to CONTRIBUTORS. Squash-merge; turn on `delete_branch_on_merge`.
- **13.** Decide at org level whether licence detection should change §B. Add the CC BY 4.0 URI, and say which licence covers the JSON, certificate and commitment files.
