title: Research review: the Track 1 result docs leave out unconservative checker defects and overstate what was verified

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Error, gap, wrong label and missing prior art, in the result documents PR #3 added or changed and in seed and docstring text still on main at `01e5182`. Items are grouped by theme and keep the numbers other issues in this batch cite; items 1, 2, 3 and 8 matter most to an engineer relying on the checker.

## Where

`docs/audit.md`, `docs/status.md`, `results/track-1-flexure/` (`PROOF.md`, `certificate.json`), `tracks/`, `README.md`, `NOTICE`, and the docstrings of `src/flexure440.py` (unchanged since `04012d4`). Line links point at `01e5182`.

## Evidence

"Reproduced" means run on a copy of `01e5182` with `python3 src/flexure440.py`, on the Track 1 input with the listed fields changed. "Handout" is Simpson Strong-Tie's [SE University handout of 12 July 2021](https://doc.learnwithseu.com/seusessions/2021/07jul/seu_jul_2021_design_methods_calc_frp_handouts_1pp.pdf), cited by slide.

### Known defects left out of the result docs

1. **[docs/audit.md "Known weak points"](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/docs/audit.md?plain=1#L47-L65) lists only fc,s. Checker defects that overstate strength or pass a beam are not there, in the PROOF.md Scope (L101-102) or in the status debts (L32-44).** Reproduced; six PASS lines and exit 0 unless stated:
   - #4 item 2: `steel.As_in2` 12 gives existing Mn 986.2 kip-ft at εs 0.00105 < εy 0.00207. Strain compatibility gives 896.3 (10% high).
   - #4 item 3: `steel.As_in2` 10 crushes with α1β1 0.747, against 0.7225 for the Whitney block §10.2.10 gives for crushing (#4 asks to confirm that wording). φMn is 581.6 against 566.9 kip-ft with Whitney (+2.6%).
   - #4 item 7: `loads.wDL_kipft` 4.45, `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 0 prints "481.74 vs limit 417.19", but 1.4D = 486.7 kip-ft.
   - #4 item 4: `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 1.8 FAILs at 481.74 vs 482.81 (exit 1). Adding `beam.h_in` 2.25 PASSes at 531.27, 276.4 kips out of balance. h is never checked against d = 24 in; this beam needs h below about 7.9 in for the false PASS.
   - #8 items 1 and 2: no f'c ≥ 2500 psi gate, and no 1.0 factor for sustained live load (186.0 kip-ft against a printed limit of 156.00). Input validation: #8 item 3, #6 item 3.
   - The #4 items were known when PR #3 merged (#4 opened 15:28:10Z, merge 15:50:58Z); the rest were found later. None changes a Track 1 verdict (1.4D = 300.8 < 457.8; 1.1D + 1.0L = 361.3 < 386.6 kip-ft), so PROOF.md's "One gap" (L107) is fair for the beam, but audit.md describes the checker. The PROOF.md exclusions also omit crack width (#8 item 5) and the simple span (#4 item 8).

2. **The track file, tracks/README, the status debts and the certificate still read as complete and all-pass, though the beam fails the unchecked fc,s limit.** Extends #4 item 1, whose request to state that fc,s is not checked was met only in PROOF.md, audit.md and the README row.
   - From the checker's cracked section: fc,s = 3605 × (46.131/29000) × 8.899/(24 − 8.899) = 3.38 ksi > 0.60 f'c = 2.40 ksi.
   - The track file's [open obligations](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L65-L79) omit fc,s, PROOF.md's first, and its Goal (L5-8) still says the program "runs the flexure checks of ACI 440.2R-17 Chapter 10". tracks/README L7 and the status debts omit it.
   - [certificate.json L6-13](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/certificate.json#L6-L13): six `checks_pass`, all `true`, no field for unchecked limits. Reproduced: `verify.py` prints "RESULT: PASS".

### Claims and labels

3. **No "calculation aid, not a design" line and no not-checked list in the checker output, the replay or the certificate.** Reproduced: `grep -ciE 'aid|not a design|not checked|scope|shear|deflection|crack'` gives 0 on the checker and `verify.py` outputs, and no certificate key records scope. Scope is only in the [docstring](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L16-L21) and prose, against CONTRIBUTING L40-42: "A checker output is a calculation aid. It is not a design". #4 item 13 is number format, not this.

4. **Mu is the checker's own 1.2D + 1.6L (src L166), labelled "from printed loads" ([PROOF.md L55](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L55)) and credited to "ACI 440.2R-17, Chapter 10" (L63). No open obligation asks for the demand the example designs for.** Handout slide 4 takes load factors "stated in ACI 318". The seed obligation "Extract the demand the example designs for, and its strengthening limit check, with pages." ([L61-62 at 0e967c9](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/0e967c9/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L61-L62), deleted before `04012d4`) was dropped by PR #2 after only the second half was recorded. Slide 23 lists "Check flexural design strength vs. max. factored bending moment" for this example.

5. **"neither the checker nor the example's printed checks cover it" ([PROOF.md L107-109](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L107-L109); audit.md L61-62) is stated as fact, though PROOF.md L31 says only parts of the example have been read.** Handout slide 24 lists "Concrete stress ƒc,s ≤ 0.6 ƒ'c" for the example. L111-112 give 0.45 and 0.60 f'c with no edition: 0.60 is 440.2R-17 §10.2.8 ([Sika's PRC-440.2-23 guide](https://tha.sika.com/dms/getdocument.get/4af962fb-e849-4da3-84d4-8efe05b316ba/UserGuideSikaCarbodurACI-PRC-440-2-23-English-Sika-TH.pdf), §2.2.1), 0.45 the 2008 value.

6. **Labels outside PROVEN, VERIFIED, KNOWN and CONJECTURE (README L11), and unlabelled claims.** [PROOF.md L47-48](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L47-L48) and L53-55 use "checker output" and "from printed loads", which CONTRIBUTING L29 makes CONJECTURE. The track file's matched values (L93-104) carry no VERIFIED and its unverified outputs (L106-112) no CONJECTURE. The README row (L25) puts "Five pass or fail checks pass" under "VERIFIED for the ten printed quantities". PROOF.md L77-78 has a unit test "to prove the cap holds"; CONTRIBUTING L27: "A finite check is not a proof."

7. **PROOF.md has no prior art, which [REPO-STANDARD L92-93](https://github.com/Foundation-0/.github/blob/570bd0e/REPO-STANDARD.md?plain=1#L92-L93) requires, yet status.md L3-4 claims sections A to D.** PR #3's Prior art has no links or searches (PR template L15-18) and omits ACI 318 and ACI 562-16, which PROOF.md cites. The approaches rejected in the [PR #3 review](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/3#issuecomment-6395691425), items 1, 4, 5 and 9, are not in the track file's Failed attempts (L119-125), which PR #3 did not touch; CONTRIBUTING L16-18 asks for them.

8. **The checker prints "FRP debonding controls" ([L64](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L64)) when the 0.9 εfu cap governs and when there is no FRP.** Reproduced: `frp.tf_in` 0.02 (efd_uncapped 0.00985 > cap 0.00688) and `frp.wf_in` 0 (Af = 0) both print that mode. Track 1 is right (0.00493). The always-true debonding row is a track obligation (L71-75) that open PR #7 renames; neither PR #7 nor draft PR #15 changes the mode label.

9. **[NOTICE L39-40](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/NOTICE#L39-L40) says "record only the numbers a checker needs", but the track file records numbers the checker does not read:** the 215/125 k-ft split, the existing live load, "4 No. 9" and rs (reproduced: `loads.wLL_existing_kipft`, `steel.bars` and `source` are never read). Some feed open work (#5 item 8, #4 item 9, #8 item 5), so the fix is the wording.

### Citations and sources

10. **[README L15](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/README.md?plain=1#L15) credits "the concrete stress block rules" to ACI 318. Corrects #5 item 9.** Reproduced: Track 1 converges at α1 0.9282, β1 0.7886, the ACI 440.2R parabolic block (L59, L72-73). Whitney is used only in `existing_strength()` and not in crushing (item 1), contrary to #5 item 9. NOTICE L24-25 likewise.

11. **[NOTICE L34-36](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/NOTICE#L34-L36) says printed numbers carry their page; none does, and no file links the example. Extends #5 items 5 and 7.** New: on 2026-10-25 Simpson's CSS FRP page redirected to one saying Structural Technologies "has acquired the CSS product line", which now serves the CSS data sheets. The handout treats the example as a separate handout (slides 18-25); no public copy was found. A VERIFIED result (PROOF.md L18-20) and most open obligations (φMn and c, CE, pages) rest on it.

12. **[NOTICE L12](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/NOTICE#L12) and L16-17 say guide numbers are "cited to their section"; no ACI 440.2R constant in the checker is. Extends #5 item 5.** The only section number is ACI 562-16 Section 5.5.2 (L7, L20). ECU and ψf (L28-29) cite "ACI 440.2R-17" only, L44 says "Eq. for efd", and 1.7 (L59), the φ transition (L96-101; ACI 440.2R-17 Eq. (10.2.7), to be confirmed), β1 (L109-111) and 1.2/1.6 (L166) cite nothing. Since #5, CE became an input, and 0.80 fy and 0.55 ffu got sources in PROOF.md L64-65.

13. **ACI 562-16 is superseded too. Extends #6 item 1.** [ACI's abstract page](https://www.concrete.org/publications/internationalconcreteabstractsportal/m/details/id/51689083): "This document was replaced by 562-19"; the current edition is CODE-562-21. On `01e5182`, `grep -rniE 'supersed|562-19|PRC-440'` finds nothing.

14. **The service-stress closed form is credited to the example (src L121-125, PROOF.md L92-94, audit.md L49-52), and the [failed-attempt note](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L121-L124) credits the missing εbi term to "the example's closed form", not the guide's equation.** ACI's [440.2R-17 preview](https://www.concrete.org/Portals/0/Files/PDF/Previews/440.2R-17_preview.pdf), pp. 7-8, defines fs,s, ff,s and εbi in the guide's notation (equation number unconfirmed). Reproduced: `ebi` 0 gives fs,s = 41.771 ksi, the logged 41.8. Also, ff,s uses the full service moment (L138): 8.62 ksi, against −0.40 ksi at 215 k-ft; conservative for carbon, but unstated (#4 item 9).

15. **No ACI 318 edition is stated (NOTICE L19-22, README L15, docstring L8, [PROOF.md L66](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L66)).** Handout slide 7 cites "ACI 318-14; Sec. 21.2.1". `phi_for` matches 440.2R-17 Eq. (10.2.7) for the strengthened section and ACI 318-14 for the existing one. Under ACI 318-19 (εty + 0.003; [ICC overview](https://www.iccsafe.org/wp-content/uploads/An-Overview-of-Changes-from-ACI-318-14-to-ACI-318-19.pdf), slide 22) the existing φ at fy 80 ksi, εs 0.0050 would be 0.837, not 0.900. Track 1 is unaffected (existing εs 0.0091).

### Docstrings and stale text

16. **Docstrings describe what the code does not do.** [L18](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L18), "full width factor taken from input", names no input (also #8 item 3). L10 lists kip-in, which nothing uses, and omits ft and kip/ft. L105 omits the yield assumption (#4 item 2), and the scope omits the simple span (#4 item 8).
17. **"a JSON block with every number" ([L13-14](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L13-L14)).** Reproduced: it omits ε'c, the trial efe, ρs, ρf, the modular-ratio terms, the service lever arms, the steel and FRP parts of Mn, the existing β1 and the inputs.
18. **[README L10](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/README.md?plain=1#L10) says a program "will run each check"**, though L5 records a result, and README never names `src/flexure440.py`.

## What should change

**In docs PR #16:** item 1 (a "Known checker defects" list in audit.md, the PROOF.md Scope and the status debts, each with direction and reference; crack width and the simple span are still missing from the PROOF.md exclusions), item 2 (fc,s in the track obligations, tracks/README and the status debts; the track Goal is not yet qualified), items 5, 10, 13 and 18 in full, and the NOTICE wording for 11, 12 and 15, including that the ACI 318-19 φ affects only the existing section.

**Can go in the docs pull request, not there yet:**
- Item 2: qualify the track Goal.
- Item 4: label Mu CONJECTURE ("1.2D + 1.6L assumed, ACI 318-14; 1.4D not checked; the example's demand not yet read"), cite ACI 318, and restore the obligation to extract the example's maximum factored moment and combination, with pages.
- Item 6: relabel PROOF.md L47-48 and L53-55 CONJECTURE; label the track file's values VERIFIED or CONJECTURE and the README row's other claims; "shows" for "prove".
- Item 7: a Prior art section with the sources checked, links, and where searches found nothing (only the ACI 562 reading is there so far); the review-rejected approaches in Failed attempts.
- Item 9: NOTICE L39-40 to "the numbers needed to run, test or review the checker".
- Item 14: credit the service method to ACI 440.2R-17 in PROOF.md, audit.md and the note; say the εbi term the 41.8 ksi run left out is part of the guide's equation; state that ff,s uses the full moment, which is conservative.
- Item 15: the edition at PROOF.md L66.

**Needs a checker pull request** (hash-locked; see #4):
- Item 3: print "Calculation aid, not a design. Not checked: …" on every run and carry the list in the JSON (output format: #14).
- Item 8: name "FRP rupture cap (0.9 εfu)" when it governs; send Af = 0 to the plain section.
- Items 12, 14, 16, 17: section and equation numbers marked "to be confirmed against a licensed copy", the service equations credited to the guide, and "the main results" for "every number", or the missing values plus an input echo.
- Item 2: a certificate can only record all-PASS (#10 item 1). Until that is settled, add a field for unchecked limits, or say in PROOF.md that `checks_pass` covers only implemented checks.
- Open PR #7, the checker pull request for #4, and draft PR #15, stacked on it, both keep "every number", "the closed form the example prints", L44 and the mode label. PR #7 renames the debonding row, drops "full width factor", states the simple span and documents the strain-compatible existing strength, but keeps L10's units and prints no scope line. Draft PR #15 adds NOT CHECKED lines for the substrate requirements only, puts every verdict in the JSON, and keeps L10's units.

**Questions for a maintainer:**
- Item 11: where did the copy of the example come from? Record it in NOTICE (URL and date, or "supplied privately"), or ask Simpson Strong-Tie or Structural Technologies for a citable copy.
- Item 12: who checks section numbers against a licensed ACI 440.2R-17?
- Item 13: which ACI 562 and ACI 440.2 editions does Track 2 use? #6 item 1 asks the same for 440.2.

title: Research review: Track 1 tests do not pin the strengthened-section result; unsafe checker edits pass every test

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Gap. The Track 1 tests on main (`01e5182`) do not pin the strengthened-section result, never run a FAIL verdict or the exit code, and leave several branches unrun. Single checker edits that raise φMn by up to 25%, or turn a FAIL into a PASS, pass all six unit tests. After the lock update and `make certificates` that any checker change needs before CI can go green (#10), they also pass every CI step.

Extends #4 items 10 to 12 and 15, and #5 item 8.

## Where

`tests/test_track1.py`, `expected.json`, `verify.py`, `Makefile`, `src/flexure440.py`, and summary lines in the README, PROOF.md, docs/audit.md and the track file. Links point at `01e5182`; a bare L number refers to the file linked just before it.

## Evidence

Each edit is one text change to `src/flexure440.py` on a copy of `01e5182`, then the six unit tests. "Every gate" means it also passes the CI sequence in [verify.yml L28-32](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/.github/workflows/verify.yml#L28-L32) after a lock update: "RESULT: PASS", then a clean `git diff` after `make certificates`. Probe inputs change the named fields of the Track 1 input. Baseline: φ = 0.90, φMn = 481.74, Mu = 457.81 kip-ft.

### Design strength, the checker's main output

1. **No test pins the strengthened c, Mn, φ, φMn or Mu, and the force-balance test checks only what the solver drives to zero.** Extends #4 items 10 and 11.
   - [test_track1.py L48-59](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tests/test_track1.py#L48-L59) reads none of them; the only link is the threshold 481.74 ≥ 457.81 (5.2% margin). `test_force_balance` fails if the bisection stops at 12 steps, but an edit that drops a force term still balances to about 1e-13 kips.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`. Each edit passes all six tests and every gate:
     - ψf 1.0 (src L29): φMn 499.90 (+3.8%).
     - φ = 0.90 boundary at εs 0.006 (src L97): φ 0.923, above the cap.
     - Steel lever arm taken from df instead of d (src L155): φMn 535.74 (+11.2%). With `frp.tf_in` 0.02 the design check flips from FAIL (422.85 vs 457.81) to PASS.
     - Live-load factor 1.0 (src L166): Mu 382.81.
     - Design predicate `True` (src L197), with `frp.tf_in` 0.02: "PASS  Design strength, phiMn >= Mu: 422.85 vs limit 457.81", exit 0.
     - β1 dropped from compression (φMn 495.87), FRP force dropped (494.18), and α1 = β1 = 0.85 in debonding (475.68).
   - The only edit caught was a dead-load factor of 1.4 (1.4D + 1.6L, Mu 500.78).
   - The certificate embeds the checker hash (verify.py L111), so any checker change regenerates it. The only trace is a diff such as `phiMn_kipft` 481.7 → 499.9; the forced-`True` predicate changes only the hash and the date.
   - The `section_state(6.0, …)` test that #4 item 10 proposes, now in PR #7, does not close this (last section).

2. **No test runs a FAIL verdict, a printed check line or the exit code.**
   - No test calls `main()`, and `make verify` sends the CLI output to `/dev/null` (Makefile L10). The duplicated limits ([src L187-201](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L187-L201)) are #4 item 15; new here is that no test catches drift between the copies.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`. Each edit passes the tests and every gate, changes no certificate value, and turns a FAIL into a PASS:
     - fs,s predicate at 0.85 fy, with `service_moment_kipft` 362: "PASS  Service steel stress, fs,s <= 0.80 fy: 48.83 vs limit 48.00", exit 0 instead of 1.
     - ff,s predicate at 0.60 ffu, with `steel.As_in2` 0.8: "PASS … 63.17 vs limit 59.84".
     - As,min predicate `True`, with As 1.0: "PASS … 1.00 vs limit 1.12".
     - Strengthening-limit predicate `True`, with `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 2.6: "PASS … 386.62 vs limit 388.67".
     - `main()` returning 0, with As 1.0: four FAIL lines, exit 0.
     - `service_limits.fs_limit_ksi` at 0.85 fy: the JSON says 51.0 ksi, while the check uses 48.0.

3. **The crushing branch, φ below 0.90, and several input branches have no numeric test.** Extends #4 item 12.
   - The crushing test ([L80-86](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tests/test_track1.py#L80-L86)) gives φ = 0.720 and φMn = 575.8 on As 8, and asserts neither. src L100 (φ = 0.65) and src L110 (β1 above 4 ksi) never run. Every `run()` test uses 1 ply, f'c 4 ksi and an efd below the cap.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`. Each edit passes all six tests:
     - On As 8, φMn moves from 575.8 to 719.9 (+25%) with φ forced to 0.90, to 587.0 with a transition slope of 0.30, and to 558.4 with ECU 0.0035.
     - φ floor 0.70: As 14 φMn 615.1 → 662.4.
     - `plies` dropped from efd, 2 plies: φMn 468.8 → 558.3 (+19%). The unedited 2-ply case, at φ = 0.816, is untested.
     - As,min from 2.5√f'c at f'c 6: 1.30 → 1.12 in².

4. **The debonding cap is tested in the function, not in the solve, and the replay's cap entry cannot fail on Track 1.** Not in #4 or #5.
   - The cap tests ([L62-77](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tests/test_track1.py#L62-L77)) call `debonding_strain()` directly. No test runs `run()` where the cap binds.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182` with `frp.tf_in` 0.04, `concrete.fc_ksi` 8, `concrete.Ec_ksi` 5098 (formula 0.00985, cap 0.006885, φMn 476.1). Each edit passes the tests and every gate, with six PASS lines:
     - Solver fed `efd_raw` (src L153): φMn 510.7 (+7.3%). The FRP strain is 0.00985, above the 0.00765 rupture strain.
     - efu without CE (src L38): φMn 490.5.
   - The replay's cap entry ([verify.py L103-107](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L103-L107)) uses checker output, and the cap does not bind on Track 1. With `return raw, raw`, the lock updated and `make certificates` run, a unit test fails, but verify.py prints "PASS  check Debonding cap applied, efd = min(formula, 0.9 efu)" and "RESULT: PASS".
   - So the docs overstate the tests. [PROOF.md L75-78](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L75-L78): "The replay asserts the cap is applied". audit.md L7-9 calls both cap tests synthetic; one uses the Track 1 input. Track L73-74 says the tests treat the cap as a definition, yet `test_all_checks_pass` asserts the debonding row. The certificate has six `checks_pass` entries; PROOF.md L59 says five.

5. **`test_all_checks_pass` is a threshold, and certification is gated on it.** Extends #4 item 11.
   - A Mu of 382.8 or 470.3 passes.
   - verify.py will not certify a false verdict ([L132-134](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L132-L134)). Reproduced with 1.4D + 1.6L and the lock updated: "FAIL  check failed: Design strength, phiMn >= Mu", "certificate not written". See #10 item 1.

6. **The fs,s and ff,s matches hold only with the example's rounded ebi.** Extends #5 item 8. The derivation is in this review's comment on #5.
   - PR #3 tightened both tolerances in `expected.json` from 0.2 to 0.05. Reproduced on `01e5182`: with the derived ebi, 0.0012517, fs,s = 45.969 and ff,s = 9.206, both outside ± 0.05. With the printed ebi and the derived Ms, 339.84, both still match, so only ebi matters.
   - ff,s matches only for ebi in [0.0012973, 0.0013053], yet [track L14](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L14) lists ebi among inputs "as printed in the example". No wrong PASS follows.

### Smaller

7. **Printed values that would cost nothing to test are untested.** Extends #4 item 10.
   - Af, efu, 0.9 efu, the c = 6 in first pass and the 48 and 60 ksi limits ([track L37-63](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L37-L63)) are not in `expected.json`.
   - In floating point efu is 0.007649999999999999, 5.000000000000143e-05 from the printed 0.0077, so its tolerance must be just above 5e-5. These values would catch the efu-without-CE and `service_limits` edits (items 4 and 2).
   - PR #7 adds c = 6 in. efu, 0.9 efu and the 48 and 59.84 ksi limits stay unasserted there and in draft PR #15; Af is covered only indirectly (item 9).

8. **The ten-value summary does not say that none of the ten depends on the strengthened solve.** Extends #4 item 10 and #5 item 8; the wording is new.
   - [README L25](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/README.md?plain=1#L25), PROOF.md L18-27 and audit.md L5-7 omit this.
   - Reproduced: ffe = 69.937 ksi at c = 1, 3, 6, 7.49 and 8.7 in.

9. **The ten values are checked in one loop with no `subTest`** ([L48-52](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tests/test_track1.py#L48-L52)).
   - Reproduced with Af for 2 plies: five values leave tolerance, but unittest reports only `ff_service_ksi`, and `make verify` stops before verify.py, which would list all five.

10. **The k allowance is stated as fact, and it never binds.**
    - `expected.json` says the example's 0.3709 comes "from its own rounded intermediate products". The checker gives 0.370796.
    - Rounding ρs, ρf, ns and nf to 0.0119, 0.0029, 8.04 and 3.94 gives 0.370948 (0.3709). Rounding only ρs, the one intermediate the track file records, gives 0.370745 (0.3707). So the stated reason is CONJECTURE.
    - kd = k·d ([L137](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L137)), so kd's 0.005 tolerance confines k to [0.370625, 0.371042]. Reproduced: k × 1.001 passes the k check but fails kd at 8.9080.

### The same edits on the two checker pull requests

I ran the 21 edits from items 1 to 4 on both branches. PR #7 says it addresses #4 items 10 to 12.
- **Draft PR #15, stacked on PR #7 (44 tests):** a re-run of 24 single edits (these plus three others) fails a test for 15. Still passing: uncapped efd, efu without CE, `plies` dropped from efd, As,min 2.5√f'c, the As,min, fs,s, ff,s and strengthening-limit predicates, and the fs,s limit value.
- **PR #7 at `e9aa47f` (18 tests):** catches 3: the ebi sign in εc (passes on `01e5182`, c 8.66 in), φ forced to 0.90, and ECU 0.0035. It misses ψf, the lever arm, the φ boundary, the Mu factor and the forced design predicate. Its Makefile parses the CLI's JSON and ignores the exit code: Track 1 exits 1 there (fc,s fails), and `return 0` gives exit 0 with no test failing.

## What should change

Tests that need a checker change ride with that checker pull request. Tests are not locked (#5 item 1), so pins of current values could land alone.

**Draft PR #15 already** pins Track 1 c, α1, β1, Mn, φ, φMn and Mu, adds a design-strength FAIL just above φMn, hand-computed crushing, over-reinforced and two-root cases, FAIL cases for substrate strength and sustained live load, and exit-code tests. That catches every item 1 edit, item 3 except plies and As,min, and in item 2 the design predicate and the exit code.

**Still to add**, in whichever checker pull request lands:
1. A 2-ply case, and an As,min case above f'c 4.44 ksi, where 3√f'c exceeds 200 (item 3).
2. A `run()` case where the cap binds, asserting `section.efe` = 0.006885 and a hand-computed φMn (item 4).
3. FAIL cases for As,min, fs,s and ff,s that assert the line and the limit, with each limit computed once (item 2).
4. Property tests: 0.65 ≤ φ ≤ 0.90, and Mn recomputed from the forces with ψf on the FRP term only (items 1 and 3).
5. The c = 6 in state, Af, both limits, efu (0.0077, tolerance just above 5e-5) and 0.9 efu (0.0069) in `expected.json` (item 7).
6. The design verdict moved out of `ExampleMatch` into a named regression test; the always-true debonding row dropped from the asserted verdicts (items 4 and 5).
7. A replay cap entry recomputed from the input on a cap-binding case, or dropped from `checks_pass` (item 4, #10).

**Docs PR #16** labels the k reason CONJECTURE and notes that kd bounds k (item 10), states that fs,s and ff,s match given the example's ebi (item 6) and that the ten values do not depend on the strengthened solve (item 8), and corrects the cap-test wording (item 4). The check count, five in PROOF.md against six `checks_pass` entries in the certificate, is left for a maintainer (item 4).

Questions for a maintainer:
- Should the unit tests pin the strengthened values, or is the regenerated certificate meant to be the only snapshot?
- Should the checker compute ebi, or should the repo record it as the example's intermediate?

title: Research review: the checker fix for #4 cannot pass CI, and the checker lock, replay and certificate can be bypassed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Gap and failed replay, from a review of main at `01e5182`, about the verification machinery PR #3 added or extended: enforcement of the checker lock, `verify.py`, the certificate and commitment hashes, the new Makefile targets and CI. Items that extend #4, #5 or #6 say so and add only what is new.

Item 1 blocks the fix for #4 item 1. Items 2 to 6 let one pull request change what gets certified with both required checks green. Item 7 is a gap the unit tests catch today. Items 8 to 13 are lower-consequence: wrong failure messages, CI hygiene and unchecked fields.

## Where

`results/track-1-flexure/verify.py`, `Makefile`, `verify.yml`, `tests/`, `expected.json`, `commitment/`, the lock line (track file L84), and open PR #7 (head `e9aa47f`). Line links point at `01e5182`.

## Evidence

Unless an item says otherwise, each reproduction ran on a git-initialised copy of `01e5182`. "CI green" means `make verify`, `make certificates` and `git diff --exit-code -- results certificates commitment` all exit 0 on Python 3.12 (and 3.11 where stated), as in [verify.yml L24-32](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/.github/workflows/verify.yml#L24-L32). Branch protection on main (read 2026-10-25): required checks `verify (3.11)` and `verify (3.12)`, `enforce_admins` on, `require_code_owner_reviews` false, and no CODEOWNERS file.

### Blocks the fix for #4 item 1

1. **verify.py refuses to certify any check FAIL, and replay is bound to the checker hash. A correct fc,s fix therefore cannot pass required CI, and Track 1 cannot be re-certified after it.** Extends #4 item 11; the test side is #11 item 5.
   - `failures()` rejects any false check ([verify.py L132-134](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L132-L134)) on replay and on `--write`, and replay needs the certificate's checker sha256 to match. So any checker edit must move the lock and regenerate the certificates in the same pull request.
   - Reproduced: with fc,s = Ec·(fs,s/Es)·kd/(d − kd) ≤ 0.60 f'c added, the lock moved, and `test_all_checks_pass` and Makefile L10 changed to accept the FAIL, the tests pass but `make certificates` prints "FAIL check failed: Service concrete stress, fc,s <= 0.60 f'c / certificate not written". CI goes green only once L132-134 is also deleted: 10 files in one pull request, against CONTRIBUTING L12-15.
   - PR #7 is here now. `verify (3.12)` passes 18 tests, then fails at `Makefile:16` with "differs: checker / checks_pass / input" and "check failed: Service concrete stress, fc,s <= 0.45 f'c"; `verify (3.11)` was cancelled. With `enforce_admins` on, merging it needs a branch-protection change. On its head `make certificates` prints "certificate not written", so its promised result pull request would also have to edit verify.py. Draft PR #15, stacked on PR #7, hits the same gate.
   - [PROOF.md L125-126](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L125-L126) still says "The result then gets regenerated." A certificate can only record all-PASS; today's records six `true` checks under a checker that does not check fc,s.

### One pull request can change what is certified with CI green

2. **The lock hashes `src/flexure440.py`, but verify.py and the tests run whatever `import flexure440` resolves to** ([verify.py L39-41](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L39-L41)). Each of these certified φMn 499.9 kip-ft (`PSI_F` 1.00, against 481.7) with CI green on 3.11 and 3.12, while the file, the lock and the certificate's `checker.sha256` stayed `77583629…`:
   - a 3-line package `src/flexure440/__init__.py` that execs the real source with `PSI_F = 1.00`;
   - unchecked-hash `.pyc` files in `src/__pycache__/`, added with `git add -f`; they pass from a fresh clone, and `.gitignore` hides them from `git status`;
   - a `results/track-1-flexure/json.py` that patches `flexure440`, found first on `sys.path`. `python3 -I` stops this route, but not the first.

   Each shows in the diff, but nothing automated flags it, and docs/audit.md L20-24 says a pass proves the replay "with the locked checker".

3. **CI checks a pull request's merge commit only against itself, with gate code the pull request supplies.** Extends #6 item 2 and #5 item 1 (checker, lock and judge changed and re-certified with CI green; it reproduces on main, φMn 481.7 → 499.9). New here:
   - No hash covers verify.py, `tests/`, the Makefile or verify.yml. The test's `delta=spec["tol"]` → `delta=1e9` keeps CI green and ROOT unchanged. With the lock comparison ([verify.py L126](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L126)) made `elif False:`, an edited checker certifies as `7eab728a…` while the lock still reads `77583629…`.
   - The workflow and Makefile that run are the pull request's own: PR #7's job checks out `refs/remotes/pull/7/merge` and fails at "Makefile:16", a command that is at L13 in main's Makefile.
   - Mn and φMn are not in `expected.json`, so any change that keeps φMn ≥ Mu (457.8 kip-ft) is certified once the lock moves.

4. **The commitment covers four files, and ROOT is recorded nowhere else.** Extends #6 item 2. [commitment/SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/commitment/SHA256SUMS) lists the checker, `input.json`, `expected.json` and the certificate, not verify.py, `tests/`, the Makefile, verify.yml or the track file that holds the lock. `make verify-hashes` passed in every case of items 2, 3, 5 and 6. docs/status.md L22-24 calls these "commitment hashes"; they show that the tree agrees with itself.

5. **The printed-value set has no floor.** Extends #5 item 1, which covers tolerances. [tests L48-52](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tests/test_track1.py#L48-L52) and verify.py L97 loop over whatever `expected.json` holds; at `04012d4` a missing key raised `KeyError`. With `"values": {}` and `make certificates`, CI is green: "Ran 6 tests ... OK", "RESULT: PASS", `printed_match` `{}`. #5 item 1's tolerance case also reproduces on main (efd 0.005637 vs printed 0.0049 passes at tol 0.001).

6. **verify.py takes the lock from the first `sha256: <hex>` anywhere in the track file** ([L57](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L57)). With `PSI_F` 1.00, `<!-- sha256: 7eab728a… -->` added as line 2 and `make certificates`, CI is green; the rendered Checker section still shows `77583629…`.

### A gap the unit tests catch today

7. **`make certificates` runs no tests and no equilibrium check.** [Makefile L21-26](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/Makefile#L21-L26) runs `verify.py --write`, then copies and hashes; `failures()` never reads `balance_kips`, and in debonding mode no printed value depends on c. Bisection `range(200)` → `range(4)`, relocked, is written with balance −13.91 kips and φMn 484.6; input `beam.h_in` 7.5 with balance −21.25 kips. Replay prints "RESULT: PASS" for both. In CI `test_force_balance` fails first, so this is defence in depth, but docs/audit.md L24-25 ("A failing result cannot be certified") holds only for what `failures()` checks.

### Lower consequence: wrong messages, CI hygiene, unchecked fields

8. **No `.gitattributes`, so a Windows checkout of unmodified main fails the lock with tamper messages.** In a `git -c core.autocrlf=true clone` (the Git for Windows default), `src/flexure440.py` hashes to `f7fb8a3c…`, verify.py prints "checker differs from the hash locked in the track file", and `make verify` exits 2; at `04012d4` it passed. Docs PR #16's `.gitattributes` fixes it (reproduced). Not tested: [verify.py L153](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L153) writes without `newline`, so Windows would write a CRLF certificate. The BOM crash is #8 item 8.

9. **The 3.11 job passes with no tests, and verify.yml pins none of its settings.** With `tests/test_track1.py` renamed to `tests/track1_checks.py`, 3.11 gives "Ran 0 tests ... OK" and CI green; 3.12 exits 5 ("NO TESTS RAN"), so only that job blocks it, and nothing asserts the six tests the track file states. There is no `permissions:` block: PR #7's log (a same-repo branch) shows Contents, Metadata and Packages read, so the default is read-only but not pinned. The matrix ([L18](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/.github/workflows/verify.yml#L18)) has no 3.13 and no `fail-fast: false`, so PR #7's 3.11 job was cancelled.

10. **verify.py's argument and error handling.** Only the exact `--write` is checked ([L139](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L139)), so `--wirte` runs a replay. Bad files end in tracebacks with exit 1, the FAIL code, and the `JSONDecodeError` names no file. `--write` loads the old certificate first, so a corrupt one, or one with no `date`, blocks regeneration until deleted by hand.

11. **The certificate date is copied, never checked** ([L160](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/verify.py#L160)). With `1999-01-01`, or `null`, in both copies, `make certificates` keeps it and CI is green. New dates come from local-time `date.today()`. No number depends on it.

12. **The checker's own output names neither the checker nor the input** ([src/flexure440.py L210-213](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L210-L213)), and there are no tags. This matters for the output CONTRIBUTING L16-17 asks result pull requests to paste. Output format in general is #14.

13. **The Makefile hard-codes `python3`, and no doc states a supported Python.** `make -n verify PYTHON=python3.11` still prints `python3`; only [docs/status.md L18-19](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/docs/status.md?plain=1#L18-L19) implies 3.11 and 3.12.

## What should change

### First, a decision on item 1

- **Which pull request moves the lock and the certificate?** (a) The checker pull request, reviewed as checker acceptance; CONTRIBUTING L12-15, verify.py L14-18 and #4's plan, which disagree today, then say so. Today's CI can only go green this way, and for the fc,s fix only with the next change. (b) A separate result pull request, as #4 plans, after CI gains a mode that checks a checker pull request against the base branch's certificate.
- **Can a certificate record a FAIL?** It must, or Track 1 cannot be re-certified after the fc,s check lands. A suggestion: certify on replay, lock and printed-value match, and record each verdict as data, checked against a reviewed expected-verdicts file that includes the fc,s FAIL.

Until then, PROOF.md L125-126 should not promise a regeneration the code refuses.

### Close the bypasses (items 2 to 7)

- **Item 2.** Check the hash of `src/flexure440.py`, then `compile()` and `exec()` those bytes into a fresh module under `python3 -I`. Fail CI if `git ls-files src` lists anything else.
- **Items 3 and 4.** Add a guard the pull request cannot edit: CODEOWNERS on `src/`, `tests/`, `tracks/`, `results/*/verify.py`, `Makefile` and `.github/` with code-owner review required (the standard's org ruleset does not require it), or a required org-ruleset workflow that fails on lock, judge, input or gate-code changes against `origin/main` without a maintainer label. Then anchor the commitment (#6 item 2) or call it internal consistency only. CONTRIBUTING wording is in #13.
- **Item 5.** Assert the exact set of ten keys, and bound each `tol` by half the printed precision, with `k` excepted by name.
- **Item 6.** Read the lock only from the `## Checker` section, and fail on a second `sha256:`.
- **Item 7.** Make `certificates` depend on `verify-fast`, and check and record `balance_kips` when writing.

### Lower-consequence fixes (items 8 to 13)

- **Item 8.** `.gitattributes` (docs PR #16), and `newline="\n"` at verify.py L153.
- **Item 9.** Assert the test count. Add `permissions: contents: read`, `fail-fast: false` and 3.13, and state the supported versions in the README.
- **Item 10.** Use `argparse`, name the bad file and exit 2, and let `--write` rebuild an unparseable certificate.
- **Item 11.** Validate the date as ISO 8601 in UTC, or take it from the commit.
- **Item 12.** Print the checker and input sha256 and the Python version, and tag locked checker commits.
- **Item 13.** Add `PYTHON ?= python3`.

Questions for a maintainer:
- Item 1: (a) or (b)? May a certificate record a FAIL? Should PR #7 merge through a one-off branch-protection change, or wait for a verify.py that allows a FAIL?
- Items 3 and 4: should the split between checker, judge and result be enforced by people (CODEOWNERS) or by a CI rule?

title: Research review: Track 1 result (merged PR #3): ACI 562-16 Section 5.5.2 misstated as 1.2D + 0.5L; the example's citation is correct

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Error and wrong label. PR #3, following fdn-0's review comment, which repeats #4 item 6, added a false statement of what ACI 562-16 Section 5.5.2 says and, in the track file, filed it under KNOWN. The citation it replaced was correct. Also a missing source entry and a wrong term in the checker docstring.

## Where

- `results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md` L69-73 and `tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md` L51-54, added by PR #3 (commits `3f980ed` and `9a618c9`).
- `NOTICE` and `CONTRIBUTORS.md`, unchanged since the seed.
- `src/flexure440.py` L6-7 and L19-20, hash-locked and byte-identical to `04012d4` (sha256 `77583629…a81d872`).
- #4 item 6, #5 item 6, and open PR #7, which carries #4 item 6 into the checker docstring and NOTICE.

Line links point at `01e5182` unless marked.

## Evidence

Sources:

- **ACI 562-16 provisional text**, ACI's [562-16_Provisional.pdf](https://www.concrete.org/Portals/0/Files/PDF/562-16_Provisional.pdf), "An ACI Provisional Standard", PDF created January 2016. Printed pp. 44-45 are PDF pp. 46-47.
- **ACI webinar slides** (Alkhrdaji; webinar 2017-04-17 per the file name, PDF created April 2016), the deck #4 item 6 links: [ws_2017_0417_Alkhrdaji_DSREARS.pdf](https://concrete.org/portals/0/files/pdf/webinars/ws_2017_0417_Alkhrdaji_DSREARS.pdf). The cited slides carry no printed numbers, so PDF page numbers are given.
- **Simpson Strong-Tie SE University handout**, "Design Methodology and Calculations using Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Systems" (Jarvinen, 12 July 2021; no public URL found), PDF pp. 7-8.

Moments use the Track 1 inputs: wDL = 2.75 k/ft, wLL = 1.60 k/ft, L = 25 ft, M = w·L²/8.

### Wrong statement of ACI 562-16

1. **PROOF.md and the track file say ACI 562-16 Section 5.5.2 is 1.2D + 0.5L. Section 5.5.2 contains 1.1D + 0.75L, which is what the example computes.**
   - [PROOF.md L71-73](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L71-L73): "The example text cites ACI 562-16, Section 5.5.2 for the check. That section's own combination is different: 1.2 dead + 0.5 live gives 320.3 kip-ft here, not the printed 330."
   - [Track file L51-54](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L51-L54) says the same under "KNOWN, from the example." ([L45](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L45)). The sentence is not from the example and names no source; [CONTRIBUTING L28](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L28): "KNOWN: cited to a source. Name the source."
   - ACI's material gives Section 5.5.2 in two forms. In both, 1.1D + 0.75L is in 5.5.2 and 1.2D + 0.5L is the 5.5.3 extraordinary-event case:
     - Provisional text, pp. 44-45: "The required strength of the structure without external reinforcement shall satisfy Eq. (5.5.2)", φRn ≥ 1.1D + 0.75L + 0.2S. Section 5.5.2.1 raises the live load factor "from 0.75 to 1.0" for sustained live load. Section 5.5.3, "after an extraordinary event", is φex·Rex ≥ 1.2D + 0.5L + 0.2S, and 5.5.3C names "fire, impact, or blast".
     - Slides, PDF p. 10, headed "ACI 562-16 (revision)": "φRn ≥ 1.1D + 0.5L + 0.2S (5.5.2a)" and "φRn ≥ 1.1D + 0.75L (5.5.2b)", noting "Equation (5.5.2b) is similar to limit in ACI 440.2R-08 (FRP)". PDF p. 12 gives 5.5.3, for a fire event, as "(0.9 or 1.2)D + 0.5L + 0.2S" with φex = 1.0.
     - Simpson's handout matches the slides: "ACI 562-16 Eq. 5.5.2b: (ΦRn)existing ≥ (1.1D + 0.75L)new (ACI 440.2R-17 Eq. 9.2)" (PDF p. 7), and gives 5.5.3 as "(0.9 or 1.2)D + 0.5L + 0.2S" (PDF p. 8).
     - The two-equation form comes from the later documents, so the published code probably uses it. The published ACI 562-16 has not been read here.
   - Calculation: 1.1D + 0.75L = **330.08 k-ft**, the example's printed 330. That is Section 5.5.2 with S = 0 in either form, and ACI 440.2R-17 Eq. (9.2). 1.2D + 0.5L = 320.31 k-ft. Reproduced on `01e5182`: `PASS  Strengthening limit, phiMn existing >= 1.1DL + 0.75LL moment: 386.62 vs limit 330.08`. No checker number or verdict depends on the false sentence.
   - Consequence: a reader who takes 1.2D + 0.5L as the Section 5.5.2 limit gets a lower demand whenever L/D > 0.4. It is 3.0% low on this beam (L/D = 0.58), 8.1% low at L/D = 1.0 and 15.4% low at L/D = 2.0, and it drops the 0.2S term and the 5.5.2.1 factor. The text also tells the public that a published example mis-cites the code, which it does not.
   - History: at `04012d4` the track file read "Strengthening limit, in the form the example uses (ACI 562-16, Section 5.5.2)" ([L49-51 at 04012d4](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L49-L51)), which was right. The re-review on PROOF.md L67 ([comment](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/3#discussion_r4371405609)) identified the slide as ACI 562-13 Eq. 5.5.1, but still called it "ACI 562's combination". It suggested adding "to be checked against the 562-16 text" as "optional tightening, not blocking", and PR #3 merged two minutes later without it.
   - The Eq. (9.2) citations PR #3 added are correct and should stay: [PROOF.md L67](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L67), [docs/audit.md L34-36](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/docs/audit.md?plain=1#L34-L36), [tracks/README.md L11](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/README.md?plain=1#L11).

2. **#4 item 6 takes the ACI 562-13 extraordinary-event combination as ACI 562's strengthening limit (corrects #4 item 6).**
   - #4 item 6: "ACI's own published material gives ACI 562's form as 1.2D + 0.5L + 0.2S (+Ak)", linking the slides. There that equation is on PDF p. 6, headed "ACI 562-13": "Uex ≥ 1.2D + 0.5L + Ak + 0.2S (5.5.1)". PDF p. 7 gives its purpose as failure of the repair system from "Fire, impact, or blast".
   - The PR #3 re-review already named it ACI 562-13 Eq. 5.5.1 (item 1). What is new: the same deck's ACI 562-16 slide, PDF p. 10, puts 1.1D + 0.75L in Section 5.5.2, and #4 item 6 has not been amended.
   - #4 item 6 points the fix toward removing the citation (suggested order, step 2: "Fix the citation once the publisher copy is read"). The confirmation it asks for, against the 562-16 text, shows the citation is right, so the item should be amended before a checker pull request acts on it.
   - Open PR #7 has already acted on it. At `e9aa47f`, its `src/flexure440.py` L8-9 reads "The example text cites ACI 562-16, Section 5.5.2 for that check. That section's own combination is different. See NOTICE." Its `NOTICE` L21-22 adds "ACI 562's own combination is different (1.2 dead + 0.5 live, from ACI's published webinar material)". Merged, that puts the error into the hash-locked checker.
   - #5 item 6 relays #4's suggestion that the right citation "may be ACI 440.2R-17 Eq. 9.2". Eq. (9.2) is also correct, but as an added citation, not as a replacement for a wrong one.

### Checker wording

3. **The docstring calls the strengthening limit a "load test".** [src/flexure440.py L19-20](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L19-L20): "No shear, no anchorage design, no deflection, no fire design. / The strengthening limit check is the load test of Section 5.5.2 form."
   - [L165](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L165) computes the demand and [L195-196](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L195-L196) compare existing φMn with it: a required-strength comparison, with nothing tested. Indented under "no fire design", the sentence also reads as a scope limit.
   - In the provisional text, Section 5.5 is "Additional load combinations for structures rehabilitated with external reinforcing systems" (p. 44). Load testing is Section 6.8, "Strength evaluation by load testing" (p. 59), which refers to ACI 437.2-13.
   - [L6-7](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L6-L7) credit "existing strength" to the same 562 form, but `existing_strength()` ([L104-117](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L104-L117)) is "Plain reinforced concrete strength, Whitney block, no FRP", an ACI 318 calculation.
   - Not tracked in #4 or #5. Other docstring lines are in #12 item 16.

### Sources and credit

4. **NOTICE still has no ACI 562-16 entry after PR #3 added a third citation, and CONTRIBUTORS credits neither ACI 318 nor ACI 562 (extends #5 item 6).**
   - PR #3 added [PROOF.md L71](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L71) to the existing citations at [src L7](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L7) and [track file L51](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L51). Reproduced on `01e5182`: `grep -n 562 NOTICE` prints nothing. The rule it breaks is quoted in #5 item 6.
   - [CONTRIBUTORS L25-27](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/CONTRIBUTORS.md?plain=1#L25-L27) credits only ACI Committee 440 and Simpson Strong-Tie. ACI 318, which [NOTICE L19](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/NOTICE#L19) lists, has no credit either.
   - The unstated ACI 318 edition and the uncited 1.2D + 1.6L demand are in #12 items 15 and 4.

## What should change

- **Items 1 and 4: docs PR #16** corrects the track file, PROOF.md, NOTICE and CONTRIBUTORS:
  - The example's Section 5.5.2 citation is consistent: 1.1D + 0.75L is in Section 5.5.2 and, with S = 0, equals ACI 440.2R-17 Eq. (9.2). 1.2D + 0.5L + 0.2S is the Section 5.5.3 extraordinary-event case (ACI 562-13 Eq. 5.5.1).
  - Each equation form is labelled by its source (the provisional text, or ACI's slides and Simpson's handout); neither is stated as the published code.
  - The statement leaves "KNOWN, from the example" and names its sources, and the earlier error goes under failed attempts.
  - NOTICE gets an ACI 562-16 entry, and CONTRIBUTORS the ACI 318 and ACI 562 credits.
- **Item 3:** the docstring is hash-locked, so the fix waits for a checker pull request. PR #7's docstring already drops the "load test" sentence and cites Eq. (9.2), but adds the 1.2D + 0.5L statement quoted in item 2. Draft PR #15, stacked on PR #7, corrects that statement in the docstring, NOTICE and track file, attributing each ACI 562-16 form to its source, adds the Section 5.5.2.1 factor of 1.0 as an input (`loads.live_load_sustained`), and states S = 0.
- **Item 2:** a maintainer should amend #4 item 6 and step 2 of its suggested order. PR #7 should drop the docstring and NOTICE text quoted above before it merges; draft PR #15 does so. On #5 item 6, the NOTICE gap stands, but the 562-16 citation is correct.
- The citation fix does not make the check complete. On `01e5182`, Section 5.5.2.1 is not modelled (1.1D + 1.0L = 361.33 k-ft on this beam, still under 386.62); see #8 item 2.
- Question for a maintainer: confirm against the published ACI 562-16 which form Section 5.5.2 takes. It is either one Eq. (5.5.2), 1.1D + 0.75L + 0.2S, as in the provisional text, or Eq. (5.5.2a) 1.1D + 0.5L + 0.2S with Eq. (5.5.2b) 1.1D + 0.75L, as in ACI's slides and Simpson's handout. Also confirm whether Eq. (5.5.3) reads 1.2D or (0.9 or 1.2)D. Either way the example's citation holds.

title: Research review: checker defects not tracked in #4 to #6, four of which can pass a non-compliant design

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Error and gap, from a review of main at `01e5182`. None of these is in #4, #5 or #6 unless an item says it extends one. In items 1 to 4 the checker prints six PASS lines and exits 0 for a beam that should not pass.

## Where

`src/flexure440.py` at `01e5182` (byte-identical to `04012d4`, sha256 `77583629…`), and disclosure lines in `results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md`, `docs/audit.md` and `tracks/README.md`.

## Evidence

Each reproduction was run on `01e5182` with `python3 src/flexure440.py <input>`, on a copy of `tracks/track-1/input.json` with the listed fields changed. Where an item sets `ebi`, it is the cracked-section soffit strain under that item's dead load, and `service_moment_kipft` is (wDL + wLL_new)·L²/8, as in Track 1.

#4 items 1 to 4 and 7 are not repeated. What this review adds to them is in a separate comment on #4 posted with this issue.

### Can print PASS and exit 0 for a design that should fail

1. **The ACI 440.2R-17 §1.2.1.4 substrate limits are not checked.** f'c is never compared with a floor, and there is no input for pull-off strength or substrate condition. The scope ([L16-21](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L16-L21)) and the docs on main mention neither.
   - §1.2.1.4: FRP "should not be used when the concrete substrate has a compressive strength fc′ less than 2500 psi", and for bond-critical work pull-off strength "should be at least 200 psi" ([ACI's 440.2R-17 preview](https://www.concrete.org/Portals/0/Files/PDF/Previews/440.2R-17_preview.pdf), pp. 5-6).
   - Reproduced on `01e5182` with `beam.b_in` 18, `concrete.fc_ksi` 2.0, `concrete.Ec_ksi` 2549.1 (57√f'c), `steel.As_in2` 1.5, `frp.tf_in` 0.04, `frp.wf_in` 16, `loads.wDL_kipft` 0.6, `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 0.8, `service_moment_kipft` 109.375, `ebi` 0.00068: six PASS, exit 0, φMn 215.55 vs Mu 156.25. The FRP is needed: existing φMn is 152.07.
   - fc,s is 1.13 ksi, within the -17 limit 0.60 f'c = 1.20 ksi, so the PASS stands once #4 item 1 is fixed at 0.60 f'c. PR #7 codes 0.45 f'c and FAILs this beam on concrete stress (1.13 vs 0.90), which is not the check this item asks for.

2. **The strengthening limit has no 1.0 live-load factor for sustained live load.** [L165](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L165) always uses (1.1 wDL + 0.75 wLL)·L²/8.
   - ACI 562-16 §5.5.2.1, under the §5.5.2 the docstring cites, says: "If the applied live load has a high likelihood of being sustained the live load factor in Eq. 5.5.2 shall be increased from 0.75 to 1.0." §5.5.2.1C names library stacks, heavy storage, warehouses and live loads over 100 lb/ft² ([provisional text](https://concrete.org/Portals/0/Files/PDF/562-16_Provisional.pdf), p. 45).
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`, for a beam whose 2.4 k/ft live load is storage or library stacks: `beam.b_in` 16, `steel.As_in2` 1.5, `frp.plies` 3, `span_ft` 20, `loads.wDL_kipft` 1.2, `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 2.4, `service_moment_kipft` 180, `ebi` 0.000864. Six PASS, exit 0, the strengthening limit at 156.42 vs 156.00. With the 1.0 factor the demand is (1.1 × 1.2 + 1.0 × 2.4) × 20²/8 = 186.0 kip-ft; the existing beam is 16% short.
   - fc,s is 2.24 ksi, within 0.60 f'c = 2.40 ksi. PR #7's 0.45 f'c FAILs it on concrete stress instead (2.24 vs 1.80).
   - Track 1 is not affected: (1.1 × 2.75 + 1.0 × 1.6) × 25²/8 = 361.3 < 386.6 kip-ft. Eq. (5.5.2) also has + 0.2S; the checker takes no snow and does not state S = 0, which matters for roofs.
   - [tracks/README L11](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/tracks/README.md?plain=1#L11) says Track 1 "already carries" the Eq. (9.2) check, true for the 0.75 factor only.
   - #4 item 6 covers only the citation. The equation it quotes is ACI 562-13 Eq. (5.5.1), whose 562-16 counterpart is the §5.5.3 extraordinary-event case, not §5.5.2; see #9.

3. **Inputs are not validated, and a crash exits 1, like a FAIL.** This extends #6 item 3 (zero or negative values, `plies: 0`).
   - Base: Track 1 with `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 1.795 and `service_moment_kipft` 355.08, which exits 1 on "FAIL Design strength, phiMn >= Mu: 481.74 vs limit 482.19". Reproduced on `01e5182`, each single change below gives six PASS and exit 0:
     - `frp.wf_in` 16, wider than b = 14 (φMn 510.52);
     - `frp.tf_in` 2.03 or `frp.wf_in` 305, thickness or width entered in mm (φMn 547.67, 591.18);
     - `span_ft` 0, with service moment and `ebi` 0 (both demands 0.00);
     - `loads.wLL_new_kipft` −1.795 with `service_moment_kipft` 74.61 (Mu 33.44).
   - `frp.CE` 1.2, above the 0.95 maximum of ACI 440.2R-17 Table 9.4, is accepted (FRP service limit 84.48 ksi); `Infinity` prints "vs limit inf" and writes `"ffu_ksi": Infinity`.
   - `steel.As_in2` 0 (ZeroDivisionError, [L113](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L113)), `concrete.fc_ksi` −4 (math domain error) and a missing `ebi` (KeyError) crash with a traceback, no check lines and exit 1. [L213](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L213) also returns 1 for a FAIL, so a script cannot tell "the beam fails" from "the checker did not run".
   - The docstring's "full width factor taken from input" ([L18](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L18)) names no real input.

4. **A duplicate key silently takes its last value, which can turn a FAIL into a PASS.** [L207-208](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L207-L208) use plain `json.load`, with no schema.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182`: in the Track 1 input, `"As_in2":2.0,"As_in2":4.0` gives six PASS and exit 0; the reverse order exits 1 with three FAILs (204.66 < 330.08, 304.81 < 457.81, 79.33 > 48.00).
   - `"plies": true` runs as 1 ply (exit 0). An unknown key such as `"fiber": "glass"` draws no warning (the fiber limit itself is #4 item 9). The JSON does not echo the inputs, so a reader cannot see which value won.

### Wrong, undeclared or unclear, with no false PASS shown

5. **Crack width is neither checked nor declared out of scope.** The scope at [L19](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L19) excludes deflection by name, not crack width. The checker reads no cover or bar spacing and never uses the input's `steel.bars` text ("4 No. 9"). [PROOF.md L64](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/results/track-1-flexure/PROOF.md?plain=1#L64) labels the steel check "Section 10.2.8, steel limit only".
   - ACI 440.2R-17 §10.2.8 refers serviceability (deflections and crack widths) to ACI 318. That text is not in the public preview: **confirm** it against the publisher copy. Simpson Strong-Tie's SE University handout "Design Methodology and Calculations using Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Systems" (July 12, 2021, slide 23; no working public link found) says "Check ACI 318 serviceability requirements (deflections and crack widths)".
   - Calculation, ACI 318-14 Table 24.3.2 with cc = 3.0 − 1.128/2 = 2.44 in: the checker's fs,s = 46.13 ksi gives s ≤ 6.92 in; fs = 2/3 fy = 40 ksi (§24.3.2.1) gives 8.91 in. Track 1 passes either way if its four bars are in one layer, about 2.7 in apart (no input gives spacing). Bars about 6.9 to 8.9 in apart pass with the 2/3 fy shortcut and fail with the checker's own stress, and nothing says the check was skipped, against [CONTRIBUTING L40](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L40): "Engineering limits stay visible."

6. **At low f'c the force balance can have several roots, and the solver has no rule for which one it returns.** This extends #4 item 4 (no root).
   - [L72-73](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L72-L73) give α1β1 = r − r²/3 (r = εc/ε'c, ε'c = 1.7 f'c/Ec), which peaks at r = 1.5. With Ec = 57√f'c, that peak comes before εc = 0.003 when f'c is below about 4.5 ksi, so compression can fall as c grows.
   - Reproduced on `01e5182` with `beam.b_in` 22.3, `beam.d_in` 22.9, `beam.df_in` = `beam.h_in` = 25.3, `concrete.fc_ksi` 2.6, `concrete.Ec_ksi` 2907, `steel.As_in2` 5.79, `frp.plies` 3, `frp.wf_in` 22.3, `loads.wDL_kipft` 1.47, `service_moment_kipft` 239.84, `ebi` 0.00048. Scanning `section_state` finds roots at c = 12.22 in (debonding, φMn 501.1 kip-ft), 12.90 (debonding, 479.0) and 13.24 (crushing, 463.0). `run()` returns 12.22 with six PASS (Mu 337.81) and no warning. That root, the first limit state reached, is defensible, but the bisection ([L84-93](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L84-L93)) returns whichever sign change the halving lands on. With Track 1's dead load (`ebi` 0.000895) the same section has one root; `ebi` is a free input, see #14.
   - Below about 2.53 ksi the block gives β1 > 1 (Track 1 at f'c 2.0, Ec 2549.1: β1 = 1.166). Track 1 at f'c 1.0 with Ec 1802.5 (57√f'c) pins the solver to c = 25.65 in, 30.9 kips out of balance, φMn −104.5 kip-ft (the #4 item 4 case). Both are below the item 1 floor.

7. **The minimum-steel check applies the ACI 318 beam minimum to any rectangle.** [L168-170](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L168-L170) compute max(3√f'c, 200)·b·d/fy (ACI 318-14 §9.6.1.2). Reproduced on `01e5182` with a slab strip, `beam.b_in` 12, `beam.d_in` 6.75, `beam.df_in` = `beam.h_in` = 8, `steel.As_in2` 0.20 (No. 4 at 12 in), `frp.wf_in` 4, `span_ft` 14, `loads.wDL_kipft` 0.10, `loads.wLL_new_kipft` 0.15, `service_moment_kipft` 6.125, `ebi` 0.00098: "FAIL Minimum steel, As >= As,min: 0.20 vs limit 0.27", exit 1, all else PASS. The Table 7.6.1.1 slab minimum is 0.0018 × 12 × 8 = 0.17 in². A conservative false FAIL, and the line does not say it is the example's beam minimum.

8. **A BOM or UTF-16 input crashes the checker.** The same `open` ([L207](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L207)) reads strict UTF-8. Reproduced on `01e5182`: the Track 1 input with a UTF-8 BOM gives `JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM`, and as UTF-16 gives `UnicodeDecodeError`; both exit 1 with no check lines. Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes UTF-16LE on `>` and UTF-8 with a BOM on `-Encoding utf8`. `encoding="utf-8-sig"` reads the BOM file.

## What should change

The checker is hash-locked, so as #4 sets out, these go in a checker pull request with no result in it.

- **Draft PR #15, stacked on PR #7,** adds items 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8, the duplicate-key and JSON-boolean part of item 4, and crack width in the scope list (item 5), with tests. Choices for a maintainer to confirm:
  - Item 1: f'c below 2500 psi FAILs; pull-off prints NOT CHECKED unless `substrate.pull_off_psi` is given; substrate condition always prints NOT CHECKED.
  - Item 2: a `loads.live_load_sustained` flag selects the 1.0 factor, and the scope states S = 0.
  - Item 6: with several roots it takes the lowest φMn and prints a NOTE, not the smallest-c root.
- **Still open after it:** a plausibility bound on `tf_in` (the mm value is positive); a warning on unknown keys outside `loads` and `substrate`; an input echo in the JSON (item 4); item 7.
- **Open PR #7**, the checker pull request for #4, on its own covers none of items 1, 2 or 6. It keeps `(1.1 * wdl + 0.75 * wll)`, never compares f'c with 2.5 ksi, and keeps one bisection with no second-root search. Beyond solver guards it checks only fiber type and support condition. Its 0.45 f'c limit (the 2008 value) FAILs the item 1 and 2 beams on concrete stress, which is not what those items test.
- **Tests:** each reproduction can become a test that fails on `01e5182`; see #11.
- **Docs, until a checker change lands** (see #12): `docs/audit.md` "Known weak points" ([L47](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/docs/audit.md?plain=1#L47)) and the PROOF.md Scope should name items 1, 2 and 5. tracks/README L11 should say Track 1 carries Eq. (9.2) with the 0.75 factor only, not the 1.0 factor for sustained live load.

Questions for a maintainer:
- Item 1: keep pull-off optional (NOT CHECKED when absent), or require it?
- Item 2: keep the sustained flag and S = 0, or add a snow load?
- Item 6: keep the lowest φMn, or take the smallest c?
- Item 7: beams only, or a member-type input with the slab minimum?

title: Research review: ACI 440.2R-17 superseded, commitment root not anchored, no input validation

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Gap and missing prior art. These are findings from a review of main at `01e5182`. They are not already in #4 or #5. Line links point at `01e5182`.

## Where

`README.md`, `NOTICE`, the `Makefile` `certificates` target, `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, and `src/flexure440.py`.

## Evidence

### 1. ACI 440.2R-17 has been superseded

ACI's preview of **ACI PRC-440.2-23** says it supersedes ACI 440.2R-17. It was first printed in November 2023. [Preview PDF, concrete.org](https://www.concrete.org/Portals/0/Files/PDF/Previews/440.2-23_preview.pdf)

[README L15](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/README.md?plain=1#L15) and NOTICE name the 2017 edition. They do not say it is no longer current.

Track 1 should stay on -17, because the Simpson Strong-Tie example follows -17. But a reader, or a Track 2 agent, would assume -17 is the current guide.

I have **not** checked what changed between -17 and -23. The service concrete stress limit (#4 item 1) and the Section 9.2 strengthening limits that Track 2 depends on are the places to look first. That comparison is CONJECTURE until someone reads both texts.

### 2. The commitment ROOT only detects drift inside the repo

The [`certificates` target (Makefile L21-26)](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/Makefile#L21-L26) regenerates:
- the certificate,
- `certificates/SHA256SUMS`,
- `commitment/SHA256SUMS`,
- `commitment/ROOT`.

All four come from whatever is in the working tree. So a pull request that changes the checker can run `make certificates`, edit the hash in the track file, and commit everything, and `make verify` stays green. CI only checks that the committed files are consistent with each other ([verify.yml L32](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/.github/workflows/verify.yml#L32)).

CONTRIBUTING's rule that a checker change never shares a pull request with a result is enforced by review alone. This is related to #5 item 1, which is about the test set rather than the checker/result split.

### 3. Inputs are not validated, and `plies: 0` crashes

Setting `frp.plies` to 0 raises `ZeroDivisionError` in the debonding strain formula ([L48](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/01e5182/src/flexure440.py#L48)). So the checker cannot be run on the unstrengthened beam as a baseline.

Other zero or negative values (`tf_in`, `Ec_ksi`, `df_in <= d_in`) are not checked either.

Reproduce:

```
python3 -c "import json,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); import flexure440 as f; i=json.load(open('tracks/track-1/input.json')); i['frp']['plies']=0; f.run(i)"
```

## What should change

1. Add one line to README and NOTICE: ACI PRC-440.2-23 supersedes 440.2R-17, and Track 1 stays on -17 because its example does. A maintainer should decide which edition Track 2 uses before it opens.
2. Decide what the commitment is meant to prove. Then:
   - Add a CI step that fails when a pull request diff touches both `src/` and `results/` (or `certificates/` or `commitment/`). For example, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`.
   - If ROOT should be a real commitment, anchor it outside the repo, for example in a signed tag on the merge commit.
   - Otherwise, describe it in `docs/audit.md` as internal drift detection only.
3. In the checker pull request from #4, validate inputs: raise a clear error for zero or negative dimensions, moduli and areas. Either allow `plies: 0` to mean "unstrengthened" or reject it with a message.

title: Research review: seed scaffold (merged PR #1): lock scope, contradictory rules, unsupported citations

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Gap, wrong label and missing prior art. This is a retroactive review of [PR #1](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/1), which merged without review.

## Where

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `NOTICE`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `tracks/README.md`, `tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md` and `docs/status.md`. Line links point at `04012d4`. Each line cited was written in PR #1 and is still on main. Text that PR #2 later rewrote is left out.

## Evidence

I recomputed every recorded Simpson Strong-Tie value from the recorded inputs, and they agree within the example's rounding. The FRP properties match Simpson's CSS-CUCF44 datasheet. The problems are in the rules and the citations, not the arithmetic.

### Process rules

1. **The lock covers only the checker, not the test set.** See [CONTRIBUTING L12-13](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L12-L13). The printed values, `input.json`, `expected.json` and its tolerances are not locked, and the agent prompt lets result PRs edit inputs.
   - PR #3 now enforces the checker hash and records `expected.json` in `commitment/SHA256SUMS`.
   - A result PR can still change the judge, though. PR #3 itself edits `expected.json` and the tests, in good faith, to tighten tolerances. The same path lets a later PR loosen a tolerance or change a printed value so that a wrong output "matches".
2. **The checker/result split is circular.** See [CONTRIBUTING L12](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L12). A checker is a valid judge only after it matches the printed example, and that match is itself a VERIFIED result, which a checker PR may not carry. "Result" is never defined. PR #2 shipped ten printed-value matches in the checker PR, and the README then said both "matches the worked example" and "no result is recorded yet".
3. **The agent prompt forbids writing a checker.** See [CONTRIBUTING L52](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L52): "Work only on inputs, notes, or result files." The prompt gives no path for a track that has no checker yet, which applies to Tracks 2 to 4 now. The PR #2 agent had to set this rule aside.
4. **PROVEN overlaps VERIFIED.** See [CONTRIBUTING L24](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L24): "a written proof or a full derivation from stated inputs". Any checker run on an input file fits that definition, which contradicts L27 ("A finite check is not a proof") and the Foundation-0 standard.

### Citations and claims

5. **NOTICE claims citations that don't exist.** [NOTICE L36](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/NOTICE#L36) says printed numbers are recorded "with the page they came from", but none has a page, and page citations are still an open obligation. [L16](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/NOTICE#L16) says guide numbers are cited to their section, but CE = 0.85, the 0.9 efu cap, 0.80 fy, 0.55 ffu and 0.083 carry no section reference.
6. **NOTICE is incomplete.** [L3](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/NOTICE#L3) says it lists "every outside source the work depends on", and [L44](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/NOTICE#L44) says new sources are added before the code that uses them. ACI 562-16 is cited in the checker and the track file but has no entry. #4 item 6 suggests the right citation there may be ACI 440.2R-17 Eq. 9.2.
7. **The test-set source can't be found.** [NOTICE L39](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/NOTICE#L39) says "cite it, link to the publisher", but no URL, document number or product name appears anywhere. Simpson publishes more than one FRP flexure example, so a reviewer can't fetch the "publisher copy" that every open obligation depends on.
8. **Derived values are recorded as inputs.** See [track file L23](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L23). ebi = 0.0013 comes from the dead-load moment and the cracked section; recomputing from MDL = 215 k-ft gives 0.00125, which the checker never reproduces because ebi is an input. ffu = 108.8 is just 0.85 × 128, yet it counts as one of the ten VERIFIED matches, which overstates the evidence.
9. **The stress-block rules are credited to ACI 318.** See [README L15](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/README.md?plain=1#L15) and NOTICE L24-25. In the debonding mode that governs Track 1, α1 and β1 come from ACI 440.2R-17 itself. The ACI 318 Whitney block applies only to the crushing case and the unstrengthened section, which is also what the checker does.
10. **Track 4 is outside ACI 440.2R.** See [tracks/README L13](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/tracks/README.md?plain=1#L13). ACI 440.2R covers concrete only. FRP for masonry is ACI 440.7R, which NOTICE does not list.
11. **"A calculation that cannot match a published example is wrong" overclaims.** See [README L19](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/README.md?plain=1#L19). Published examples have rounding and errata. The track file expects some recorded values to need correction, and k already needs a stated allowance.
12. **The 0.55 ffu limit is recorded as a general service limit.** See [track file L59](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L59). In ACI 440.2R-17 §10.2.9 it is the creep-rupture limit, applied to the sustained moment. The text also rounds 59.84 ksi up to 60. See #4 item 9.

### Repo

13. **Seed tier is claimed with checklist items unmet.** See [docs/status.md L3](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/docs/status.md?plain=1#L3). REPO-STANDARD §A requires og.jpg and links to the open tracks; neither is there. §C requires secret scanning, push protection and Dependabot security updates; all were reported disabled at review time. None of this is listed as debt. Re-check the settings, since I could not read them directly.
14. **The licence split is ambiguous.** See [LICENSE L1](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/LICENSE#L1).
   - MIT's "associated documentation files" overlaps the CC BY 4.0 grant for text.
   - Data files (`input.json`, `expected.json`) and figures fall under neither licence.
   - CC BY 4.0 is given without its URI or the name to credit.
   - The preamble makes GitHub detect the licence as "Other" (NOASSERTION).

## What should change

Proposed corrections. Items 1, 2 and 14 need a maintainer decision.

- **1:** Add a CODEOWNERS entry, or a CI rule, so that `tracks/track-*/`, `tests/` and the track files need the same separate review as `src/`.
- **2 and 3:** Define "result". Allow a checker PR to carry its own match tests, labelled as checker acceptance rather than a result. Add a "no checker yet" branch to the agent prompt.
- **4:** Restrict PROVEN to written proofs.
- **5 to 7:** Add page citations or drop the claim. Add the missing standards and the example's URL or document number to NOTICE.
- **8:** Move ebi, ffu and efu under "derived". Either compute ebi in the checker, or say plainly that it is taken from the example.
- **9 to 12:** Correct the wording as listed.
- **13:** List the unmet Seed items as debt, or enable the settings.
- **14:** Use a plain MIT `LICENSE` file for code, and a separate statement naming which paths are CC BY 4.0, with its URI and the attribution name.

Implementation pull request: [PR #17](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/17).
