title: Research review: Track 1 checker (merged PR #2): missing service concrete check, yield assumption, test gaps

labels.name: review
labels.description: Research review: an error, a gap, a failed replay, missing prior art, or a wrong label

body:
## What kind

Error and gap. This is a retroactive review of [PR #2](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/2), which merged without review.

## Where

`src/flexure440.py`, `tests/test_track1.py` and `Makefile`, as merged (`04012d4`, unchanged on main). The checker hash locked in the track file is `77583629…`. Line links below point at `04012d4`.

## Evidence

Each item was either reproduced by running the checker on modified copies of `tracks/track-1/input.json`, or computed from its own output. Items marked **confirm** rest on code text that has to be checked against the publisher copy.

### Affects results

1. **The ACI 440.2R service concrete stress limit is not checked, and the Track 1 beam fails it.** See [L198](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L198). §10.2.8 limits both steel stress (fs,s ≤ 0.80 fy, which is checked) and concrete compressive stress (fc,s, which is not).
   - From the checker's own cracked section (d = 24 in, kd = 8.899 in, fs,s = 46.13 ksi, Ec = 3,605 ksi): fc,s = Ec·(fs,s/Es)·kd/(d − kd) = **3.38 ksi**.
   - The limit is 0.45 f'c = 1.8 ksi (the 440.2R-08 value) or 0.60 f'c = 2.4 ksi. Either way the beam fails, while every check prints PASS and `make verify` exits 0. **Confirm** the factor in the -17 text.
2. **`existing_strength()` assumes the steel yields.** See [L111](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L111): `a = As·fy/(0.85 f'c b)`, with no check that es ≥ εy.
   - As = 12 in²: Mn = 986 k-ft at es ≈ 0.001 < εy = 0.00207. Strain compatibility gives about 896 k-ft, so the result is 10% high, and the strengthening-limit check uses that overstated value.
   - As = 40 in²: a = 50 in > h and Mn = −242 k-ft, with no error raised.
3. **The parabolic stress block is used even when concrete crushing controls.** See [L72](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L72). §10.2.10 points to the Whitney block (α1 = 0.85, β1 per ACI 318) for the crushing case.
   - At f'c = 4 ksi, α1β1 is 0.747 against 0.7225, so φMn is about 3% high.
   - At f'c = 6 ksi, it is 0.737 against 0.6375, so φMn is about 12% high and φ = 0.90 instead of 0.835.
   - The example beam is debonding-controlled, so its numbers are unaffected. **Confirm** the §10.2.10 wording.
4. **The bisection never checks that a root was bracketed.** See [L93](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L93). With no sign change over [lo, hi], it returns an endpoint carrying a large force imbalance, and `run()` reports Mn from it. One case: f'c = 3 ksi, Ec = 6,000 ksi, As = 8 in² ends at c = 0.95h with a −611 kip imbalance and φMn = −95 k-ft. That Ec is unrealistic, but a root above 0.95h, or df < h, fails the same silent way. An assertion that the final balance is near zero would catch it.
5. **FRP stress is not clamped at zero.** See [L71](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L71). When ECU·(df − c)/c < ebi, the FRP is counted as a compressive force. ACI 440.2R does not count FRP in compression. With As = 40 in², ffe = −1.9 ksi. With ebi = 0.003, this starts once c > 13.5 in. Steel stress at [L70](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L70) is capped only in tension.
6. **The strengthening-limit citation looks wrong.** The docstring at [L6-7](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L6-L7) cites ACI 562-16 §5.5.2, but [L165](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L165) computes 1.1D + 0.75L, which is the ACI 440.2R-17 Eq. (9.2) form.
   - ACI's own published material gives ACI 562's form as 1.2D + 0.5L + 0.2S (+Ak): [ACI webinar slides](https://concrete.org/portals/0/files/pdf/webinars/ws_2017_0417_Alkhrdaji_DSREARS.pdf).
   - 1.2D + 0.5L gives 320.3 k-ft, not the printed 330, so the example is computing Eq. 9.2 whatever section it cites. **Confirm** against the publisher copy and the 562-16 text.
7. **Mu leaves out 1.4D.** See [L166](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L166). With wLL_new = 0.1 k/ft, the checker uses Mu = 270.3 k-ft while 1.4D gives 300.8 k-ft, which is unconservative. It does not govern for the example's loads.
8. **Strength moments are hard-coded as simple-span w·L²/8.** See [L162-166](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L162-L166). The service moment, by contrast, is an input (`service_moment_kipft`). For a continuous or cantilever beam, the strength and service checks would describe different structures, and nothing records the support condition.
9. **The creep-rupture limit is fixed at 0.55 ffu and uses the full service moment.** See [L200](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L200). §10.2.9 sets the limit by fiber type (glass 0.20, aramid 0.30, carbon 0.55) and applies it to the sustained-plus-cyclic moment, not the full Ms. The track file ([L59](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/tracks/track-1-flexure-example.md?plain=1#L59)) records it as a general service limit and rounds 59.84 ksi up to 60.

### Tests

10. **No test exercises the strain-compatibility solver.** See [L41](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/tests/test_track1.py#L41). In debonding mode, ffe = Ef·efd for any c, and the other nine printed values come from separate functions. A sign error in the ebi term, a wrong ψf lever arm or a wrong stress block would therefore leave all ten tests green. The example prints the first-trial strains at c = 6 in (εc = 0.0018, εs = 0.0053); a test of `section_state(6.0, …)` against them closes the gap.
11. **`test_all_checks_pass` asserts unverified output.** See [L55](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/tests/test_track1.py#L55). It sits in the example-match class but asserts φMn ≥ Mu, which the example does not print, so it locks in unverified checker output as if it had been matched.
12. **`CrushingModeSanity` checks only the mode string and the force balance.** See [L67](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/tests/test_track1.py#L67). It cannot fail for a wrong stress block (item 3) or a wrong φ.

### Output and cleanup

13. **`:.2f` on every check line hides strains.** See [L211](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L211). The debonding line prints "0.00 vs limit 0.01". The JSON block shares stdout with the PASS/FAIL lines, so `> out.json` followed by `json.load` fails.
14. **`make verify` hides the reason for a failure.** [Makefile L3](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/Makefile#L3) sends checker stdout to `/dev/null`, so a failing check shows only as `Error 1`.
15. **The same values are computed in several places.** [L117](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/blob/04012d4/src/flexure440.py#L117) calls `phi_for` twice with the same arguments, and `run()` builds each limit and pass flag more than once. A later change to one copy can leave the JSON fields and the PASS/FAIL lines disagreeing.

The always-passing debonding check is already recorded as a checker obligation in the track file by PR #3, so it is not repeated here.

## What should change

The checker is hash-locked, so these changes go in **one checker PR, with no result in it**. After that, a separate result PR updates the lock and regenerates the Track 1 certificate.

Suggested order:
1. **Items 1 and 2.** Item 1 changes the outcome for the Track 1 beam itself. Item 2 gives wrong values on realistic inputs. Add a FAIL path and a test for each.
2. **Item 6.** Fix the citation once the publisher copy is read. NOTICE needs the matching entry.
3. **Items 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9.** Each needs a test that would have failed before the fix.
4. **Items 10 to 12** go in the same PR, so the new behaviour is covered.
5. **Items 13 to 15**: cleanup.

Until item 1 lands, the Track 1 result should state that concrete service stress is not checked.

Questions for a maintainer:
- Is the checker meant to stay specific to this one example's beam (simple span, CFRP only)? Or should items 7 to 9 become inputs?
- Which 440.2R-17 factor applies for item 1, 0.45 or 0.60 f'c?

Implementation pull request: [PR #7](https://github.com/Foundation-0/cfrp-strengthening/pull/7).

title: Send the consolidated Figure 3D source-clarification request to the authors
body:
**Status (2026-11-04):** sent as [WangLab #4](https://github.com/WangLab-MSSM/CPTAC_Ovarian_Chemo_Response/issues/4); this issue stays open until answers arrive.

On 2026-10-24 the owner authorized putting the code-audit questions to the authors of Chowdhury et al. (Cell, 2023). The consolidated request is on main (draft only; the owner alone decides whether and when to send it) in `templates/pilot-001-source-request.md` ([view the file](https://github.com/Foundation-0/project-asma/blob/main/templates/pilot-001-source-request.md)). It merges the draft held since 2026-10-23 (#2, #3) with the questions from the [code-audit addendum](https://github.com/Foundation-0/project-asma/blob/main/docs/pilot-001-code-audit-addendum.md).

**Why the owner sends it.** GitHub rejected automated posting earlier ("Resource not accessible by integration"), and a 2026-10-24 access check from an automated session was also refused. Under the updated `AGENTS.md`, automated sessions must not post, retry posting or email the request.

**Checklist**

- [ ] Owner reviews the full text. Items 3 and 5, and the original parts of items 1–2, were held on 2026-10-23. The 2026-10-24 authorization named the code-audit questions.
- [x] Sent by the owner from his own account on 2026-11-04 as a standalone issue, [WangLab-MSSM/CPTAC_Ovarian_Chemo_Response#4](https://github.com/WangLab-MSSM/CPTAC_Ovarian_Chemo_Response/issues/4), instead of a comment on their issue #1. ~~Originally planned: a comment on issue 1, or an email to the corresponding author.~~
- [ ] Fill the sending record in `docs/pilot-001-source-request-handoff.md`, then add a one-line pointer here.
- [ ] When answers arrive, record them as aggregate statements only. Update the addendum, the protocol and the reconstruction contract as needed. Never post patient-level files, linkage rows or identifiers here.

**What the request asks**, in brief:
1. Where the RData workspaces and `balanced_folds.R` are, and on what reuse terms; how labels are coded; and how the candidate list was built.
2. Which code, objects and environment produced Figure 3D, and how the released scores were exported. It gives the 0.81 vs 0.83 context neutrally, with no cause attributed.
3. Frozen subgroup definitions, alignment samples, and which aligned frozen file (if any) fed `data_nov.RData`.
4. How the 98%-specificity sensitivity and the AUC interval were derived.
5. Which supplement carries the corrected legends.

**Out of scope.** Recruiting collaborators or external reviewers remains on hold. This issue covers only this request.

title: Fold each light curve at the GCVS period and flag lost eclipses

labels.name: task
labels.description: One piece of work, with what done means and how it is checked

body:
### What to do

For each star with TESS data, fold its light curve at the GCVS period: cut it into one-orbit pieces and stack them, so every eclipse lands in the same place. Measure the eclipse depth. Flag stars whose depth is below 20% of the GCVS amplitude.

### Done when

- A table for every star with TESS data: sectors, folded depth, GCVS amplitude, their ratio, and the flag.
- A plot of the folded light curve for every flagged star.
- The code that makes them.

### How the result is checked

Every flag lists its TESS sectors, the folded depth and the GCVS amplitude, and can be regenerated from the committed code.

### Context

Risks named in the scouting report (not yet re-checked):

- Wrong identifications in the GCVS.
- Ellipsoidal or RS CVn variables catalogued as eclipsing. Their light changes because the stars are stretched or spotted, not because of eclipses.
- Blended TESS pixels, where a neighbouring star's light dilutes an eclipse or adds a false one.

title: Contribution rules: reword the checker-PR rule to match practice, record the #11 re-pin of the locked checker, and create the research-review label
body:
The contribution rules say that a pull request that edits a checker is never merged together with a result (`CONTRIBUTING.md:5`, `.github/pull_request_template.md:7`, `docs/reproducibility.md:59`). Merged PRs have not followed this, and the rule is ambiguous. A new result has to ship with its own new checker (#1, #2, #33). #11 (`aea9dd6`) edited and re-pinned the hash-locked fold checker `autoresearch-fold/verify.py`, and the same merge regenerated a certificate, corrected a README number and edited site pages. #11 disclosed the checker edit in its PR description and its commit message. No file in the repository records it, though: the docs still describe the pinned file as the checker that judged the original search, and `autoresearch-fold/program.md:10` says "NEVER edit it". The edit changed no verdict, so no claim is affected.

Separately, the research-review issue template applies a label, `research-review`, that does not exist, so review issues arrive with no label.

Both need a maintainer. The rule's wording is a policy choice, and labels are created in the repository settings.

## Evidence

### 1. The rule as written

- `CONTRIBUTING.md:5`: "Pull requests that edit a checker are reviewed separately and never merged together with a result."
- `.github/pull_request_template.md:7`: "Does it edit a checker (`verify.py`, `chk_independent.py`, `autoresearch-fold/verify.py`)? Checker edits are reviewed on their own and are not merged together with a result." The same template lists "new check" as a PR type (`:6`), and a new check always edits a checker.
- `docs/reproducibility.md:58-59`: "`autoresearch-fold/verify.py` is the locked checker. Its sha256 is in `autoresearch-fold/verify.sha256` and is checked by `verify-fold-tests`. Do not edit it; changes are reviewed separately from results."
- None of these says what "a result" is: a new result folder, a regenerated certificate or a changed claim. None says whether a new result's own new checker counts as editing a checker.

### 2. What merged PRs did

| PR | Commit | Checker files changed | Also in the same merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | `603e654` | new `results/fold-end-exact/verify.py` | new result (PROOF.md, certificate) |
| #2 | `627ec4b` | new `results/fold-m1/verify.py` | new result |
| #33 | `abeb94b` | new `results/fold-continuous-fcc/verify.py` and `independent.py` | new result, `docs/audit.md` and `docs/status.md` rows, README |
| #11 | `aea9dd6` | `autoresearch-fold/verify.py` (locked, re-pinned), `results/fold-close-packing/verify.py` (+20 lines: pin check, one more control, one more certificate field), `results/fold-close-packing/make_fcc_path.py` (+2 lines: precondition); docstring-only changes to `results/fold-2d/verify.py` and `results/rigidity-nd/verify.py` | regenerated `results/fold-close-packing/certificate.json`, `certificates/` and `commitment/`; `results/fold-3d-cubic/PROOF.md`; README beat-fcc window corrected from `0.4102 < gamma < 0.4159` to `0.41023 < gamma < 0.41591`; four site pages (`index.html`, `matter.html`, `motion.html`, `open.html`); fold notes; `docs/status.md`, `docs/reproducibility.md` |
| #19 | `5cf931e` | `results/fold-close-packing/chk_independent.py`, new `checkers.sha256` | certificate (only the `chk_independent.py` input hash changed), PROOF.md description of the checker, a new "Checked by" row in `docs/audit.md` |
| #20 | `0609523` | `results/radius-ratio/verify.py`, `radius_ratio.py` | regenerated certificate (new `h1_*` fields), PROOF.md replay description, a new VERIFIED row in `docs/audit.md` for the H1 mirror check |

#19 and #20 changed no claim's statement or label. They only regenerated certificates and described the new checks, which a rule of the form "a checker PR may regenerate certificates and describe the replay" would allow.

#11 is the case that shows the ambiguity. Its PR description answers the template's question with "Yes" ("The edited checkers are `autoresearch-fold/verify.py`, `results/fold-close-packing/verify.py`, and `results/fold-close-packing/make_fcc_path.py`") and gives "Result(s) touched: none". The same merge also regenerated a certificate and corrected a claim's stated numbers (the README window).

### 3. The #11 change to the locked checker is not recorded in the repository

```
$ git log --oneline -- autoresearch-fold/verify.py
aea9dd6 Audit hygiene: stale docs, site numbers, checker hardening (#11)
18dcb6e Incentre lattice: interactive site, research notes, and fold-density research track
$ git show aea9dd6 -- autoresearch-fold/verify.sha256
-5062e649aafe62ad2d08c8faf5255049865cf474c6d14840c24e3166d788f00b  verify.py
+05d2385dcd3ec5a4ec7fec5d23971c9df685c2ccedcea2edf43629ac813835cd  verify.py
$ git show aea9dd6 -- autoresearch-fold/verify.py | grep '^[-+] '
-            res["end_state_error"] = str(e)
+            # Fail closed: an end-state analysis that throws must not report a valid path.
+            fail("end-state analysis failed: %s" % e)
```

The change is recorded in the commit message ("Checkers: fail-closed end_state_report (sha256 pin updated)", "No result changed") and in the PR #11 description ("`verify.sha256` updated"). Inside the tree, the old hash appears nowhere, and the new hash appears only as the pin and as certificate inputs:

```
$ grep -rnI '5062e649' . --exclude-dir=.git
(no output)
$ grep -rnI '05d2385d' . --exclude-dir=.git | cut -d: -f1,2
./certificates/selected-results.json:109
./certificates/selected-results.json:160
./autoresearch-fold/verify.sha256:1
./results/fold-m1/certificate.json:3
./results/fold-close-packing/certificate.json:6
```

These places describe the locked checker as if it had not changed since the search:

- `docs/audit.md:86` and `:88`: "The checker itself | 16 unit tests including must-fail cases; hash lock".
- `docs/reproducibility.md:58-59`, quoted above.
- `docs/review-ledger.md:19`: the fold-close-packing (hcp) row, reviewed at `18dcb6e` when the pin was still `5062e649...`, says "Same verdict as the locked `verify.py`". `docs/review-ledger.md:3` asks for a row for every PR that changes a checker, and #11 has none. Those missing rows are tracked in #41.
- `autoresearch-fold/program.md:10`: "`verify.py` LOCKED trusted checker (sha256 in `verify.sha256`). NEVER edit it." The same instruction is at `:29` and in `autoresearch-fold/run.sh:6` ("it is locked; never edit it").
- `autoresearch-fold/best/verify.json` is the original checker's output. It was committed in `18dcb6e` and has not changed since.

### 4. The #11 edit changed no verdict

In `autoresearch-fold/verify.py`, `fail()` only appends to `reasons` (`:155-157`). `res["valid"] = len(reasons) == 0` is set at `:262`, before the end-state block (`:263-268`).

So #11 moved an end-state exception from the side field `end_state_error` into `reasons`, and `valid` stays true either way. Despite the comment at `:267` and the PR description ("Now it fails closed"), the checker does not yet fail closed.

To reproduce: load each version of the checker, replace `end_state_report` with a function that raises, and run `verify_arrays` on the one-state path `canonical_state(2)`:

```
5062e649 valid=True reasons=[] end_state_error=simulated end-state failure
05d2385d valid=True reasons=['end-state analysis failed: simulated end-state failure'] end_state_error=None
```

On the stored paths the end-state analysis does not throw. The end-state fields (`contact_pairs` 288, `final_density` 0.7404804897, ...) are in `results/fold-close-packing/certificate.json` both before and after #11, and at HEAD the locked checker reports `valid: true` for both the hcp and the fcc path. So no claim is affected.

The fail-closed fix itself, which needs a second re-pin, is in #50. At `db3b51d`, `make verify-fold-tests` passes (`1 checksums OK`, `Ran 16 tests ... OK`).

### 5. The template's label does not exist

```
$ sed -n 5p .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/research-review.md
labels: research-review
$ gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/labels --jq '.[].name' | paste -sd,
accessibility,bug,documentation,duplicate,enhancement,good first issue,help wanted,invalid,needs decision,question,wontfix
$ gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/labels/research-review
gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)
```

GitHub ignores a template label that does not exist. Issues opened from this template therefore have no label, and `README.md:125` and `docs/reproducibility.md:80` send reviewers to this template. No issue so far (#1 to #36) has been opened from it, so nothing needs relabelling.

## Options / proposed resolution

1. **Label (a maintainer action in the repository settings).** Create the label:
   `gh label create research-review --description 'External or internal research review of a result'`
   Alternatively, change `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/research-review.md:5` to one of the eleven existing labels, though none of them fits as well.

2. **Rule wording (needs a decision).** Pick one of these for `CONTRIBUTING.md:5`, `.github/pull_request_template.md:7` and `docs/reproducibility.md:59`:
   - **a. Match practice (proposed).** For example: "A pull request that edits an existing checker does only that: it may regenerate certificates and update the description of the replay in PROOF.md and docs/audit.md, but it must not change a claim or add a result, and it gets its own review-ledger row. A change to a hash-pinned file records the old and new hash. A new result ships with its own new checker." Under this wording #1, #2, #19, #20 and #33 comply. #11 would have been split, with the checker hardening apart from the README and site corrections.
   - **b. Keep the strict rule and define its terms.** "A result" means any change to a result folder's claim, label or certificate, and a new result's own new checker is exempt. #19 and #20 would then also have needed splitting, because they regenerated certificates.
   - **c. Option (a), plus a stricter rule for the search judge only.** `autoresearch-fold/verify.py` is edited only in a PR that changes nothing else apart from its pin, the certificates that hash it, and the ledger.

   Whichever option is chosen, also decide whether a new VERIFIED row for a new check of an existing claim (as in #20) counts as "changing a claim".

3. **Record the #11 change.** Add a note to `docs/audit.md:88` (row "The checker itself"), or put it in the #11 ledger row from #41. For example: "`autoresearch-fold/verify.py` was edited once after the search (PR #11, `aea9dd6`): an exception in the end-state analysis is now reported in `reasons` instead of a separate `end_state_error` field; this edit did not change `valid`. Pin `5062e649...` -> `05d2385d...`. The stored paths are accepted by the new checker; `best/verify.json` is the original checker's output." Do not describe this edit as "now fails closed", because Evidence 4 shows it does not.
   Add a matching one-line note to `autoresearch-fold/program.md:10` and `docs/reproducibility.md:58`: "NEVER edit it" is an instruction to search agents, and maintainers changed the file once, in #11. After #50 merges, record its re-pin the same way.

4. **Implementation.** Once the wording is agreed, do items 2 and 3 as one small docs PR (suggested branch `audit/contributing-checker-rule`). It changes no checker, certificate or claim.

## What this blocks or affects

- **Planned checker PRs.** Ten planned audit PRs edit checkers and regenerate certificates: #50, #43, #54, #55, #56, #57, #58, #52, #51 and #59. Whether they fit the rule as written depends on what "a result" means. The wording chosen here decides how they are reviewed and merged.
- **Edits to the same lines.** #50 re-pins the locked checker a second time and updates the test count in `docs/audit.md:88`. Write the record in item 3 after that PR merges, or coordinate with it, to avoid a conflict on that row. #41 adds the missing ledger rows (#11, #19 and #20 among them) and a ledger checkbox in the PR template. #75 edits `CONTRIBUTING.md:22`, `.github/pull_request_template.md:25` and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/research-review.md:20`, which are near the lines the docs PR in item 4 would change.
- **Outside contributors.** `CONTRIBUTING.md:5` and the research prompt (`CONTRIBUTING.md:34`, "Never edit verify.py.") are what they read first. At present these do not match what the repository does.
- **Review triage.** Until the label exists, review issues cannot be filtered or triaged by label.
- **Claims and certificates.** No claim, label or certificate changes.

## AI assistance

Prepared by Claude (Anthropic), via Claude Code, as part of an internal audit at db3b51d; findings were reproduced by independent verifier agents. No person has checked them yet.

title: Review ledger backlog: add rows for 13 merged PRs that changed results, checkers or claims, fix the #28 row, and require a row in the PR template

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
`docs/review-ledger.md:3` says to "Add a row for every pull request that changes a result, a checker or a claim". The ledger has PR rows only for #23, #25, #27, #28 and #30. Thirteen merged PRs that changed a result, a checker or a claim have no row. They include #11, the only edit to the hash-locked fold checker since the initial commit, and #1 and #2, whose results the v2 paper uses (`papers/source/main.tex:205`, `:291`). The existing fold-continuous-fcc row (line 21) does not name a reviewed commit, and it does not mention #33, the PR through which that result reached main. The PR template does not ask for a ledger row, so nothing enforces the rule. Each missing row needs a verdict and a reviewer. Before the rows are written, the "Reviewed commit" column also needs a convention, because a squash merge leaves the PR-branch commits out of main's history. Only the maintainer can make these decisions.

## Evidence

All of this is checked at `db3b51d`. The PR heads, merge targets, closing issues and PR comments come from the GitHub API (`list_pull_requests`, `pull_request_read`, `issue_read`).

### 1. The rule and the existing PR rows

```
$ sed -n 3p docs/review-ledger.md
One row per review of a result. Add a row for every pull request that changes a result, a checker or a claim, and for every external review.
$ grep -oE '^\| \[PR #[0-9]+\]' docs/review-ledger.md
| [PR #25]
| [PR #27]
| [PR #28]
| [PR #30]
| [PR #23]
```

The other eight rows are `(internal)` reviews of the working tree at `18dcb6e`, or of the build that added `results/`.

### 2. Merged PRs with no row

```
$ git log --format='%h %s' | grep -E '\(#(1|2|7|8|9|10|11|18|19|20|21|31|34)\)$'
38bbf45 Write v2 of the preprint and a specialist outreach draft (#34)
9d9bb0a Rereview hygiene: symmetry counts, stale numbers (#31)
627ec4b Fold at m = 1: close packing (hcp and fcc) in the smallest cell (#2)
0609523 radius-ratio: assert the premises and numbers the certificate records; check H1 numerically (#20)
5cf931e Hash-lock the second checker and the fcc path generator; derive image shifts from the lattice (#19)
4ea3693 fold-close-packing: qualify the 27 degrees of freedom as the Maxwell count (#21)
f4e6ef4 Align site evidence labels with PROOF.md (CaB6 packing, 2D fold uniqueness) (#18)
aea9dd6 Audit hygiene: stale docs, site numbers, checker hardening (#11)
```

The `verify.py` hunk replaces `res["end_state_error"] = str(e)` with `fail("end-state analysis failed: %s" % e)`, so the end-state analysis now fails closed. The squash message says "No result changed".

HEAD has 91 (`research/1-mechanics.md:59`, `motion.html:126`).
- The #1 and #8 comments were posted after those PRs had merged (17:29:52 and 17:21:12).

The closed issues (#3 to #6, #12 to #16, #26) are the findings or assessments that led to each PR. They are not reviews of the change that was merged.

**Disclosure lines for the Notes column:**
- #1 and #2: "What a person verified: nothing yet."
- #11 and #31: "Models and roles: Muse (...)" and "What a person verified: nothing yet."
- #34: "What a person verified: no independent human review is claimed." `HAND-PROOF.md:81` says: "Internal work only; no person has checked it yet."

### 3. The fold-continuous-fcc row (line 21)

The row reads: `| [PR #28](…/pull/28) | fold-continuous-fcc | explicit construction added after `f015da0` | confirmed (internal); outside review open | …`

- `git cat-file -t f015da0` prints `fatal: Not a valid object name f015da0`. The GitHub API gives #28 `base.ref = codex/complete-result-commitments` and `base.sha = f015da0f0f78eb19d5eac5a65e697882cd57aa07`. So `f015da0` is the commit #28 was based on (the head of the #25 branch at that time), not a commit that was reviewed.
- The commits on #28 are:
  - `53e9de8`: "Prove a continuous density-increasing cab-to-fcc motion". `fold-continuous.js:1` calls it the "proof revision".
  - `2879c0b` and `548c468`: ledger-row edits.
  - merges of #30, #25 and #31 from main.
  - `56537f0`: "Merge main into continuous fcc motion; regenerate certificates and commitment".
- #28 was merged at 2026-10-13T08:42:04Z into `codex/complete-result-commitments`, not into main. #33 (same branch `codex/continuous-fcc-path`, same head `56537f0`) was merged into main at 08:51:41Z as `abeb94b`. The #33 body says: "It replaces PR #28, which was stacked on the #25 branch and so merged into that branch instead of main. The content is unchanged apart from merging main and regenerating `certificates/` and `commitment/`." The row mentions neither #33 nor `abeb94b`.

### 4. The "Reviewed commit" column in other rows

- Row 24 (#30) gives `90adcdd`. That is the first of the two commits on #30's branch; the head is `2fe8f42` "Record site research update review". `90adcdd` is not in main's history (the squash is `82f91c8`), and `git cat-file -t 90adcdd` fails.
- Rows 11, 13 and 25 (#25, #27, #23) give `2ed2ab7`. That is the main commit (#22) these branches started from, and it does not contain the files that were reviewed: `git ls-tree 2ed2ab7 results/cab6-packing/` has no `ATTAINMENT.md`, and `results/rigidity-nd/` has no `LITERATURE.md`. The PR heads are `8252530` (#23), `d41f4a0` (#25) and `90629ab` (#27).
- This follows from "How to add a row", step 2 (`docs/review-ledger.md:33`): "Name the result folder and the commit you reviewed (`git rev-parse HEAD` at review time)". For a review of uncommitted changes, that command returns the base commit. After a squash merge, PR head commits survive only in GitHub's PR refs: `git branch -a` shows only `main` and `origin/main`.

### 5. Nothing enforces the rule

```
$ grep -c ledger .github/pull_request_template.md
0
```

The Validation checklist (`.github/pull_request_template.md:13-17`) asks for `make verify`, finite checks, proofs, must-fail controls and status/audit updates, but not for a ledger row. `CONTRIBUTING.md` does not mention the ledger. `CONTRIBUTORS.md:56-57` says that a contributor's credit "will be recorded here and in `docs/review-ledger.md` for reviews."

### 6. Borderline PRs

#17 (`6ce4f6e`: README evidence-map diagram with labels, and result charts) and #35 (`37a2ae7`: Zenodo title and abstract for v2) also present claims, in the same sense as the site-only #9 and #18. #22 (`.gitignore`) and #36 (DOI) change no claim.

## Options / proposed resolution

The maintainer needs to decide:

1. **Scope.** Either (a) the 13 PRs in section 2, or (b) those 13 plus #17 and #35. Either way, line 3 should say whether README, site and archive-metadata wording counts as "a claim".
2. **Reviewed-commit convention.**
   - (a) Proposed: give the PR head that was reviewed and the squash commit on main, for example "`877f494` (PR head); main `603e654`". Reword step 2 of "How to add a row" to match, for example: "the PR head commit you reviewed, as shown on the pull request; for a review of uncommitted changes write 'working tree on <base>'". Apply the same form to rows 11, 13, 24 and 25.
   - (b) Give only the squash commit on main. It is always fetchable, but it is not what was reviewed.
   - (c) Apply the convention to new rows only.
3. **Verdict and reviewer for each row.** Proposed defaults:
   - #11, #18, #19, #20, #21, #31, #34: `open`, "no review recorded".
   - #1, #2, #7, #10: the PR comment is an internal AI review. The maintainer decides whether it supports `confirmed (internal)`, and says who or what wrote it (the comments say only "agentic team with human oversight").
   - #8: `open`, or `confirmed (internal)` if the maintainer agrees that the comment's tolerance points apply only to an earlier head.
   - #9: the maintainer decides the verdict, because the review's count correction (103/23/80) was disputed and not adopted (#31).
   - For every row, link the issue the PR closed in Notes ("fixes #N"), as the finding the PR answers rather than as the review.
4. **What specific rows say.**
   - #11: "Edited the locked checker `autoresearch-fold/verify.py` (end-state analysis now fails closed); pin `5062e649aafe62ad2d08c8faf5255049865cf474c6d14840c24e3166d788f00b` → `05d2385dcd3ec5a4ec7fec5d23971c9df685c2ccedcea2edf43629ac813835cd`; stored paths re-accepted (`make verify-fold-tests`, `make verify-fold-cp`, per the PR body)." The row should also list the other checker edits from the table.
   - #11 and #31: name Muse in the way #39 decides. The #31 row should also note that the PR body describes a 103/23/80 change which the merged diff does not contain.
   - #1 and #2: credit as #39 decides. Note that the PR bodies say no person has verified the work.
   - #34: "Internal AI work; no person has checked it (`HAND-PROOF.md:81`, PR #34 body)."
   - Row 21: replace "explicit construction added after `f015da0`" with the reviewed commit. The maintainer says which one: `53e9de8`, the construction, or `56537f0`, the head merged through #33. Then append: "Merged to main via PR #33 (squash `abeb94b`); #28 itself was merged into the `codex/complete-result-commitments` branch."
5. **Enforcement.** Add after `.github/pull_request_template.md:17`: `- [ ] \`docs/review-ledger.md\` row added (PR, result, reviewed commit, verdict)`.
6. **Implementation.** Once points 1 to 3 are decided, make one docs-only PR (suggested branch `audit/ledger-backlog`) that changes `docs/review-ledger.md` and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Neither file is referenced in `certificates/`, `commitment/`, `tools/`, the `Makefile` or `.github/workflows/` (grep finds nothing), so no checker, certificate or commitment changes. Each audit PR adds its own row.

## What this blocks or affects

- `README.md:115` directs readers to the ledger as "reviews so far". Today the ledger leaves out the only locked-checker edit (#11) and the two results behind `main.tex:205` and `:291` (#1, #2).
- **Depends on:**
  - #39: Muse for #11 and #31; the submitter of #1 and #2; what a person has checked.
  - #82: rewrites the ledger's PR and issue links from `aska-digital/incentre-lattice` to `Foundation-0/incentre-lattices`. New rows should use the new address.
- **Keep consistent with:**
  - #42: rewords `.github/pull_request_template.md:7` and records the #11 re-pin in `docs/audit.md`.
  - #50: re-pins the locked checker a second time and adds its own row with the old and new hashes. The #11 row records the earlier step.
  - #45: adds a row for its change to `HAND-PROOF.md`. The #34 row here covers the original addition.
  - #65: fixes `fold-continuous.js:1` with the same #28/#33 wording.
- **Expected merge conflicts in `docs/review-ledger.md`:**
  - #80: rows 13 and 25 (it leaves row 21 to this issue).
  - #44: row 14.
  - #63: row 19.
  - #68: line 27.
  - Most other audit PRs append a row.
- **Other edits to the PR template:** #48 edits line 13 and #75 edits line 25. The new checkbox goes after line 17.
- The `run.sh` timeout point in the #10 review comment is handled by #71.

title: Release notes and Zenodo records: record the v1.0.0 verify-rigidity failure, and correct the v2.0.0 notes and Zenodo text (elastic qualifiers, Borcea-Streinu wording, AI credit, licences)
body:
The public texts for the two releases no longer match the repository, and in one case they no longer match the archive itself.

- **v1.0.0:** the release advertises a replayable `make verify`. On some machines it fails at its first target, and nothing records this.
- **v2.0.0:** the release notes and the Zenodo v2 record drop the qualifiers of the elastic result. They also repeat the "same periodic graph" wording about Borcea and Streinu, which the tree is being corrected away from.
- **AI credit:** the release notes and the Zenodo record give two different AI-assistance statements for the same DOI.
- **Licences:** the v1 and v2 Zenodo records declare only CC BY 4.0. The archives also hold MIT code and IUCr-conditioned data.

A pull request cannot fix any of this. Only the maintainer can edit GitHub release notes and published Zenodo metadata, and archived files cannot change. Two more decisions are needed:

- edit the published Zenodo records now, or carry the corrections in the next version;
- keep the 25 IUCr-provided CIF files in future release archives, or drop them.

In-tree counterparts:
- #68: the licence sentence in `.zenodo.json`.
- #69: the AI credit in `.zenodo.json` and `NOTICE`.
- #47: the n >= 3 scope, the shear wording and the Borcea-Streinu wording.
- The paper's copies of the same wording are in #37.

## Evidence

**Tags.** `v1.0.0` points to 1e44cf0 and `v2.0.0` to 37a2ae7 (`gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/git/refs/tags`). `git diff --stat 37a2ae7 db3b51d` touches only `README.md` and `index.html`. So every in-tree line cited below is also the text of the v2.0.0 archive.

**Sources.** The release bodies were read with `gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/releases`. The live Zenodo records could not be fetched, because the audit machine is blocked from zenodo.org. The Zenodo texts below are the `.zenodo.json` files at the tags, which Zenodo's GitHub integration uses to build the records. Please check the live records before editing.

### 1. v1.0.0: `make verify` fails at `verify-rigidity`, and nothing says so

What the release promises:
- v1.0.0 release notes: "Verified results with replayable verifiers and certificates (make verify)".
- Zenodo v1 description (`git show 1e44cf0:.zenodo.json`): "The archive contains the preprint, the interactive site, replayable verifiers and certificates."
- `papers/source/main.tex:384` (the v2 paper): "`make verify` replays all of them. The results of v1 are archived in release v1.0.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23322080".

CI on the tagged commit (`gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/commits/1e44cf0b6ee5ff75d79de219b621fb4e3640da0a/check-runs`):

| Job | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| make verify (Python 3.11), job 114904005263 | success |
| make verify (Python 3.12), job 114904004901 | failure |
| make verify (Python 3.13), job 114904005076 | failure |

Both failing job logs end with:

```
python3 results/rigidity-nd/verify.py
VERIFY FAILED: n=7, c=0.3000: elastic constants
make: *** [Makefile:39: verify-rigidity] Error 1
##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.
```

This is issue #6. It was fixed on main by #8 (merge commit 81aa067, after the tag). CI on 37a2ae7 (v2.0.0) passes on all three Python versions.

**Local replay.** I replayed the tagged tree in a scratch worktree. `requirements.txt` is identical at 1e44cf0 and HEAD. The setup was Python 3.13.16, numpy 2.3.5, scipy 1.16.3 and the scipy-openblas 0.3.30 bundled in the wheels, on an Intel Xeon:

```
$ git worktree add --detach <scratch> 1e44cf0 && cd <scratch>
$ OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python results/rigidity-nd/verify.py; echo $?
VERIFY FAILED: n=7, c=0.3000: elastic constants
1
```

- With 4 threads the result is the same.
- `make -k verify-fast` on the same tree: `verify-rigidity` fails. radius-ratio, cab6-packing, fold-2d and the 16 fold-checker tests pass. I did not run the slow targets locally.
- HEAD's `results/rigidity-nd/verify.py`, unchanged since v2.0.0, prints `rigidity-nd: OK (n = 2..8; 5 controls rejected)` on the same machine.

**The miss is not a tolerance problem.** This corrects the audit's earlier diagnosis. I printed the residuals of the archived `elastic()` on this machine. Only n = 7, c = 0.3 misses:

```
C11 err 6.504e-05  C12 err 9.157e-06  shear 4.807e-06  coupling 4.841e-06  nu100 err 2.358e-03
```

The numerical C11 is 0.022894 against the exact 9/392 = 0.022959. A relative tolerance would not absorb that. The second commit of #8 states the cause. At the tag, `results/rigidity-nd/rigidity_nd.py:159` reads `P = np.eye(len(bars)) - Bw @ np.linalg.pinv(Bw)`. With its default cutoff, `pinv` can keep one round-off singular value of the bar matrix, and that changes the projector. #8 replaced this with an SVD whose rank is read from a checked spectral gap, and it kept the 1e-12 tolerance.

Copying #8's `rigidity_nd.py` and `verify.py` into the v1 tree makes `verify-rigidity` pass. But the certificate then records a different hash for `rigidity_nd.py`, so that is not a clean replay of the archive either.

**Nothing records the failure.** `grep -rnI -i 'v1\.0\.0\|known issue\|81aa067' .` at HEAD finds only `main.tex:384`. `docs/reproducibility.md` has no note on v1, and neither the release notes nor the Zenodo v1 text mention it.

### 2. v2.0.0: the elastic result without its qualifiers

- v2.0.0 release notes: "Headline results: unit-spring elastic constants in every dimension (all shear moduli zero, C11/C12 = (n-1)^2, Poisson ratio 1/(n^2-n-1)); ..."
- Zenodo v2 description (`.zenodo.json:5`, the same at 37a2ae7): "we prove that with unit springs every shear modulus vanishes, C11/C12 = (n-1)^2 and the Poisson ratio is 1/(n^2-n-1), for every dimension n >= 3". This text has n >= 3 but not the cube axis.

The repository attaches both qualifiers:
- `papers/source/main.tex:40`: "the Poisson ratio for uniaxial stress along a cube axis is $\nus=1/(n^2-n-1)$, for every $n\ge3$".
- `results/rigidity-nd/PROOF.md:3`: "PROVEN for every n >= 3 (written proof below); VERIFIED (finite check) for n = 2, ..., 8."
- `results/rigidity-nd/PROOF.md:34-35`: "the Poisson ratio for uniaxial stress along a cube axis is **nu_100 = 1/(n^2 - n - 1)**".
- `README.md:50`: "unit-spring elastic constants in every dimension n >= 3 (all shear moduli zero, C11/C12 = (n-1)^2, nu_100 = 1/(n^2-n-1))".
- `docs/audit.md:36`: "PROVEN for all n >= 3".

Why the qualifiers matter:
- **n = 2.** "In every dimension" includes n = 2, where the formulas hold only formally. `PROOF.md:138-139`: "C11 = C12 = 1/4, all shear moduli vanish, only the bulk modulus is non-zero, and nu_100 = 1 formally".
- **Cube axis.** The certificate records `"C44": 0` (`results/rigidity-nd/certificate.json:5`). A uniaxial stress along any other direction has a shear component in cube axes, which the framework cannot carry. So only nu_100 is defined.
- **"All shear moduli zero"** (taken from `main.tex:40` and `:55`) is imprecise in standard cubic terms. C44 = 0, but the tetragonal shear modulus C' = (C11 - C12)/2 = 2((n-1)^2 - 1)/(n^2 2^n) is positive for n >= 3. From the formulas at `PROOF.md:34`: n = 2 gives 0, n = 3 gives 1/12, n = 4 gives 1/16, n = 5 gives 3/80 and n = 8 gives 3/512. `main.tex:139` states it precisely: "every component of $C$ involving a shear strain vanishes".

### 3. v2.0.0: "same periodic graph as Borcea and Streinu"

- v2.0.0 release notes: "Corrected novelty: the framework is the same periodic graph as Borcea and Streinu (2021), Section 7; the zero-mode and self-stress counts are lemmas following from existing machinery."
- Zenodo v2 description (`.zenodo.json:5`): "For the periodic framework of regular cross-polytopes joined by bars (the same periodic graph as Borcea and Streinu 2021, Section 7), ..."

This corrects the audit plan: neither public text says "our counts cover it". That half of the claim appears only in the tree (`results/rigidity-nd/LITERATURE.md:59`, `results/rigidity-nd/PROOF.md:169`), where #47 fixes it.

It is the same infinite framework, but not the same periodic graph:
- Borcea and Streinu use a periodicity lattice with two cross-polytope orbits (`LITERATURE.md:59`: "two orbits of regular cross-polytopes").
- The counts here are per cell of 2Z^n, with one cross-polytope per cell.

Per-cell counts depend on the lattice. I recomputed the counts of the same framework with index-2 lattices, using a scratch script built on `results/rigidity-nd/rigidity_nd.py` with c = 2 - sqrt2. Each entry is (dof, bars, zero modes, self-stresses) per cell of the coarser lattice:

| n | generic phase (either sublattice) | phase 0, checkerboard sublattice | phase 0, sublattice {2m : m_1 even} |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | (36, 30, 6, 0) | (36, 30, 9, 3) | (36, 30, 11, 5) |
| 4 | (64, 56, 12, 4) | (64, 56, 16, 8) | (64, 56, 19, 11) |
| 5 | (100, 90, 20, 10) | (100, 90, 25, 15) | (100, 90, 29, 19) |

The generic counts are twice the 2Z^n values n(n-1)/2 and n(n-3)/2. The phase-0 counts depend on which index-2 sublattice is used. An earlier revision of the file (`LITERATURE.md:59-60` at f6f7cc1, PR #27 branch) said exactly this: "orbit counts depend on the translation group. Exact correspondence and priority of the elastic formulas remain open."

### 4. v2.0.0: two different AI-assistance statements for one DOI

- v2.0.0 release notes: "Computation, proofs, checking and writing were carried out with AI assistance (Claude models from Anthropic; some contributions developed with OpenAI Codex) under the author's direction; see CONTRIBUTORS.md."
- Zenodo v2 notes (`.zenodo.json:22`, unchanged since v1): "... with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5.5 and other Claude models from Anthropic) under the author's direction; see CONTRIBUTORS.md."
- `NOTICE:5` also names only Claude models.

The repository's own credit is more specific:
- `CONTRIBUTORS.md:29-31`: "GPT-6 (Codex) derived the curve, written proof and first exact arithmetic implementation. GPT-6.1 Sol independently checked the analytic reductions and supplied a separate polynomial-convolution replay. GPT-6 Luna handled repository publishing."
- `CONTRIBUTORS.md:23`: "OpenAI Codex (GPT-6) prepared the exact CaB6 attainment proof in `results/cab6-packing/ATTAINMENT.md`; GPT-6 Luna handled its repository submission."
- `papers/source/main.tex:381`: "GPT-6 (Codex) derived the explicit curve of Section~\ref{sec:motion}, its first written proof and the first exact certificate, and prepared the all-pairs attainment proof for Theorem~\ref{thm:cab6}; GPT-6.1 Sol independently checked the analytic reductions and supplied a second exact implementation".
- `results/rigidity-nd/LITERATURE.md:4`: "internal literature audit assisted by GPT-6.1 Sol".
- The body of PR #25: "GPT-6.1 Sol implemented the registry, guards, and tests; GPT-6 reviewed the change; GPT-6 Luna handled repository submission."

By these records, GPT-6 produced two of the v2.0.0 headline results: the exact motion in the first bullet (its curve, first proof and first certificate) and the attainment proof in the third bullet. The release sentence names neither GPT-6.1 Sol nor GPT-6 Luna, and the Zenodo notes name no OpenAI model. Credit for "Muse" and for the second human contributor is undecided; that is tracked in #39.

### 5. Licences declared on Zenodo

**What the records and the tree say:**
- `.zenodo.json:21`, and the same line in `git show 1e44cf0:.zenodo.json`: `"license": "cc-by-4.0"`. This is the only licence on the v1 and v2 records.
- `LICENSE:1-2`: "Code in this repository is released under the MIT License. Text, figures and site content are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)." `CITATION.cff:12-14` lists MIT and CC-BY-4.0.
- `NOTICE:7`: "Nothing below is relicensed by this repository's own licence."
- `NOTICE:13-16`: the 25 IUCr-provided COD files (the 2xxxxxx entries) "may be used within the scientific community so long as proper attribution is given ... These files must not be assumed to be CC0".
- `NOTICE:22-25`: `TableS1.csv` is under MIT (Bartel).

**What the archives contain:**
- Both archives contain all 45 CIFs. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 1e44cf0 research/chemistry/cod | grep -c '\.cif$'` gives 45, and `git archive 37a2ae7 | tar -t | grep -c 'research/chemistry/cod/.*\.cif$'` gives 45.
- The folder is identical at both tags and at HEAD.
- `grep -l 'IUCr Journals' research/chemistry/cod/*.cif | wc -l` gives 25, and these are exactly the files that match `2*.cif`.

**The export-ignore option, tested:**
- There is no `.gitattributes`.
- In a scratch worktree, I added a working-tree `.gitattributes` containing `research/chemistry/cod/2*.cif export-ignore` and ran `git archive --worktree-attributes HEAD`. The archive kept 20 CIFs.

**What depends on the files:**
- `make verify` does not read them.
- `research/chemistry/borides_real.py:15` reads `cod/<id>.cif` for every entry of `cod_index.json`.
- `research/chemistry/fetch_borides.py` re-queries the COD by formula, downloads missing files and rewrites `cod_index.json` (line 32). If the COD has changed, it may not reproduce the archived 45-entry selection.

## Options / proposed resolution

1. **v1.0.0 release notes**, and optionally the Zenodo v1 description: add the following known issue.

   > Known issue: on some machines `make verify` in this archive stops at its first target, `verify-rigidity`, with "VERIFY FAILED: n=7, c=0.3000: elastic constants" (issue #6; CI on this tag failed this way on Python 3.12 and 3.13). The numerical elastic relaxation in `results/rigidity-nd/rigidity_nd.py` uses `np.linalg.pinv` with its default cutoff, which can keep a round-off singular value; C11 at n = 7 then misses by about 7e-5. The proven exact values are not affected. Fixed in #8 (81aa067); replay the v1 results with v2.0.0 or main.

   This replaces the audit plan's draft, which blamed the absolute 1e-12 tolerance. Optionally, add one sentence to `docs/reproducibility.md` under "If a replay fails" (`:77-80`). Do this in a small PR coordinated with #73, which edits the same file.

2. **v2.0.0 elastic result.** Replace the headline bullet of the release notes with:

   > Headline results: unit-spring elastic constants for every n >= 3: C44 = 0 (every stiffness component involving a cube-axis shear strain vanishes), C11/C12 = (n-1)^2, and Poisson ratio nu_100 = 1/(n^2-n-1) for uniaxial stress along a cube axis; an exact continuous motion ...

   In the Zenodo v2 description, use: "... with unit springs C44 = 0 (every stiffness component involving a cube-axis shear strain vanishes), C11/C12 = (n-1)^2 and the Poisson ratio for uniaxial stress along a cube axis is 1/(n^2-n-1), for every dimension n >= 3".

   If you prefer to keep "every shear modulus vanishes" until the paper changes (`main.tex:40` and `:55`, in #37), add at least "along a cube axis" and "n >= 3".

3. **v2.0.0 Borcea-Streinu wording.** This matches the wording that #47 puts in the tree.
   - Release notes: "Corrected novelty: Borcea and Streinu (2021), Section 7, describe the same infinite framework at a different bar length, with a two-orbit periodicity lattice; our counts are per cell of 2Z^n. The zero-mode and self-stress counts are lemmas following from existing machinery."
   - Zenodo v2 description: "(the same infinite framework as Borcea and Streinu 2021, Section 7, at a different bar length; our counts are per cell of 2Z^n)".

4. **AI credit.** Use one sentence in both the v2.0.0 release notes and the Zenodo v2 notes, so the two statements for doi:10.5281/zenodo.23340326 agree. For example:

   > Computation, proofs, checking and writing were carried out with AI assistance under the author's direction: Claude Opus 5.5 and other Claude models (Anthropic) did most of the computation, proofs, code and writing; GPT-6 (Codex, OpenAI) derived the exact motion's curve, its first written proof and first exact certificate, and prepared the CaB6 attainment proof; GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI) checked the analytic reductions, supplied a second exact implementation, implemented the certificate registry and assisted the literature audit; GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI) handled repository publication. See CONTRIBUTORS.md.

   The shorter `.zenodo.json` "notes" wording in #69 also works, as long as the release notes use the same text. Add "Muse" and any human contributor once #39 is decided.

5. **Licences on the Zenodo v1 and v2 records.** Add the sentence that #68 appends to `.zenodo.json`: "Licences: code MIT; text, figures and site content CC BY 4.0; third-party data keep their own terms (see NOTICE), including 25 COD CIF files provided by IUCr Journals for scientific use with attribution." If the Zenodo editor allows more than one licence entry, also add MIT next to CC BY 4.0.

6. **Decide on the 25 IUCr CIFs in future release archives.** Choose one:
   - (a) Keep them, relying on the NOTICE wording and the files' own headers. Nothing changes.
   - (b) Add a `.gitattributes` with `research/chemistry/cod/2*.cif export-ignore`, so GitHub's source archives, and therefore Zenodo, omit them. Readers then need a way to restore the files: a fetch-by-ID mode that downloads the IDs listed in `cod_index.json` (the current `fetch_borides.py` re-queries by formula and rewrites the index), plus a line in `NOTICE:18-19` and in `research/chemistry`.
   - (c) Ask the IUCr and the COD whether redistribution in the archive is covered.

   A metadata edit does not change the published v1/v2 files. Only a future version would pick up option (b).

7. **Timing.**
   - GitHub release notes can be edited at any time.
   - For Zenodo, either edit the metadata of the published v1/v2 records now (no new DOI), or carry items 2-5 in the next version's `.zenodo.json` (see #37 for the v3 question).
   - A new version leaves the v1 record unchanged, so the v1 parts of items 1 and 5 can only be done as a metadata edit.

## What this blocks or affects

- Readers who follow `main.tex:384` to the v1.0.0 archive can hit the `verify-rigidity` failure, with no pointer to #8.
- After the in-tree PRs merge, the release notes and the published Zenodo records keep the old wording until someone edits them. The next release's `.zenodo.json` picks up those PRs; the published records do not.
- The v2 DOI carries two different AI-credit statements, and both credit less than `CONTRIBUTORS.md` and the paper do.
- Option 6(b) adds a `.gitattributes`, changes `NOTICE:18-19` and may need a change to the fetch script. Options 1 to 5 change no file in the tree, apart from the optional `docs/reproducibility.md` sentence.
- No checker, certificate or result is touched.

## AI assistance

Prepared by Claude (Anthropic), via Claude Code, as part of an internal audit at db3b51d; findings were reproduced by independent verifier agents. No person has checked them yet.

title: Attribution: decide how to credit 'Muse' (PRs #11, #31) and `abu-aska` (PRs #1, #2), and whether the author has checked the proofs

labels.name: question
labels.description: Further information is requested

body:
The public PR and issue record names two contributors that the repository does not credit anywhere. Separately, the v2 paper makes a statement about human checking that the per-result credit lines contradict. Only the maintainer (`ahrazzle`) can settle three facts: what 'Muse' is, how (or whether) `abu-aska` should be credited, and which proofs, if any, the author has checked. Each answer decides the text in `CONTRIBUTORS.md`, `docs/review-ledger.md`, `NOTICE`, the per-result credit lines and the next paper version. So the follow-up edits have to wait for these answers, and they cannot be fixed by a PR alone.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at `db3b51d`. GitHub data was read with `gh api` (read-only). Names and emails in the git output below are replaced by the GitHub login.

### 1. 'Muse' is named in the PR and issue record but nowhere in the tree

- PR #11 (squash `aea9dd6`, "Audit hygiene: stale docs, site numbers, checker hardening"). Its body says `- Models and roles: Muse (full audit: code read, verification runs, edits, writing).` and `- What a person verified: nothing yet.`
- PR #31 (squash `9d9bb0a`, "Rereview hygiene: symmetry counts, stale numbers"). Its body says `- Models and roles: Muse (rereview: code read, verification, edits, writing).`
- Issues #12, #13, #14, #15 and #16 each say `Audit by Muse; no person has verified this report.`, and issue #32 says `Rereview by Muse; no person has verified this report.` All six were closed as completed. PR #18 fixed #12 and #13, PR #19 fixed #14, PR #20 fixed #15 and PR #21 fixed #16.
- PR #11 is the PR that edited the hash-locked checker `autoresearch-fold/verify.py`: `end_state_report` now fails closed. It also re-pinned `autoresearch-fold/verify.sha256` from `5062e649aafe62ad2d08c8faf5255049865cf474c6d14840c24e3166d788f00b` to `05d2385dcd3ec5a4ec7fec5d23971c9df685c2ccedcea2edf43629ac813835cd`. Other files it changed:
  - `results/fold-close-packing/verify.py` (+20 lines: the half-way-blend must-fail control now also runs through the independent checker);
  - `results/fold-close-packing/make_fcc_path.py` (a sqrt precondition);
  - the docstrings of `results/fold-2d/verify.py` and `results/rigidity-nd/verify.py`.
- The tree's AI credit names only Claude Opus, Sonnet and Haiku, plus GPT-6, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (`CONTRIBUTORS.md:10-23`, `papers/source/main.tex:381`). `NOTICE:5` names only "Claude models by Anthropic, PBC".
- The squash commits `aea9dd6` and `9d9bb0a` name Claude Opus 5.5 as the only co-author. On the PR branches, the first commit of each PR has no `Co-authored-by` trailer: `3495907` (#11, which contains the locked-checker edit and the re-pin) and `01fa059` (#31). The later branch commits all carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`: `e8a146b` and `e9c4e95` (#11), and `253b88a`, `2160fc4` and `9a1e7a7` (#31).
- `docs/review-ledger.md:3` says "Add a row for every pull request that changes a result, a checker or a claim". The ledger has PR rows only for #23, #25, #27, #28 and #30, and none for #11 or #31.

So the tree does not say whether Muse is a name for an agent running on Claude or a different system. As a result, the tree's AI disclosure cannot be matched to the PR's own disclosure for the only change to the locked checker.

```console
$ git grep -nIiw muse; echo "exit $?"
exit 1
$ git show -s --format='%h %an | %(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly)' aea9dd6 9d9bb0a
aea9dd6 ahrazzle | Claude Opus 5.5
9d9bb0a ahrazzle | Claude Opus 5.5
$ git show aea9dd6 -- autoresearch-fold/verify.sha256
-5062e649aafe62ad2d08c8faf5255049865cf474c6d14840c24e3166d788f00b  verify.py
+05d2385dcd3ec5a4ec7fec5d23971c9df685c2ccedcea2edf43629ac813835cd  verify.py
$ gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/pulls/11 --jq .body | grep 'Models and roles'
- Models and roles: Muse (full audit: code read, verification runs, edits, writing).
$ gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/pulls/31 --jq .body | grep 'Models and roles'
- Models and roles: Muse (rereview: code read, verification, edits, writing).
```

### 2. The second human contributor, `abu-aska`, is credited nowhere

- `abu-aska` (author association MEMBER) opened two PRs, both merged by `ahrazzle`:
  - PR #1, which added `results/fold-end-exact` (squash `603e654`);
  - PR #2, which added `results/fold-m1` (squash `627ec4b`).
- `abu-aska` also opened issues #3, #4, #5 and #6, fixed by PRs #10, #9, #7 and #8. Issue #5 supplied prior-art sources, and PR #7 (`0360ce3`) added them. Four of those sources are cited in the v2 paper (`papers/source/refs.bib`): Johnsson and Lemmens, Shan et al., Li, Refson and Dove, and Travesset 2017.
- The squash commits of #1 and #2, and the README commit `523e6a4`, have the git author of GitHub login `abu-aska`. The #1 and #2 squash commits also carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer for the same person. The contributors API returns `ahrazzle 32`, `abu-aska 3`.
- The v2 paper builds on both results:
  - `main.tex:205`: "The integer matrix $L(1)$ is the exact fcc end state of a numerical path in the one-cell framework".
  - `main.tex:289-291`: the one-cell paths, and "The end states of these paths have exact integer closed forms".
  - `results/fold-continuous-fcc/PROOF.md:116` also says "The endpoint matrix is the fcc matrix already recorded in [fold-m1]".
- No file in the tree contains the login or the name. `CONTRIBUTORS.md:56-57` says a contributor's "credit will be recorded here and in `docs/review-ledger.md` for reviews". `docs/review-ledger.md:3` requires a row for every PR that changes a result. Neither file has an entry for #1 or #2.
- Some context suggests the omission may be intended:
  - Both PR bodies credit the work to Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code) and say "What a person verified: nothing yet."
  - Issues #3-#6 each end with a Claude Code attribution footer.
  - `523e6a4`, authored by `abu-aska`, changed the README credit from "Ahraz Arifuddin, Aska Digital, and contributors." to handles for `ahrazzle`, `aska-digital` and `claude`. That line is now `README.md:129`; `0df3441` and `df14ba2` later added the links.
  - `NOTICE:2` still says "Ahraz Arifuddin, Aska Digital, and contributors."
  - `CITATION.cff:5-8` and `.zenodo.json:6-10` list only Ahraz Arifuddin.

```console
$ git grep -nIiE '<login or name of the contributor>'; echo "exit $?"
exit 1
$ git log --no-walk --format='%h %an | %s | %(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly,separator=; )' 603e654 627ec4b 523e6a4
627ec4b <abu-aska> | Fold at m = 1: close packing (hcp and fcc) in the smallest cell (#2) | <abu-aska>; <Claude co-author trailer>; Ahraz Arifuddin
603e654 <abu-aska> | Add exact closed forms of the hcp and fcc fold end states (m = 2) (#1) | <abu-aska>; <Claude co-author trailer>; ahrazzle
523e6a4 <abu-aska> | Update README.md |
$ for n in 1 2; do gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/pulls/$n --jq '[.number,.user.login,.author_association,.merged_by.login]|@json'; done
[1,"abu-aska","MEMBER","ahrazzle"]
[2,"abu-aska","MEMBER","ahrazzle"]
$ for n in 3 4 5 6; do gh api repos/Foundation-0/incentre-lattices/issues/$n --jq .user.login; done
abu-aska
abu-aska
abu-aska
abu-aska
$ grep -n 'PR #1\b\|PR #2\b' docs/review-ledger.md; echo "exit $?"
exit 1
```

### 3. The paper says the author checked the proofs; the proofs' credit lines say no person has

- `papers/source/main.tex:381` (Acknowledgments, AI-assistance paragraph) says: "All reviews so far were performed by AI models under direction; no person other than the author has checked the proofs. Responsibility for the content rests with the author." The v2 PDF (`papers/incentre-lattice.pdf`, pp. 13-14) prints the same sentence. The v1 PDF has no such sentence; it was added in `38bbf45` (#34, v2).
- Readers will naturally take this to mean the author checked the proofs. But the credit lines of the proofs the paper relies on say that no person has checked them:
  - `results/fold-continuous-fcc/HAND-PROOF.md:81` (the symmetry-reduced written proof of Theorem 2(b), non-overlap): "Internal work only; no person has checked it yet."
  - `results/fold-end-exact/PROOF.md:78-79` (the exact end states of Section 6): "... wrote `exact_end.py`, `verify.py` and this note; no person has checked them yet."
  - `results/fold-m1/PROOF.md:88` (the one-cell paths and $L(1)$): "No person has checked them yet."
  - The PR #1 and PR #2 bodies: "What a person verified: nothing yet."
- Either the paper claims more human checking than the record shows, or those credit lines are out of date.
- The following statements fit either reading:
  - `main.tex:376`: "none has had independent human review".
  - `results/cab6-packing/ATTAINMENT.md:106`: "no independent human review is claimed".
  - `results/fold-continuous-fcc/PROOF.md:164`: "No independent human review is claimed."
  - `CONTRIBUTORS.md:26`: "a person has not independently re-derived every proof".
  - The PR #34 body: "What a person verified: no independent human review is claimed."

```console
$ sed -n 381p papers/source/main.tex | grep -o 'All reviews so far.*the author\.'
All reviews so far were performed by AI models under direction; no person other than the author has checked the proofs. Responsibility for the content rests with the author.
$ grep -rn -i 'no person' results/*/*.md
results/fold-continuous-fcc/HAND-PROOF.md:81:checked by GPT-6.1 Sol). Internal work only; no person has checked it yet.
results/fold-end-exact/PROOF.md:79:note; no person has checked them yet.
results/fold-m1/PROOF.md:88:steering stage and this note were made with Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code) in a copy of `autoresearch-fold/`. No person has checked them yet.
$ pdftotext papers/incentre-lattice-v1.pdf - | grep -c 'other than the author'
0
$ git log --format='%h %an | %s' -S'no person other than the author' -- papers/source/main.tex
38bbf45 ahrazzle | Write v2 of the preprint and a specialist outreach draft (#34)
```

## Options / proposed resolution

1. **What is Muse?** Please state what system produced the work in #11, #12-#16, #31 and #32.
   1. If Muse is a name for an agent running on Claude, add to `CONTRIBUTORS.md`: "Muse, an agent running on Claude (Anthropic; name the model as in the existing CONTRIBUTORS.md entries), did the audits in issues #12-#16 and #32, the checker hardening in PR #11 and the rereview in PR #31." `NOTICE` and the paper then need no change for Muse.
   2. If Muse is a different system:
      - add a separate `CONTRIBUTORS.md` line naming the system, its provider and these roles;
      - extend `NOTICE:5`, coordinating with #69, which already rewrites that line;
      - in the next paper version, extend the AI-assistance paragraph at `main.tex:381` (#37);
      - note in `CONTRIBUTORS.md` that the Claude co-author trailers on `aea9dd6` and `9d9bb0a` do not cover this work.
   3. Either way, the ledger rows for #11 and #31 name Muse as decided here (#41).
2. **How should PRs #1 and #2 and issues #3-#6 be credited?**
   1. If credit is intended: ask the contributor which name and login to use. Then add them to `CONTRIBUTORS.md` for submitting `results/fold-end-exact` (#1) and `results/fold-m1` (#2) and for filing issues #3-#6. Also decide whether the generic "and contributors" in `NOTICE:2` is enough, or whether `CITATION.cff` and `.zenodo.json` should list them too.
   2. If the omission is intended (they are covered by the Aska Digital credit), say so in `CONTRIBUTORS.md`, for example: "Pull requests #1 and #2 and issues #3-#6 were submitted by a member of Aska Digital; the work in them is credited to the AI models named in each result."
   3. Either way, add the rows for #1 and #2 that `docs/review-ledger.md:3` requires, and optionally 'external' rows for #3-#6 (#41).
3. **Has the author checked any of the proofs?**
   1. If not: in the next paper version, replace the clause with "no person has independently checked the proofs; responsibility for the content rests with the author." (#37). The credit lines stay as they are.
   2. If the author has checked some or all of them, say which proofs and when. Then:
      - replace the "no person has checked ... yet" sentences in `results/fold-continuous-fcc/HAND-PROOF.md:81`, `results/fold-end-exact/PROOF.md:79` and `results/fold-m1/PROOF.md:88` with, for example, "Read and checked by the author (Ahraz Arifuddin) on <date>; no independent human review.";
      - if it applies, add the same sentence to `results/cab6-packing/ATTAINMENT.md:106`, which today says "no independent human review is claimed". Coordinate with #80, which rewrites that line;
      - make the paper sentence name the proofs the author checked.

Once these are decided, the repository changes fit in one docs-only follow-up PR, which may be combined with #80 if that has not yet merged. The PR would cover `CONTRIBUTORS.md`, `NOTICE` and the credit lines above. It touches no checker and no hash-pinned file. The only hash-pinned document in these result folders is `results/fold-continuous-fcc/PROOF.md` (pinned at `results/fold-continuous-fcc/certificate.json:57` and `certificates/selected-results.json:194`), and none of the proposed edits touches it. The `main.tex` wording goes into the next paper version, because v2 is already published.

## What this blocks or affects

- #80: its new credit sections for `fold-3d-cubic` and `fold-close-packing` mention the PR #11 edits, and its Muse wording follows this decision. It also rewrites `ATTAINMENT.md:106`.
- #69: it rewrites `NOTICE:5` and `CONTRIBUTORS.md:10-11` to name the OpenAI models, and it leaves Muse and the human credit to this issue.
- #41: the missing rows for #1, #2, #11 and #31 need the contributor and model names settled here.
- #37: the rewrite of `main.tex:381` in the next version.
- #40: the v2.0.0 release-note AI credit omits both Muse and the second human contributor.
- #42: it proposes recording the #11 locked-checker re-pin in `docs/audit.md`, and that record should name the agent the same way as decided here.

## AI assistance

Prepared by Claude (Anthropic), via Claude Code, as part of an internal audit at db3b51d; findings were reproduced by independent verifier agents. No person has checked them yet.
